en: Preface to the *Recorded Sayings of the Sixth Assembly* of Chan Master Chu-shih Hui-pien, the Sun of the Buddha’s Radiance Shining Universally.
Dahui propagated the Way of Yuanwu at Mount Jing; his divine mechanisms and wondrous applications were vast and unimpeded.
Those who entered his gate had all worldly sentiments utterly extinguished. Among his Dharma heirs, there were more than ten individuals, each of whom expounded the source of his transformation.
Yet Fo-zhao was among them, whom he called Shanji (Good Successor). After Fo-zhao, Miaofeng succeeded him; after Miaofeng, Zangsou inherited him.
It was as if they were passing a left-hand promissory note from one to another; their capacity and character were so perfectly harmonious that there was not the slightest discrepancy.
Jizhao, following these four transmissions, was again able to emulate his predecessors; truly, this is what is meant by "succession through generations."

Its excellence is such that, although there are differences in how the various Buddhas realized and entered [enlightenment], in their supreme reception of the fundamental principle transmitted from the West—which enables people to leave behind defilements and manifest their essential brilliance—they are one and the same.

Chushi Chan Master, a disciple of Jizhao, possessed a precocious and enlightened disposition from an early age and applied himself with keen resolve to the Way. Among the renowned virtuous masters of his time were Heiji, [...]

Whether he encountered those like "the empty valley" or "beyond the clouds," they all sought to draw him out from beneath their seats; the Master declined them all, choosing instead to visit the chamber of Jizhao.
There, he questioned and investigated repeatedly until, upon hearing the sound of a drum, his myriad doubts melted away like ice.

He realized that the myriad things of the world, in all their profusion and variety, are all capable of assisting in the awakening of the mechanism of true permanence. From then on, he presided over six monastic centers, preaching the Dharma and delivering sentient beings.
Whether laughing, joking, scolding, or reviling, everything was nothing other than Buddha-work.

As for manifesting jeweled pavilions and various forms of adornment to guide those in the Dharma-ending age, causing them to attain awakening through the arising of signs—this never deviated from the realm of the single reality.

When the Śrāvakas arose, it was like water surging forth or mountains emerging; yet when his worldly conditions were about to end, his countenance did not differ from his usual state, and he passed away while sitting serenely.

It is like returning to one’s ancestral home; as for its magnificence and brilliance, how does it compare to those who rely on mere verbal dexterity while remaining ignorant of the mind? Alas! The Way of Great Wisdom (Mahāmati) is supreme.
Speaking in terms of both our own and other schools, there have certainly been many who upheld the True Dharma and roared like lions; however, in recent years...
The transmitters have lost the original truth; like surging waves following one another, what they pursue declines day by day.

Furthermore, those who hold the office of judicial authority have recklessly bestowed their seal of approval, causing "fish eyes" to be mixed with rare jewels. In the mere blink of an eye or a raised brow, they immediately declare, "That person has already attained enlightenment."
"How easy it is to awaken! people then ridiculed him, calling him "the gourd-seed seal. It did not stop there.
He transcribed the essential tenets of the five houses and memorized them thoroughly, saying, "This is Linji; this is Caodong, Fayan; this is Guiyang and Yunmen.
Without asking whether the lineage was transmitted or had been severed, he would set up "live mechanisms" (huojī) when questioned in such a manner. Thus it was.
He answered in this manner, producing more than ten or so turns of phrase, resolving matters through his mouth; this is what is called "transmitting a public case" (*kōan*).
Those who act thus are all rejected by the Master. Now, observing the Master’s words from the six assemblies:

they enter the minute without entering within, and enter the vast without entering without. Their functional application is earnest and true, leaving nothing to be ashamed before the former worthies. Only those who possess the adamantine eye can [perceive this].
It is because you know that there is substance in my words. I am old and infirm; beset by a multitude of those who demand texts, I have firmly resisted them.

That I alone took pleasure in composing this preface and did not set it aside was out of compassion for the harm caused by demonic teachings, and to manifest the authentic transmission so as to exhort the world.
The Master’s name was Fanqi, his courtesy name Chushi. For details regarding his conduct and deeds, they are fully recorded in his stupa inscription.
Among those who requested this preface for the inscription was the foremost disciple of the Dharma, Master Yingzhong Huán.
This preface is respectfully composed by the Layman Wuxiang, Song Lian of Jinhua.
Preface to the *Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chu-shih Hui-pien*, “The Sun of the Buddha Shining Universally.
Since the plucking of the flower at Vulture Peak and the demonstration of entering nirvana at Crane Forest, more than two thousand years have passed.
What is called the true mark being markless, this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate, has from the beginning neither increased nor decreased. Yet, as an ancient said: "To obtain it..."
The mind: it would turn the *eranda* tree into a sandalwood tree, yet one loses the essential point; it would turn nectar into a garden of thorns.
If one were to engage in such calculations of gain and loss, one cannot avoid being ridiculed by bystanders. Upon what do beginners and later students rely?
Bodhidharma observed that the land of Eastern Zhendan possessed the atmosphere of the Mahayana, and so he crossed the seas and deserts to arrive there.

In Jinling, he presented his realization to the Prince of Liang, but the Prince did not accord with him. He then broke a reed for a raft to cross the Yangtze River and took up residence at Shaolin, where he sat facing a wall for nine years.
Ultimately, he would not remain silent and return empty-handed; he required the certification of Shen Guang before he could attain it.
After five transmissions from Shen Guang, the lineage reached Caoxi, which split into two schools. One was the Nanyue line, from whom Mazu received the Dharma. Under Mazu came Linji...
Ji (Linji) succeeded to the Yangzong (Yangqi) school. One of his lineages was Qingyuan, who obtained Shicheng.
Below Shicheng, Yunmen, Caodong, and Fayen succeeded to his teachings; these constitute the Five Houses of Chan. Linji obtained Xinghua; Xinghua obtained Nanyuan;
Nanyuan obtained Fengxue; Fengxue obtained Shoushan; Shoushan obtained Fenyang; and Fenyang obtained Ciming.
Chiming. Chiming obtained Yangqi; Yangqi obtained Baiyun; Baiyun obtained Wuzu; Wuzu obtained Yuanwu.
At this point, the lineage again split into two schools: Miaoxi and Huqiu. Their descendants filled the land.
Miaoxi obtained Yuyang Fozhao; Fozhao obtained Lingyin Miaofeng; Miaofeng obtained Jingshan Zangyun; Zangyun obtained...
Jizhao Yuansou was preeminently a man of towering integrity who shook heaven and overturned earth; today’s Chan Master Chushi Tianning truly inherits his legacy.
Over the course of fifty years, he presided over six monasteries, and his verses and sayings have spread throughout the monastic community.
His recorded teachings comprise six volumes of discourse records (*huìlù*). He cast off the narrow confines of recent times and strictly maintained the dignified standards of the ancient masters.
Like lightning splitting the clouds and frost clearing the sky, his voice was as resonant as gold and jade. He is truly called the bone-descendant of the fifth-generation successor of Miaoxi.
Those who read this shall surely find for themselves a point of realization and entry. Written in the autumn of the *zhèngwǔ* year of the *zhìzhèng* era by the Layman Qiūjiāng, Qián Wéishàn.

Volume One of the *Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Huibian Furi Puzhao*:
Recorded Sayings from His Residence at Fuzhen Chan Monastery.
Compiled by the junior monks Zu Guang and others.
In the winter of the first year of the Taiding era, the Master was invited to enter the temple while residing in the Head Seat’s Quarters at Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple on Mount Jing.
The Mountain Gate: The entire earth is the gate of liberation. It is a mistake to treat this as a mere assembly for the Buddha-dharma; when the mud is deep, the Buddha is large;
when the water rises, the boat is high. The Buddha Hall:
The old woman east of the city does not wish to see it; the Bhikṣu Devadatta is constantly angry and resentful. Reaching out with his hand, he plucks one—
Incense is being offered. This too is winter practicing the ordinances of spring.
The Patriarchal Hall—these are all this very same group of men. Had the Buddha-dharma not reached the present day, it would not have been because of this very same group of men.
The Buddha-Dharma has not reached today. Tell me, do you accept this or not?
I take possession of the room. Within three feet of the corner of this rope bed is where all of you beg for your lives.
To let one matter pass by is already intolerable; you have immeasurable transgressions, and I too have immeasurable transgressions.
A proclamation from the Xuanzheng Yuan: atop a solitary peak, one has built a thatched hut; though one has a mouth, it is fit only to hang on the wall.
At the crossroads of the city, one unties the sack; only upon entering the water does one see the tall man. Why has it come to such a state?
The announcement for the ordination reads: "With hands that once mended the robes of the Emperor and prepared the sacrificial lamb, he now turns the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "Have you come for the sake of the Dharma, or for the sake of this seat? A soaring falcon capable of reaching the clouds should immediately seize the moment;

a weary fish stuck in a shallow pond merely exhausts itself by splashing the waves. Thereupon, he ascended the seat. Having offered incense to pray for the longevity of the Sovereign, he held up the incense and said: "This one portion of incense..."
This is offered on behalf of the Venerable Master Yuansou Duan, currently residing at Mount Jing, in order to repay the kindness of his dharma-milk. He adjusted his robes and took his seat.
The Elder Abbot of Tianning struck the gavel and said, "O assembly of dragons and elephants at this Dharma feast, you should contemplate the primary meaning.
The Master said, "That is already the secondary meaning; in another moment, it will be the tertiary meaning. Nevertheless, one who stands before the furnace does not avoid the heat."
"Sparks fly! New Elder, today your life rests in the hands of these people; they may drag you about as they please.
Under the promise of a heavy reward, there must surely be brave men—is there anyone? Is there anyone? A monk asked, "The heavens lower a jeweled canopy, and the earth wells up golden lotuses.
Within this single phrase of non-selfishness, how should one offer praise? The Master said, "I am always mindful of this. The monk pressed further, "Always?"
[The Master] took the sun and moon as his celestial eye and pointed to Mount Sumeru as his mountain of longevity. The Master said, "Once every three thousand years, the Yellow River clears.
The student asked, "I am originally without a mind that seeks anything; now this great treasure of the Dharma King has arrived spontaneously.
Furthermore, what is the great treasure of the Dharma King? The Master said, "Those with eyes see it; those with ears..."
[The monk] asked, "Is it not simply this? The Master said, "Shatter the skull; pull out the nostrils. [The monk] asked, "How is it to be used?
The Master said, "Just wait until the rain falls upon your head. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "Before leaving Tuṣita, he had already descended into the royal palace;
before emerging from his mother's womb, his work of saving beings was already complete. Thus have been the Buddhas of the three periods throughout the ages..."
The Patriarchs and the old monks of the world speak of mind and nature, citing the ancients and the present;
all of this is but windless ripples. Truly, they deserve twenty blows of the staff.

Today, at Xinfuqin, it is not that "exhausting the methods leaves no people," but because one did not meet a master from the very beginning, it has ultimately turned into mere antiquities. If people would truly understand, take them up!
Take off the hat of scorched fat; cast off the foul-smelling cotton shirt of the falconer. If you have not yet done so, there is much more to come tomorrow and the day after.
Again, he cites Linji’s address to the assembly: "Upon this ball of raw flesh, there is a true person of no rank."
"It is constantly entering and exiting the gates of the faces of all of you. Those who have not yet attained realization, look! Look!
At that time, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the true person of no station? Linji descended from his rope seat, seized him, and cried, "Speak! Speak! The monk hesitated.
Ji said, "The 'unranked true person'—what kind of dried dung-puck is that? He then returned to the abbot's quarters.
The Master said, "If Linji had not uttered those later words, he would have been caught breaking into Caizhou. Nevertheless, a house does not keep a plan for a white [madman]."
There can certainly be no such demons.
This is the small *sīmān* (evening) discourse for the eve of the New Year. How excellent! The board has been struck three times; all you kinsmen have come to attend.
Since you already well know the proper timing, I shall not repeat myself. O worthy ones, once spoken, it is not spoken again. Now that it has been spoken twice, once heard, it is not heard again.
No longer heard. Now it has been heard again. Clear in every head; realized in every object.
Such as the principle, such as the phenomenon; pervasive through all antiquity and the present. It is not the mind of nirvana, nor is it the Eye of the True Dharma.

In this way, in this way, the Buddhas of the three periods have only said that one must know for oneself. Not in this way, not in this way, the Six Patriarchs had no place to open their mouths. Even if...

Even if one were to attain realization through words, it would still be a lingering within the shell and a delusion of confinement. Even if one were thoroughly proficient in the meaning beneath a single phrase, one could not avoid encountering wild views wherever one goes.
Tonight, upon the red furnace, I shall pick up a single speck of snow; upon the withered tree, I shall sprinkle a few blossoms.
To you all, we attend to this season: the fading lamp follows the end of winter; the bursting firecrackers herald the arrival of spring. Again, Panshan said:
"The one path upward—thousand sages have not transmitted it. Ciming said: "The one path upward—thousand sages do not approve of it.
Miaoxi said: "The one path upward—the sound of a hot bowl. The Master said: "These three great elders have exerted their full strength."
The Way. One may only clarify the path leading downward; as for the upward path, when will you ever see it even in your dreams?
On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Today is the fifteenth day of the first month; the light of the moon and the lamps is in profusion.
There is not a single thing before one's eyes—beat the drum and let everyone come and look! He added: "It pierces the eye!"
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "One does not worry about thoughts arising; one only fears that awakening is slow. What is awakening? The Master said, "The horns of an ox;
the horns of a horse. The monk pressed further, "What is thought? The Master said, "Even 'four times five is twenty' you do not know. The monk bowed.
It is then said: "The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. To open one's mouth is an error; to stir a thought is to deviate.
When all the sages vie to emerge from their retreats, they cannot avoid mistaking a deer for a horse. At this point, what can possibly be said?
Can one point east and west? Can one pat one’s chest and ribs? Can one speak of fine weather or fine rain? Or can one wield the staff?
"Can you drink it? You are all merely playing with the vapors of rice gruel; you have not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma.
To disperse so abruptly for no reason is to betray those who came here to beat these two pieces of skin; you have deceived the assembly no small amount. Now, what will you do? Return to the hall."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Yantou said, 'One must have each and every thing flow forth from within one's own breast, so as to cover heaven and earth with it.
To speak in such a way is already to be buried deep in a pit dug by others. Vast is the universe, and countless are the people;
which man among them is a true hero? A man and a hero—how far apart are they? Wait until you emerge from the pit."
Come. I shall tell you: Upon returning from the imperial court, he ascended the hall.

After the prayer for the Emperor’s longevity had concluded, a monk stepped forward and asked: "Having traveled far to the Jade Capital at imperial decree, your fame has already spread throughout the capital.
Returning with heavenly incense filling your sleeves, it coincides exactly with the Yellow River becoming clear for once."

The student came forward and requested the Master to offer a benediction. The Master said, "Heaven covers all without partiality. The student stepped forward and said, "May the golden branches flourish forever throughout the ten thousand realms;
may the jade leaves endure for tens of thousands upon tens of thousands of springs. The Master said, "I shall have you, Dharma brother, bear witness to this. The student stepped forward and said:

In the past, when a monk came for an audience with Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, the Emperor questioned him, saying, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Woyun Hermitage on Mount Lu.
The Emperor said, "I have heard that where the clouds rest deeply, one does not face the court. For what reason have you come here?"
At that time, there was no one to respond. [The Master asked: "How about then? The Master said, "Is this monk not a master himself?

He further asked, "Later, Xuedou spoke on his behalf, saying, 'It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation. Does this accord with the Great Emperor or not? The Master said, "Truly it is thousands of miles away.
Then he said, "The wind does not whistle through the branches; the rain does not break up clods of earth. The people do not lose their dwellings; the roads have nothing to be picked up."
[The Master] passed away. At such a time as this, what a season of great peace! This mountain monk has recently received a mission and traveled far to the Imperial Capital.
There, he faced the Dragon’s countenance and personally heard the imperial edict. What a celebratory meeting of wind and clouds—once in a thousand years!

Now that I have returned to the mountain, with what shall I repay [the Emperor]? It does not go beyond this very moment. From the appearance of the Buddhas in the world to the coming of the Patriarchs from the West—it is all contained within this very moment.
The old masters of the world, whether speaking directly or indirectly, never depart from this very moment. Thus it is said:
"If you wish to know the meaning of Buddha-nature, you should contemplate the conditions of time and season. When the time and season arrive, its principle will manifest of itself.
But what is this principle that manifests of itself? The imperial domain matches the North Pole; the Sage’s longevity equals the Southern Mountain.
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: pointing one finger to heaven was already beyond words; pointing one finger to the earth—do not misunderstand this.
Throughout heaven and earth, one may know the rites; yet "I alone am supreme"—this is a mouth that brings disaster. At such a moment as this:

How can one fully comprehend this? [The Master] picks up his staff and says: "For ten thousand ages it flies like a long white silk ribbon; a single line breaks through the color of the green mountains.

On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascends the hall and says: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. If we do not beat the hoeing drum, our own field will fall into ruin. Ignorance...

He dismissed the master of the house and told everyone to stop this chaotic clamor; all those with red mouths and white tongues were completely eliminated, and the "True Person of No Station" broke into a sweat like rain.
He ascended the hall and said, citing a monk who asked Nan-yuan, "After [the Buddhas and] the various sages, where do they go? Nan-yuan replied, "They do not ascend to heaven."
The Abbot entered the hall. The monk immediately fell into hell. The monk asked, "What about you, Master? The Abbot said, "Do you know where Old Baoying has fallen?
The monk hesitated. The Abbot struck him across the mouth with his whisk. He then called the monk forward and said, "The order was meant for you to carry out.
He struck another blow with the whisk. Xuedou said, "Since the order was carried out by himself, the whisk did not even know it."
Regarding the place of origin, Xuedou says, "Blind. This is intended to add frost to snow.
Miaoxi said, "To weigh Linji’s Three Essentials and Three Mysteries, one must still look to Nanuan.
Why then did Xuedou say, "The whisk does not know its place of origin"? Miaoxi said, "Blind," so that both may see each other. The Master said, "Although Xuedou..."
This is indeed a master of clear vision; yet, for now, he does not know where Old Baoying has fallen.
Since he does not know where Old Baoying has fallen, why does he instead say, "The whisk does not know its place of origin; it possesses but a single eye"?
The old fellow Miaoxi says "blind"—this is like when a member of one household dies and a member of another household offers condolences.
Ascending the hall, he said: "How many times born, how many times dead? Birth and death drift on endlessly without fixed end.

Since I suddenly awakened to the non-arising of all things, what sorrow or joy can there be amidst all honors and insults? He then suddenly took up his staff and said, "This [staff] is not 'non-arising'."
"Where has Master Yongjia gone? [The Master] struck the incense altar and said, "He is right here. He threw down his staff and said, "Swift as the imperial decree!
Ascending the hall, he said: "Filling the ears is not sound; filling the eyes is not form. In every land is Avalokiteśvara; in every speck of dust is Maitreya. Right before one's eyes—"
There is an indication: throughout the entire world there are no traces. Since there are no traces, what can be attained? Do you see the wall yet? [Later,] he ascended the hall and said:
"What thing comes like this? Do not mistake the bridge of a donkey's saddle for your father’s chin. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The magpies chatter in the forest; the fish swim beneath the water. The barbarian monk wears golden rings in both ears; he has worn out his straw sandals and runs barefoot.
If you seek a wondrous or extraordinary understanding, it is not worth half a penny.
If you deliberate upon it as something ordinary and substantial, it is entirely within my hands. He took up his staff and said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of Chu was secretly transmitted from east to west.
As soon as it is mentioned, the skull is shattered; one has already been pierced by his twelve-foot needle and driven by his eight-foot wedge.

Yet you further open your great mouth and say, 'I transcend the Buddhas and surpass the Patriarchs, cutting off past and present. To be so ignorant of good and evil—by no means should you enter the gate of the patch-robed monks."
He descended from his seat. Why? "A murder may be forgiven, but rudeness is unforgivable.
He ascended the hall and said: "One is one, two is two; three is three, four is four. North, south, east, and west—each according to its place. Look closely:
they are just like the local guardian spirits in a village of three households; they simply lack the wisdom of transformation."
O King, it would be like suddenly taking Pūrvavideha and placing it in Aparagoyānī, or turning Jambudvīpa into Uttarakuru;
it would be like riding a horse on the bottom of the great ocean or sailing a boat upon Mount Sumeru.
Where else could you possibly search?
At a formal assembly, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, "The entire Canon of the Great Teaching is a 'cutting' (a homophone for *qiè*).
I wonder, what word does it cut? The Master said, "It cuts the word 'not' (*bù*). The monk pressed further, "As for that very word 'not,' what word does it cut?
The Master said, "Do not mistakenly present this to others. The monk said, "Thank you for your instruction. The Master said, "The stone ram's head faces east."
[The Master] looks [at the assembly] and says: "Among all forms of offering, the offering of the Dharma is supreme. While it is not that there is no offering, what is this Dharma?
Do not say I am deceiving you. Namo Buddhāya. Namo Dharmāya. Namo Saṃghāya. He strikes the ground with his staff and says:
"Mountains, rivers, the great earth, grasses, trees, thickets, and forests—all enter into equality right here. They have not yet attained liberation."

This causes those who have not yet attained liberation to attain liberation, and those who have not yet attained *nirvāṇa* to attain *nirvāṇa*. Although one stands within the domain of the patch-robed monk (*sōng-sung*), it is like being at a household where there is a lethal poison;
one must not let even a single drop of water from it touch oneself. Relying upon the staff, he descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: Long and short are the new bamboo shoots; Scattered and sparse are the old fences.
Dense and thin are the bean pods; Red and white are the poppy flowers. The mountains are green and the waters are lush;
The soup is fragrant and the rice is cooked. Having eaten, go wherever you please; Who can endure your idle constraints? He took up his staff and said:
"Can you still be bound by it? He threw it down and said, "One must not lack freedom.

A donor was building a Buddha hall; the Master ascended the hall and said: "In the past, there was a scholar who asked Changsha, 'I have studied the Sutra of the Thousand Buddhas, yet though I have seen the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, I do not know in what lands they dwell. Changsha called out, 'Scholar!'"
Cai merely gave his assent. The Monk said, "After Huang Tingjian inscribed the Yellow Crane Tower, did you, Scholar, ever compose an inscription yourself?
Cai replied, "I have not. The Monk said, "When you have leisure, it would be well to compose a verse. The Master offered this verse: "The names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are heard;
But what of the lands from whence they come? A single poem from within the Yellow Crane Tower— Let it stand through all eternity."

They vied with one another for the lead. He ascended the hall and said: "Maitreya, the true Maitreya, manifests a thousand billion bodies. From time to time he shows himself to those of this age, yet those of this age do not recognize him.
He took up his staff and said: "He breaks through the azure void where pines reach a thousand fathoms; he cuts off the red dust of the world where a stream flows across a single brook."

lower character pronounced *lì*) Jué (pronounced *jué*) Hāo (pronounced *hào*) Hàn (pronounced *hàn*) Kào (pronounced *kào*) Hào (pronounced *hào*) [End of] Volume Two of the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Furi Puzhao Huidian Chushi.
Record of the Sayings of the Abbot at Tianning Yongzuo Chan Monastery in Haian Prefecture, Volume One.
Compiled by the monk-disciples Wenxian and others.
On the third day of the second month in the first year of the Tianli era, the Master entered the monastery.
At the mountain gate, at the bustling marketplace gate, thousands come and ten thousands go; yet how many are there who enter the temple to look at its nameplate?
Again he asks: "What is it? and then one enters.
The Buddha Hall. "This is you; this is me. Sprinkling earth, sprinkling sand, entering and exiting through the same gate—these are karmic enemies in life and death.
Occupying the chamber: here is no secret room for the transmission of the Dharma. A painful blow, a hot shout, under the bright sun and clear sky.
Should you hesitate even for a moment, you go to Western Qin while I remain in Eastern Lu.
He held up the memorial from the Xuanzheng Yuan. "In the past at Vulture Peak, there was a personal entrustment; today, the entrustment is given to Vulture Peak.
"What serves as the proof? He pointed to the memorial and said, "This serves as the proof."
"The Dharma seat at Vulture Peak Hall has already finished preaching the Dharma for all of you. Did you hear it?
If you did not hear it, you cannot avoid the fault of adding legs to a snake. Having said this, he ascended the seat.

Holding up the incense, he said: "This one portion of incense is offered specifically to pray for the long life of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!

This one portion of incense is respectfully offered for the officials of the Xuanzheng Yuan, the officials of the Jiaxing Prefecture, and the officials of the Haiyan Prefecture, that they may all increase [in merit and longevity]."
Regarding the calculation of merit:

this single offering of incense is respectfully presented to the World-Honored Elder Master Yuansou Duan, the Fourth Generation Dharma-heir of Miaoxi, currently presiding at Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Temple on Mount Jing, in order to repay the kindness of his Dharma-milk. [The Master] then remains seated.

The Master said: "When the heavens and earth are firmly secured, there is no passage for water to leak through; when the path is opened, I allow you to deliberate. Is there such a thing? Is there? A monk asked:
"Mountains are green and waters are blue; white peaches and red plums. North, south, east, and west—all are the soil and water of the King.
The four quarters and the zenith and nadir—none are outside the gate of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. At this very moment, I pray that the Master will offer a benediction."
The Master said, "Five days of wind, ten days of rain. The student asked, "In that case, one strikes and bumps against [reality] at every turn?
The Master said, "It depends. The student said, "The spring colors have no high or low; the flower branches are naturally long or short. The Master said, "I only fear it is not jade.

The student said, "The head monk and the chief administrator have been selected by public consensus as the abbot. The dignitaries of the entire prefecture have together attended this Dharma assembly. The Master said, "Not yet."
"What matter is being clearly revealed? The Master said, "The verification is right before your eyes.
The student asked, "Master Wuzu Yan said: 'A stretch of vacant land before the mountain; with hands folded, he earnestly questions his forefather.
Several times he sold it, yet he buys it back again, for he loves the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure breeze. Now, what is this ancestral land? The Master said, "Look at your feet."
The student bowed. He stepped forward and asked, "To whom will you sell it? The Master said, "Listening to matters without sincerity.
The student asked, "If one does not treat it as precious nor as cheap, how will you buy it? The Master said, "Sixty kalpas across three lifetimes.
The student said, "Alas, the Master has completely cut off all possibilities! The Master said, "Walls and screens have ears. The student asked, "As for the deed of sale above, what is it?"
A person copied [this]. The Master said, "Today the east wind has arisen. The student stepped forward and said, "I thank the Master for your instruction.
The Master said, "Wait until another time for those thirty blows. He then said, "In the past, when I was on this mountain, I received ordination; I was a *śrāmaṇera* who had shed his white robes."
Suddenly thrust out by others before the assembly of devas and humans, you are called "Elder. You who are like muddied pigs or scabby dogs—can you still avoid it?
Today, you are placed upon the curved wooden chair; as he points east and draws west for you, this is the very first step into the gate, the first ladle of foul water.
Reaching this point, with no other choice, one must break through the mask and employ some expedient means.
Wisteria. East of Katsuge, west of Katsuge. Thus, when the morning star appeared before Mount Vimalasvabhāva, the Elder Śākyamuni suddenly attained great enlightenment.
But tell me, what did he awaken to? Today, as I open the hall to preach the Dharma, what more could I possibly say?
I cannot help but pour a second ladle of foul water over you all. (He raises his staff.)
*Claps the desk once. Takes a draught.* Again he raises the case:
When the Sixth Patriarch arrived at the Faxing Temple in Guangzhou, he took up residence in the corridors.

One evening, as the wind blew the temple banner, he heard two monks debating it. One said, "The banner moves. The other said, "The wind moves. They exchanged words back and forth, yet [the Master] never...
[The Master] said, "This accords with the principle. The Patriarch [Huineng] said, "Can one allow worldly people to engage in lofty discourse with you?

It is simply that it is not the wind or the banner that moves; it is your mind, O virtuous one, that moves. The Master [Xuefeng] said, "All you Chan practitioners, I have already picked up the matter for you: the wind moves, the banner moves, and the mind moves."
"Where can one see the Patriarch?
That evening, there was a small assembly (xiaocan). [The Master] raised the case of Venerable Tong’an Pi, concerning a monk who asked: "What is the house style of the Master?"

An said, "The golden cockling its chicks leaves the mists of heaven; the jade hare conceiving her fetus enters the Purple Microcosm. A monk asked, "If a guest should suddenly arrive, with what will you receive them?
An said, "The golden fruit was plucked by the monkey early at dawn; the jade blossom was pecked by the phoenix late in the evening. The Master said:
"In the interplay of the orthodox and the deviant, one does not strike the sharp edge. In the free and easy movement of question and answer, only the noble and honored is revealed."
The Elder of Tong’an was accustomed to seizing the opportune moment. When someone asked, "Tianning, what is the house style of the Master?
he replied, "Rice in the alms bowl. When suddenly encountering a guest, with what would he receive them? "A cup of tea after the meal."
Now tell me, is this the same as the ancients, or is it different?
[He] ascended the hall and said: "The golden blade cannot cut it; the colored brush can hardly paint it. Do not bring it from a thousand miles away;
sweep away all manner of things. The Elder Śākyamuni said: "One should know thus, see thus, and believe and understand thus, so that [delusions] do not arise."
The characteristics of dharmas are precisely what pushes the waves and aids the current; one has not yet attained liberation. What is the phrase for liberation?
"The peony blooms upon the Bodhisattva’s face; the palm leaves scatter from the Yakṣa’s head."

Ascending the hall: There are worms in the rice; there is flour in the wheat. The kitchen, the storehouse, the monks' hall, the mountain gate, and the Buddha hall—when the cup falls to the ground, the plate breaks into seven pieces.
The Record-keeper Xuechuang Guang of Jingci Monastery ascends the hall. [He recites: "The Superior Man (Shang Daren), Qiu Yiji, transforming three thousand, seventy scholars;
you, the young student, eight or nine children; well-composed benevolence—this may be known as ritual. He calls to the assembly, saying: "What kind of talk is this?
None of the disciples of Confucius recognized it; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head."
Ascending the hall: Crows cry in the ancient trees; dogs bark in the deep forest. Clouds stretch across the unbroken green mountains;

tides recede from the boundless blue sea. Fishermen’s songs emerge from the harbor; as they go their way, flocks of herons fly back to roost. Sunlight pierces through the woods; everywhere, cooking smoke rises in competition.
In the farming villages, the wheat is ripe, so they immediately plant the rice. When the neighbor’s wife’s silkworms sleep, she goes with her kin to peel the cocoons. They buy salt...
Buying vinegar; transporting timber and carrying firewood; untying moorings and hoisting sails; dangling the whip and drooping the sleeves; burning incense and sweeping the floor;
joining palms and shaking the head—Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra have, without cause, given rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma and have already been banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains.
Is there anyone who can save them? If there were, it would not hinder the resurrection of the dead. If there is none, then listen as they are buried.
Filling the ditches and blocking the ravines.
As the donor ascended the hall, Nanquan said: "The entire earth is the patron of the Old Teacher.
If the giver forms the thought of giving, it is not true giving; if the receiver forms the thought of receiving, it is not true receiving. If the giver..."
If one perceives [the recipient] as a gift-giver, one enters hell like an arrow shot. If the recipient perceives [themselves] as a receiver, they too must bite iron and carry a saddle.
Do not let it slip past Nanquan. He ascended the hall and said:
"In the heavens there is no Maitreya; on the earth there is no Maitreya. The white moon seals the thousand rivers;
the clear breeze arises in the eight directions. Holding up his whisk, he asked: "What is this? Then he added: "Even the whisk-tail fan is not recognized."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Jia Shan, "What is a 'similarity phrase'? Shan replied, "The lotus leaf is round and round, as round as a mirror;
the water chestnut is pointed and pointed, as pointed as an awl. He then asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not understand.
Shan said, "The wind blows the willow catkins like a ball; the rain beats the pear blossoms like butterflies in flight. The Master said, "Old man Jia Shan..."
He did not answer. It was like a peach blossom blooming on a bamboo stalk—adding splendor upon splendor; yet, he had simply not yet touched upon the fundamental matter.
If someone were to ask Tianning, "What is a phrase that corresponds? he would say to him:
"Do not take Zhi Dun’s crane and call it Yujun’s goose."
The donor invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "Before the primordial chaos was divided, how was it? You speak of a pillar conceiving a fetus; please, Master, give us instruction.
The Master said, "This is an old story from all quarters. The monk pressed further, "How should a student proceed toward realization? The Master said:
"A dragon is not formed upon a staff. [The monk] asked, "What is it like after the division? [The Master replied,] "Like a fragment of cloud dotting the vast void; whether it is truly so or not.
The Master said, "Once a word has been spoken, even four horses cannot overtake it. [The monk] asked, "I do not yet know: does the vast void itself receive the dot?
At that time, Lingyun did not answer. Wherein lay his meaning? The Master said, "There are no tracks or traces."
The student said, "In that case, even if sentient beings do not come, you still do not respond. Tell me, is it responding or is it not responding?
The Master said, "Releasing a black rooster at midnight. The student said, "What is it like when one has attained utter purity, free from even a single speck of dust?"
"This is still the flow of the eternal and constant. The monk asked, "Is this the same as or different from the place where you grant [the Dharma]?
The Master said, "The verdict is reached according to the facts. The monk pressed, "What is the flow of the eternal and constant? [The Master replied,] "It is like a mirror that is always bright.
The monk asked, "Why do you call it a mirror? The Master said, "It is truly a pity. The monk asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "Bring me the broken mirror."
"I have met you. [The Master asked: "What was the intention of the ancients? The teacher said, "This too is Xu Liu carrying a one-sided board.

[The student] further asked, "The moon in the empty expanse of the ten-thousand-year-old green pool—only after repeatedly searching for it can one truly know it. The teacher said, "Falling into pits and falling into ravines."
The monks prostrated. The Master then said: "If one discusses that great matter prior to the existence of either sentient beings or Buddhas, it resides right beneath the feet of everyone;
as soon as you move, you step upon it. It is simply that you do not know its point of origin. Tell me, from where does it arise?
To overturn the four great oceans and kick over the five Mount Sumerus—yet even then, one cannot find its point of origin. Have you not seen?"
The Patriarch Yeon of Dongshan said: "Yesterday, this mountain monk entered the city and saw a stage of puppet theater. Unable to resist, I drew near to watch.
I saw some figures that were dignified and extraordinary, while others were ugly and unsightly; they moved, walked, and sat about.
I observed every detail—blue, yellow, red, and white—and looked closely at them all. To my surprise, there was actually a person behind the blue cloth curtain. The mountain monk could not help but...
Unable to restrain himself, Jun asked the Chief Secretary his surname. The man replied, "The old monk has finished looking; what is there to ask about a surname?
The Master said, "In the pond of someone’s private villa, a pair of mandarin ducks cannot be fully captured in a painting."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand people crowding the gate are not equal to one person pulling the bolt.
If one person pulls the bolt, then thousands and tens of thousands will reach the ground of non-action and peace and happiness. Let me, this mountain monk, exert my strength for you all.
With his hand, he beckoned and said: "Come back! Come back!"
Ascending the hall: Before the Cold Food Festival and after Qingming, rain beats upon the peach blossoms and the wind blows through the stone mortars.
Lately, the prices of all things have been level; white rice is three cash per bushel. Good brother, go to the meditation hall.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Qianfeng, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions all share the single path to the gate of nirvāṇa;
I wonder, where does the beginning of that path lie? Qianfeng took his staff, drew a line, and said, "Right here. The Master remarked, "Ten thousand miles of white clouds.
The monk then recounted this previous dialogue and asked Yunmen about it. Yunmen said, "The fan leaps up to the thirty-third heaven."
"He strikes right at the nostrils of Śakra; he gives a single blow to the carp of the Eastern Sea, and the rain pours down like an overturned basin.
The Master said, "Ten thousand miles of white clouds. Suddenly, if someone were to come forth and ask Tianning, "Does such a critical judgment accord with the intent of those two great elders?
I would say to him, "Ten thousand miles of white clouds. Hehehe! Lalala lalala!
"How many can be known across every land and within every speck of dust? At the crossroads stands the Stone Daring-to-Meet. Suddenly, he sucks dry the waters of the vast ocean.
You fellows, you eggplants and gourds—how could you possibly know this? He struck the meditation seat and rose.

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Emperor’s Birthday, a monk asked, "I do not ask about the causes and conditions of the Buddhas and Patriarchs; what is the matter of the meeting of ruler and subject?
The Master said, "Auspicious grass grows in a fortunate era; forest flowers bloom in early spring. The monk pressed further, "What is the Ruler? The Master said:
"Do not offend the Emperor's countenance. The Official asked, "What is the subject? The Master said, "Appointing to office according to one's capacity.
The Official asked, "What is the subject facing the sovereign? The Master said, "A sincere heart, piece by piece. The Official asked, "What is the sovereign looking upon the subject? The Master said:

It is like the moon entering the water. Jin asked, "What is the convergence of the Way between sovereign and subject? The Master said, "Both. He then cited the debate between Wuzhuo and a non-Buddhist (tīrthika).
Wuzhuo said, "The world is at peace; the king lives long. The non-Buddhist was silenced and could not refute him. The Master offered this verse:
"The meanings are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, yet they do not go beyond this single phrase. A mosquito alights upon an iron ox."
There is no place for you to open your mouth. Entering the hall [he said]:

"Though the eyebrows are long, they do not obstruct the eyes; though the nostrils are high, they do not obstruct the face. Though the Buddhas have attained enlightenment, there is no duality in their mind;
though sentient beings are deluded, there is no duality in their vision. Whether seeing or not seeing—riding a cow backward, one enters the Buddha Hall."
When the Buddha was about to enter nirvana, he ascended the hall and bared his chest, showing it to the assembly, saying: "If you wish to see the Old Man Śākyamuni, recognize him right here.
You must observe well my body of purple-golden hue; today it exists, but tomorrow it will be no more."
"Hey! You wild fox spirit, shrink your head and get out! The Buddhas of the past were like this; the Buddhas of the present are like this;
the Buddhas of the future will be like this. He strikes the meditation staff once and says, "Like this, like this.
Then he strikes it again and says, "Not so, not so."
Ascending the hall for the two orders of monks during their advancement and retreat: those on the east go to the east; those on the west go to the west. Going, they truly do not go;
an iron weight has been eaten through by worms. Coming, they truly do not come; a lantern climbs the wall toward the terrace.
Now tell me, where does the Immovable Honored One dwell? A single shaft pierces the three barriers—clearly, it is behind the arrow.
On the Road. Ascending the hall, he said: "The mind is fundamentally Buddha; its contrived activity is not it. The Way does not require cultivation; it cannot be defiled.
This very non-defilement is what all Buddhas protect and keep in mind. To speak thus is already defilement. A single thread.
A single thought-moment binds one to the karmic causes of the three miserable realms; in an instant, a deluded emotion arises, and for ten thousand kalpas one remains shackled. Thus, a sutra says:
"If one sees me by means of form, or seeks me through sound, such a person walks a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata.
You say, "Which one is the Tathāgata? It is the one with copper-colored head and iron-jawed face, with a bird’s beak and a fish’s gills.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "To see form is to see the mind. The great earth, mountains, and rivers are the mind.
How do you see them? He further said: "The mind does not see the mind; there is no characteristic to be grasped. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva transformed himself into this lacquered staff and traveled once around the four continents. Upon returning to my hands, it has turned out to be..."
Master Bāzhuo said: "If you have a staff, I will give you a staff; if you have no staff, I will take your staff away from you.
If you attempt to deliberate upon this as a matter of Buddhist Dharma, you will fall alive into hell. [The Master] leaned on his staff.
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas;

yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "There is no such meaning. There is no 'what about it'."
Jin asked, "I do not yet understand when one attains the Way of the Buddha. The Master said, "There is neither Buddha nor Way.
Jin asked, "Does this not fall into emptiness? The Master said, "Emptiness itself is empty. Jin asked, "Who is it that speaks of emptiness right now?"
The Master said, "This lacquer bucket! The monk stepped forward and said, "Originally there is no hindrance; wherever one goes, one may take on any shape.
The Master said, "Xuan Sha spoke the bottom line," and then he continued: "With great perfect enlightenment as my monastery, body and mind dwell in peace; this is the wisdom of equality.
He called to the assembly, saying, "Since the wisdom of nature is already equal, what can be said of 'saint' and what can be said of 'ordinary'? What more could be said?
"Mami! What is there to speak of as 'awakening'? It was thus in the past, it is thus now; it is thus for the monastics, it is thus for the laity.
Whether entering or exiting, what hinders one’s summer retreat? Whether coming or going, this is the true observance of the *śīlavrata* (the foot-binding vow).
It is like a tiny gnat building a nest upon the eye-lashes of a mosquito, crying out at the crossroads: 'The land is vast!'"
People are few; those who meet [the truth] are rare. Furthermore, there is a verse that says: A golden-maned lion and a dung-eating dog;
A snow-white elephant king and a mill-turning donkey. If, right here and now, you do not give rise to inverted views, Then throughout the ninety days, there will be neither deficiency nor excess.
The Record of the Inscription on the Ancient Tripod at Lingyin. Upon ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The Samādhi of the World-Honored One was not known by Kāśyapa;
the Samādhi of Kāśyapa was not known by Ānanda; the Samādhi of Ānanda was not known by Śāṇakavāsin; the Samādhi of Śāṇakavāsin was not known by Upagupta.
Let us set aside for now that the Samādhis of each of these patriarchs were unknown to one another. Now, call forth Śi..."
[He] entered the *mòzuò* samādhi. After a long while, he said: "Apart from the head and horns of the yellow dragon, everything else is nothing but a red-spotted snake.
He ascended the hall, took up his whisk, struck the meditation seat, and said: "The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can save the world from suffering. [Then he asked: "Does it still..."
"Did you hear it? He struck once more and said, "Why do I not hear it? He addressed the assembly, saying, "Do not say that I am deceiving you;
you are deceiving me far too much!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The horns of a rabbit need not be non-existent; the horns of an ox need not be existent. Two by two do not form a pair; three by three are likewise not nine.
Last night, empty-handed, I grasped a hoe; at dawn, facing south, I looked at the Big Dipper."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Sometimes speech must be discerned; sometimes silence—who can fully comprehend it? For those of long-standing practice who are superior men, there is no need for repeated instruction.
For beginners of late study, it is difficult to reach a mutual understanding at once. It is just as it is said: 'If one approaches a superior person to ask about the Way, one loses the Way;
if one approaches an inferior person to ask about the Way, one attains the Way. Neither superior nor inferior—there is neither attainment nor loss. The Way resides in the ordinary."
At that time, sometimes riding upon the bright moon, he would cross the vast ocean by himself.
He ascended the hall and said: "If you can turn things over, you are the same as the Tathāgata. You say, 'How does one turn things over? Walk from the monks' hall into the Buddha hall;
pass from the Buddha hall into the monks' hall. Ride upon Mount Sumeru while talking with an ox; [be like] a wooden man."
Beating drums and singing songs; the pillar plays the zither every day. The *gandi* claps its hands and laughs at him. But tell me, what is it that he laughs at?
Hehe! Then he descended from his seat.
The Small General Talk for the End of the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "What is the student's own self? The Master said, "You ask me to find it.
He then continued, "Gentlemen, to have everything settled and perfected is what is called being a person of no affairs.
If you go to other places, they will surely arrange for you a place by a bright window. Here at Yongzuo, however, I cannot let you off so easily. Why is this? Because everything has been settled..."
"Qian Dangdi is still halfway there. Have you not seen how Master Yuanwu said: 'If one uses worldly dharmas to receive people, they fall into worldly dharmas;
if one uses the mechanism of the patriarchs and Buddhas to receive people, they fall into the mechanism of the patriarchs and Buddhas;
if one uses the upward-pointing extraction and presentation to receive people, they fall into the upward-pointing extraction and presentation. "In this way..."
If you receive people by means of "suchness," you fall into the midst of "suchness. If you receive people by means of "not suchness," you fall into the midst of "not suchness.
If you receive people by means of "neither suchness nor not suchness," you fall into the midst of "neither suchness nor not suchness.
Even if there is not a single speck of cloud ten thousand miles away—
Even the blue sky must receive a blow of the staff. You should know that this matter is not obtained from elsewhere.
"In the treasury of our King there is no such sword; yet this sword does not leave the King’s treasury. The final phrase is where one first arrives at the secure barrier;
it blocks the vital ford, allowing neither ordinary nor sage to pass. For ninety days, what do you say regarding this final phrase? The fiery clouds of midsummer.

Burning the Verdant Cave: In the clear autumn, perilous dewdrops fall upon the golden basin. Again, the Master raised a case where a monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall?
Yunmen said, "The body is exposed in the golden wind. The Master said: "If this monk had said, 'Thank you for your answer to my question,' [he would have been right]."
Master Yunmen would surely find it difficult to justify his reasoning. I, this mountain monk, am not like that. When the trees wither and the leaves fall, what then?
[The Master] raises his staff; as soon as [the student] hesitates, he drives him out of the Dharma Hall, thereby sparing him from being scrutinized by those in all quarters.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: To purchase vermilion cinnabar to paint the moon is, upon calculation, a labor spent in vain;

to apply pure white powder to create it likewise does not constitute the true moon. Mañjuśrī said: "If the one moon is truly such, within it there is naturally neither 'this is the moon' nor 'this is not the moon.
Holding up his whisk, he said: "Fundamentally, there is no place of partial illumination; yet, there are times when it is not clearly manifest."
Master Zhiquan of Lingyin ascended the hall for the morning service. He cited Master Guanghui Lian’s words:
"When I was in my late teacher’s assembly, I saw him raise a bamboo stick and ask the monk Xing: 'If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit an offense;
if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you turn your back on the truth. What shall you do? Xing stepped forward, snatched the stick away, and threw it to the ground, saying, 'What is this?'"

The former master said, "Blind! From this, Xing entered into awakening. I say that although Xing, that donkey-man, has indeed awakened to a great extent, he has still not exhausted the intent of the former master.
The Master said, "Great Guanghui, speaking as you do, does the former master truly have an underlying intent?
Take a torch and look; how thick is his skin? Not running while going downhill—what a swift opportunity!"
It is difficult to encounter. If you wish to be upheld in the higher sense, you must first return to my elder brother, Master Zhuyu.
Upon ascending the hall for the consecration of a stupa, a monk asked: "In the past, when National Teacher Nanquan was questioned by Zhaozhou, who asked, 'What is the Way?
Nanquan replied, 'The ordinary mind is the Way. What is the ordinary mind? The Master said: "Strike ice to fetch [the moon]."
"Huo! [The Master] dug into the ground to seek the heavens. Jin said, "Truly excellent is the ordinary mind.
The Master said, "I am not your equal; you have understood it well yourself. Then he said, "Since your question was not weak and your answer was indeed extraordinary, tell me:
do you accord with the two great elders, or do you not accord with the two great elders? Is there anyone who can say so? Come forward and speak! If no one can say it, [then I shall explain]."
He departed from the hall himself. One portion he offered to Śākyamuni Buddha; one portion he offered to the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha. He ascended the hall and said:
"All of you, when you see me open my mouth, you immediately take it as a discourse on the Dharma;
when you see me remain silent, you immediately take it as silence. You all seek me at both extremes; how do you know that I am not at either extreme? You say, 'Ordinarily...'"
"In what place? Is it that you stand atop a high peak without showing your head? Or that you walk upon the bottom of the deep sea without getting your feet wet?
If you act like this, you have already been found by him. Do you know the mountain monk’s secret for hiding one's form?
"Throughout the day one does not see them, yet they are always present; all day long one meets them, yet they are not met. All thoughts are but...
The shackles of affliction—when the mind is absent, this is truly the Crystal Palace.

(A shout. Entering the hall, [the Master said: "The ancients were truly sincere in their concern for others; they would simply set things down and be at ease. I, however, do not act thus: I lift my robes and go forth immediately.
Though it is the same in that we tread upon our straw sandals, why follow behind the heels of others? He took up his staff and said:
The staff rides the Buddha hall and goes out through the mountain gate. Entering the hall for discourse:
A great tree is wrapped in great bark; a small tree is bound with small bark. If one does not sleep on the same bed, how can one know that the lining of the quilt is worn through?
Winter Night Small Sermon. A monk asked, "When the ten-thousand-fathom cold pond has frozen through to the bottom, what then?
The Master said, "When the yang energy arises, there is no hard ground. He then said, "If you wish to attain such a matter, you must be such a person.
If you are such a person, why worry about such a matter? To call it 'such a matter' is already to create trouble where there is none; how much more so [to dwell upon it]!"
A collection of miscellaneous talk from the head of the assembly. Chasing after praise until time has passed; today the third day, tomorrow the fourth. Inside the belly, it is pitch black;
beneath the feet, one is floating and pressed down. When the mallet is raised and the whisk held up, he does not see it. When fingers snap and a cough is made, he does not hear it.
When the mouth opens and the tongue moves, he does not understand it. He is like a holeless iron hammer; you have merely nurtured him into this state.
Ten thousand [times]—what use is there? The trampling of dragons and elephants is not something a donkey can endure. The Goose King selects the milk; he has never been of the class of ducks.
It is valued only in being directly realized right now, without turning the head or shifting the brain, without establishing even a hair’s breadth.
