The Master said, “East, west, south, north—eighty thousand miles. Then he said, “The clay Buddha is submerged.”
It is finished! The wooden Buddha has been burned; the golden Buddha has been melted down; the true Buddha has been scrutinized through and through.
The old fellow Zhaozhou has been expelled from the monastery. Once gone, he will never return. *Duḥ!* (A blow!)
Ascending the hall, he said: "The handless man performs a fist-punch; the tongueless man understands speech.
Suddenly, if the handless man strikes the tongueless man, the tongueless man hurriedly says, 'Not necessary. He further says, 'Just this "not necessary"—no monk in the world can leap out of it.'"
Ascending the hall: Last night the drum asked the sound of the bell; today the bell answers the sound of the drum. The wooden fish by the corridor opens its mouth and laughs:
"You base fellow, you treat the Buddha-dharma as mere social courtesy!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The heavens are high in the southeast; the Yangtze, Yellow, Huai, and Ji Rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea does not overflow.

The earth inclines toward the northwest; the sun, moon, and stars are suspended in the void, yet the void does not descend. Everyone has a straight nose and slanted eyes; every day the days are bright and the nights are dark.
The Buddhas did not appear in this world, and the Patriarchs did not come from the West. The Buddha-dharma pervades the world. He spoke thus.
The dark mouth does not open. Do you understand? Śākyamuni the Old Man was in the Western Heaven; Mañjuśrī the Great Being dwells in this Eastern Land.

Entering the hall: before one has even approached, one is already separated by a great thousandfold world-system. The imperial carriage has already entered the Han-yuan Hall, yet he still strikes the "silence-whip" upon the empty steps.
Ascending the hall, he said: "One way of speaking is that water flows to the damp and fire seeks the dry. Another way of speaking is that wind follows the dragon and clouds follow the tiger.
Why is this? Because the human heart is difficult to satisfy, while ravines and gullies are easily filled."
Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "The holy regulations of the Tathāgata prohibit [the monks from traveling] to protect living beings.
Is the life of a single ant the same as or different from the lives of all people? The Master said, "When a monkey is distressed, it scratches its head.

The monk pressed further, "Are the lives of all people the same as or different from the lives of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? The Master said, "When a dog runs, it shakes its mouth. The monk pressed further, "The ancients..."
[The monk said: "In the human realm, to protect life one must kill; only when all have been killed does one find peace. I wonder, what is it that is killed?
The Master said, "Study this for another thirty years. The monk stepped forward and said, "Transcending form and transcending name, no one receives [the transmission].

When the 'blow-off-the-hair' blade has been used, it must be sharpened immediately. The Master said, "Wrong. The monk then shouted. The Master picked up his staff; the monk prostrated. The Master then said, "A single ant."
"Nature and life" refers precisely to the nature and life of all people. The nature and life of all people is the very nature and life of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
It is "one for Ding and two for Zhuo," "kicking seven and trampling eight. Those who are long have a long Dharma-body; those who are short have a short Dharma-body.

It is just like the shifting transition of cold and heat, the alternating exchange of Yin and Yang: day after day the sun rises in the east, day after day the sun sets in the west. This is mind; this is environment.
"Existence and non-existence—what kind of principle is this? Today I tie the mouth of the sack shut. Existence is covered by the sack;
non-existence is also covered by the sack. For now, there is no way out at all.
If you wish for the mouth of the sack to open, it must remain fixed for ninety days; not even a single day may be subtracted from it. He then cited the World-Honored One:
He ascended the seat. Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said, "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King is thus.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat. The Master said, "I thought the World-Honored One had some other special excellence, yet he simply ended it with a sense of regret (*mala*).
This has brought about the fate of his descendants in later generations, each of whom is a dragon's head and a snake's tail."

Ascending the hall, he closed the gate of the Sangha Hall and asked someone to guard the monastery. This did not yet constitute a "total raising" (of the Dharma). The entire earth has been left desolate;
he is precisely one who deserves a blow of the staff. If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate cause for worry.
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. The mugwort man rides upon a mugwort tiger, galloping north, south, east, and west.
Upon returning, he says: "All sentient beings throughout the great earth are suffering. This is what is called the suffering of birth, the suffering of old age, and the suffering of illness.
The suffering of death, up to the suffering of the intense proliferation of the five aggregates—all such sufferings can be treated.
Only the mental illness of a Zen practitioner is difficult to treat; neither arsenic nor rock honey, neither licorice nor dried tangerine peel can be used for it.
How, then, can it be cured? I have an ancient prescription that there is nothing it cannot heal. A monk asked Zhaozhou: "A student has just [entered the path]..."
He entered the monastery and requested the Master’s expedient means. Zhaozhou asked, "Have you finished eating your congee? The monk replied, "I have finished. Zhaozhou said, "Go wash your bowl.
To finish the congee and then wash the bowl—there is no need for doubt. When the whale swallows the ocean water, the coral branches are revealed.
[The Master] clapped his hands and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall: Buddha, Buddha, Buddha—they are all muddling through. Patriarch, Patriarch, Patriarch—they are all too reckless. Zen, Zen, Zen—how many varieties are there?
Path after path, straight ahead, is swept clear. This lapis lazuli flask is cherished and protected—what is it?
All of you have already smashed it to pieces. Yet you still come here; what bowl do you seek?
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat, a monk asked: "Before the empty kalpa, beyond the limit of awe-inspiring sound, was there still binding and unbinding?

The Master said: "Do not engage in false imaginings. The monk pressed further: "When one is not engaging in false imaginings, what then? The Master said: "A man who is dozing off. The monk pressed further.
"In the kingdom of Magadha, [the King] personally carried out this order. The Master said, "In the Western Heaven (India), they cut off heads and severed arms.

The student said, "At that time, those who attained the Way were as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. I wonder, in the mountains today, how many people have attained the Way? The Master said, "A fly laying its eggs.
The student said, "If that is so, then the assembly on Vulture Peak has remained solemnly without dispersing. The Master said, "Upon the soil."
He added more mud and said: "The entirety of the worlds in the ten directions is this very body of true human nature.

Awakening and affliction, birth and death, nirvana, the conditioned and the unconditioned, the sages of the past and the sages of the future, the commencement and dissolution of the retreat, the long-term and the short-term—all are it."
In the true essence, there is no meeting at all. Xuefeng went to Touzi three times and ascended Dongshan nine times;
it was only at the end, at the Ao Shan Inn, that he lost his nostrils. Da sui consulted with over sixty virtuous spiritual friends.
Changqing sat until seven meditation cushions were worn through. At the staff-blow from Dajue, Xinghua deeply clarified the intent of Huangbo. He [then] overturned...
Turning over the seas and mountains, laying aside the spears and shields—this is like exchanging a thousand pounds of valley echoes for ten thousand fragments of empty flowers.

Beyond the limit of majestic sound, prior to the empty kalpa: as long as there is speech, there is no real meaning. It pierces the nostrils of all people in the world. How can one speak this single phrase?
The great garuḍa spreads its wings, covering the ten continents; the swallows and sparrows by the hedge wall are left empty.
*Chiu-chiu.* Again, [the Master] raised the case of Yunmen during the end of autumn and the beginning of summer. "Suppose someone suddenly asks you on the road ahead:
'I do not know—what would you say to him? Yunmen said, 'Everyone, step back! The monk asked, 'Where does the fault lie?
Yunmen said, 'Give me back my ninety days' worth of rice money. The Master said: "To let this pass is impossible. I ask you: what would you say? Just respond!"
He said, "Seventy-two blows become one hundred and twenty; where does the fault lie?
He replied to him, "You simply take the blows; I want this saying to be put into practice."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Each and every one carries the jade of Mount Jing-shan; everyone harbors the pearl of the vast ocean. They manipulate the pivot and mechanism of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
they grasp the very core of the monks. All claim that the eye atop the head is upright; all say that the talisman behind the elbow is efficacious."
Little do they realize that the numinous tortoise bearing the celestial chart brought about the very omen of its own destruction. How is it to express a phrase that transcends the ordinary?
"When the morning mist does not appear at the market, the evening glow travels a thousand miles."
The Imperial Decree for Viewing the Tripitaka: An Address to the Assembly. A monk asked, "A single imperial edict arrives from the Nine Heavens;
the mountains and rivers of the great earth chant 'Excellent! (Sādhu). Filled with the entire canon, one does not know what it says; the blue lotus blooms within the mouth.

[The Master] said, "In accordance with the imperial decree to view the Tripitaka, we request the Zen Master to offer prayers for the Emperor’s longevity. The Master replied, "One character is one year. The monk stepped forward and said, "Piled like a mountain..."
"How many peaks do they accumulate? We join in wishing for the Dragon Palace to endure through endless years. The Master said, "A tangle of rotten vines.

The student advanced and said, "'To interpret the meaning according to the sutras is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to deviate from the sutras by even a single word is to speak like a demon.

Setting aside these two paths, I ask the Master to discern between them. The Master said, "Ants do not eat iron. He then said, "The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates all return to the single square inch of the mind."
The wondrous virtues of the sands of the Ganges are all contained within the source of the mind. Those of great merit cultivate great merit, and it is by those of great merit that this is received.

Therefore, throughout the lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, there are none who do not receive their majestic spiritual influence; even plants, trees, and insects all rely upon them for their growth and transformation.
Now, the Dharma assembly is fully opened and the treasury of teachings is grandly revealed. Layer upon layer are the gates of merit; various as they are, they are oceans of lifespan.
Like heaven, they cover all; like earth, they support all; like the sun, they shine everywhere; like the wind, they blow everywhere.
Confucius said, "I have long been praying for this. Furthermore, consider Emperor Taizong of the Song dynasty, who once entered a temple and asked a monk, "What sutra are you reading?"
The monk said, "The *Renwang Huguo Jing* (Sutra on the Benevolent Kings Protecting the State). The Emperor said, "Since this is my own sutra, why has it fallen into your hands?
The monk was speechless. Later, Xuedou spoke on his behalf: "Heaven shows no favoritism; it assists only those with virtue. The Master said:
"If I were Yongzuo, I would simply receive the sutra upon my head and say, 'Ten thousand years! Ten thousand years!'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: Nanquan asked Huangbo, "When the world is made of gold and the walls and gates are made of silver, what kind of person dwells there?
Huangbo replied, "A sage dwells there. Nanquan said, "There is yet another person;
in what land does he dwell? Huangbo stood with his hands folded. Nanquan said, "He cannot say it. Why not ask Old Master Wang? Huangbo then asked him.
"Furthermore, there was another person. In which land did he reside? Quan said, "How regrettable!

The Master said, "Of these two great elders, one creates trouble where there is none, while the other takes what is wrong and makes it his own. It is truly laughable. Had I been Huangbo at that time," [he would have acted differently].
He waited for him to say, "There is yet another person; in what land does he dwell? [The Master] simply said, "This wild fox spirit!
Even if Nanquan were possessed of a mouth as vast as the universe, he would still have to swallow his breath and stifle his voice."

Incense Offering on the Anniversary of the First Patriarch’s Death: This fellow came from the West specifically to act like a fool. To say "not relying on words and letters" is merely a hollow display of arrogance;
to say "pointing directly at the human mind" reveals how deep his illness has become; to say "seeing one's nature is to become a Buddha" turns it into nothing more than a conceptual nest.
At Vulture Peak, he simply could not bear that cow dung incense and dog-urine tea were being offered. Why was this so? It was solely because he wished to repay [the Dharma] in such a manner.
"Virtue repays kindness. This is it.

Entering the hall, the Master went before the Dharma Hall; after he had performed the *vaṃdanā* (bowing) together with the assembly, he returned directly to his quarters (*fangzhang*). The assembly followed behind him.
The Master said, "There is not a single one who is truly quick-witted. The assembly then dispersed.
When a patron offered rice and entered the hall upon the mountain, the Master cited Xuefeng’s address to the assembly:

"To take up the entire earth and make it as small as a grain of millet, and then cast it before you—those lacquer buckets do not understand! Let us all strike the drum and ask to look! The Master said, "You..."
When people cannot see it, they sit with their legs crossed upon the long benches in the Sangha Hall and chew it over carefully.
On the day of the Buddha’s Nirvana, he ascends the hall: the fifteenth day of the second month, the Mid-spring Festival; red flowers and white flowers bloom interspersed.
The golden coffin did not merely display the twin footprints; within the flowers, the numinous bird speaks even more eloquently. What does it say? *He lets out a shout.* Entering the hall, he said:
"The three bodies and four wisdoms are not absent from the sages; the eight liberations and six supernormal powers do not exist apart from ordinary beings."
A wooden man holds a board and strikes it amidst the clouds; a stone woman holds a flute and blows it beneath the water. What tune is this? *Pozhenzi*.
The lay practitioners Zhenru and Shan-zhu of Yangfu entered the mountains to provide a vegetarian feast for the monks. [The Master] ascended the hall. Śramaṇa Shi...
My son, with your head atop the donor’s house, your feet upon the donor’s land, your mouth eating the donor’s rice, and your body clothed in the donor’s garments—how will you repay the donor?
If you enter the Way without penetrating its principle, you shall return the very offerings of faith to their source.
When the elder was eighty-one, his tree did not sprout. If one eats all day long without ever biting through a single grain of rice, what is there to offer?
Throughout the day he wears robes, yet not a single thread has ever been attached to them. When walking, no walking is seen; when standing, no standing is seen.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, he does not rely upon a single thing. He sees neither giver nor receiver, nor is there any object given.
Such a view is precisely that of one with overweening pride; it will surely cause you to fall into hell.
When none of this is the case, how is it? "The assembly, return to the hall for tea."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Zen Master Dayu Zhi. One day, he asked his attendant, "After you have finished your inquiry, you stand to one side.
What is the principle behind that? The attendant replied, "I do not understand. Dayu said, "Stand over here. The attendant then moved over. Dayu said, "Pointless, pointless!
The Master remarked, "Those who help others achieve realization are few; those who ruin them are many."
Small *sǎn* (sermon) on the commencement of the summer retreat. A monk asked, "One may either gaze at mountains and play by the water, or seek the Way and search for a teacher.

Apart from these two paths, I ask the Master for instruction. The Master said, "Why do you run about so restlessly? The monk stepped forward and said, "I fear, Master, that I am not sincere. The Master said, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated.
The monk stepped forward and said, "The Han land does not claim him, and Qin does not take charge; last night the bright moon ascended the high peak. The Master— [remained silent].
The student said, “It does not attach. The student asked, “When the fifteenth day of the fourth month is reached for the binding, for whom is it bound?
The Master said, “A mangy horse tied to a withered post. The student asked, “On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when it is released, how is it released?
The Master said, “Bodhidharma has arrived. The student asked, “Is there anyone who is not included within this? The Master said, “A net that covers the heavens—hundreds [of eyes].”
[The monk] asked, "A thousand layers [of barriers]. He continued, "Originally there is no obstruction; wherever one is, it accommodates both square and round.
The Master said, "I let this one pass. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "There may be a sandalwood grove surrounded by sandalwood;
there may be a thornbush grove surrounded by thornbushes; there may be a thornbush grove surrounded by sandalwood; or there may be a sandalwood [grove...]"
A thicket surrounded by brambles. You people, carrying staffs across your shoulders and wearing tightly laced straw sandals, go here and there, east and west.

In which kind of thicket do you dwell? If it is a sandalwood thicket, then you are a golden-maned lion, capable of both yielding and seizing, capable of both killing and bringing to life. If it is a thicket of brambles, then you are...
Foxes, wolves, and jackals cannot bestow [life], nor can they take it away; they cannot kill, nor can they bring to life.

Following their packs and herds, fearing death and craving life, even if they were to slaughter tens of millions, what sin or transgression would there be? Consider, for instance, two kinds of forests.
When they surround one another, what is called a golden-haired lion is also a fox, a wolf, and a jackal;
what is called a fox, a wolf, and a jackal is also a golden-haired lion. Ultimately, what should it be called? Can it let go, or cannot it let go?
That which can be taken away cannot be taken away; that which can be killed cannot be killed; that which can be brought to life cannot be brought to life. How, then, can there be certainty?

If you are certain to attain liberation, I grant you the freedom to roam at will throughout the world. If you are certain not to attain it, for ninety days there will be no hope of release, and for a hundred kalpas you shall endure the suffering of sinking into the depths.
Again, he raised the case where a monk asked Zhaozhou, "What is the man-eating lion? Zhaozhou said, "Take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha;
do not bite the old monk. The Master said, "This monk was merely a dung-eating dog. Why?
Because as soon as Zhaozhou saw him, he immediately discharged his excrement and urine, charging headlong toward the den of the beast."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "By day he ascends Tuṣita; by night he descends Jambudvīpa. Why, then, does the maṇi jewel not appear? The Master replied, "It appears! It appears!
He then suddenly took up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said, "It is all shattered to pieces!
What is it that you all come here seeking? He threw down the staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have spoken with you in the long corridors; I have spoken with you by the rear eaves.
Yet, upon this Dharma Hall, I do not speak with you. Why? Because I do not speak; I do not speak."

When a donor provides a vegetarian feast and ascends the hall, the merit of making offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas does not equal that of making offerings to a single mindless man of the Way.
What fault do the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas have? What virtue does the mindless man of the Way possess?
If you understand the meaning within this, you will find an ox’s head placed upon its tail.
Small Assembly for the End of the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "What is it like when one is right here and now? The Master said, "Zha!

The monk stepped forward and said, "From the highest heights, looking down, there is nothing more; from the lowest depths, leveling out, there is always more. The Master said, "This is the talk of those who merely parrot words. The monk stepped forward and said—
"The ninety days of this summer retreat are now complete. I pray that the Master will employ skillful means to point out the ford for those lost.
The Master said, "My mouth is fit only for eating rice. The student pressed on, saying, "If someone were to suddenly ask you about your recent activities, what would you say to him?
The Master said, "The mandate from the Western Heavens is strict. The student said, "The Master’s three-inch tongue is too tight. The Master said, "..."
"Red clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun circles Mount Sumeru. The monk further said, "A single phrase has already traversed the entire world.
The Master said, "That too is groundless. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "To stumble on level ground is no small matter;
to miss it at one's own feet brings laughter to the bystanders. 'This very mind is Buddha,' 'Neither mind nor Buddha'—this..."
There is not even two taels of gold upon the earth; a layman sells three sheng of wine. Furthermore, there are those who are utterly incompetent:

sighing and brooding many times before the wind and under the moon, wandering aimlessly from the ends of the earth throughout their entire lives. In the Western Heaven, a wax figure is used as a test.
"In my place here, I use a bamboo staff as a test. To call it a 'bamboo staff' is to encounter resistance;

not to call it a 'bamboo staff' is to turn one's back. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! If you hesitate even for a moment, I shall strike you across the spine with the staff. He further cited Changqing, who said:
"It has been thoroughly swept clean. Yet you come forward to seek me. I shall give you a blow across the spine. There is indeed such a blow."
"It reaches you. You must feel shame and remorse. Not a single blow reached you; where, then, did you understand it?
Xuedou said, "Xuedou does not think so. It has been thoroughly cleansed and settled. You must come forward;
I will strike you across the spine with a blow. If a blow reached you, you would be wronged; if no blow reached you, I give it to you."
"Level and emerge. But understand it just like this. The Master said: "Among the assembly, they deliberate, saying: 'If you sit upon a clean ground, you must clear it away.
If you step forward to seek it, you are destined to receive a blow. What you seek is the sickness; the blow is the medicine. Therefore, Xuedou said:
'If there is one blow that reaches you, you will be wronged; if not a single blow reaches you, [it is given] to you.'"

Píngchū and Dùzuàn were Chan practitioners who were as numerous as hemp and millet. Little did they know that one of these two elders was digging a pit in the ground while the other was leveling a well and blocking a stove;
both intended to bring about a state of Great Peace through their own efforts, yet alas, they instead invited ridicule.
Vipaśyin Buddha set his mind on this long ago, yet until this very day he has not attained the wondrous.
Recorded by Wumeng as he ascended the hall for formal instruction: He cites Master Baiyun Yuan, who said, "Even if one were to write upon a thousand sheets of paper..."
It is merely a weariness of mind and hand; human sentiment is like Mount Taihua—how can it compare to the loftiness of the Way-sentiment?

The Master said, "Great and small Baiyun, you still have this remaining. When Yongzuo received a visit from his elder brother Wumeng, they shared coarse tea and plain talk, sitting upright and forgetting all concerns.
If there were even a single trace of a conceptual word, neither would find favor. Why is this? Because when people are level, they do not...
The words: "The water level does not flow.
Entering the hall, he said: "Huangbo’s staff in hand digs flesh to create sores; Dayu’s fist under the ribs uses salt to quench thirst."

If it is done quickly, it is easy to correct; if it has lasted long, it is difficult to remedy. If one who selects a Buddha lacks such an eye, what would even a thousand years accomplish? *He lets out a shout.*

Ascending the hall to preach on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra: East, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below—in every atom and in every world-system, there is nothing that does not depart from this Flower Treasury World-Ocean. There are heights and depths, breadth and narrowness, completeness and incompleteness.
There are those who are equal and those who are unequal; there are those who are pure and those who are impure;
there are those with short lifespans and those with long years. Now tell me: in which world-realm does the Tathāgata Vairocana currently reside and preach the Dharma?

Furthermore, what Dharma does he preach? Does he preach the Dharma of the Three Vehicles? Does he preach the Dharma of the One Vehicle? Does he preach the Dharma of the Unsurpassed Vehicle? Or is it...?

Try to explain what has been said. If you can explain it, I will grant that you shall purify Buddha-lands and sport with spiritual powers, such that sentient and insentient beings alike realize and enter [enlightenment] together.
If you cannot explain it, you shall continue to sink and float within the sea of birth and death.
At Huidiyan, Yuxiu requested the Master to ascend the seat. A monk asked, "The precious jewel of intention is inexhaustible;
responding to things and meeting conditions, it never grudges. What is this precious jewel of intention? The Master said, "How many people are unable to use it?
The monk pressed further, "Is it not simply this very thing? The Master said, "Try using it and see. The monk replied, "Gathering water, the moon is in my hand; playing with flowers..."

The fragrance filled his robes. The Master said, "Your words have slipped. The monk stepped forward and asked, "This morning, the donor, Inspector Dunyan, has made preparations to pre-arrange a 'deposited treasury' and invited the Venerable One to ascend the seat. How do you express the single phrase for dedicating this merit?
The Master said, "A snap of the fingers completes the eighty thousand gates; in one leap, one enters directly the stage of the Tathāgata. He then said, "The root of sentient beings relies upon..."
The ocean of wisdom is its source. The stream of all sentient beings takes the Dharmakāya as its essence.
O virtuous ones, do you recognize this source? If you recognize this source, then a thousand sources and ten thousand sources are but a single source. Do you perceive this essence?
If you perceive this essence, then a thousand essences and ten thousand essences are one and the same essence. Above, they are sages; below, they are...
As for ordinary beings: among the sages—namely the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas—they realize liberation through exclusively pure application.
As for ordinary beings—namely devas, humans, asuras, and those in the three evil realms—they fall into saṃsāra through exclusively defiled application.
To emerge from saṃsāra and fully achieve liberation is like a person who falls because of the ground and rises because of the ground.
Setting aside the vases, platters, hairpins, and bracelets, the true gold does not come from without. Within the cream, curd, and clarified butter, all exquisite flavors emerge from within.

Extending to the heavens and earth, the sun, moon, and stars, the plants, trees, insects, and the myriad phenomena of the universe—there is nothing that does not radiate brilliance through time and space.
Transcending all seeing and hearing, one must pass through the single diamond circle and swallow the single chestnut.
The "thorny burr" cannot be described. If one can swallow and penetrate the Vajra Circle and the thorny burr all at once, is this not the mark of one who has brought matters to completion?
Listen further to a verse: Within a single mote of dust lies a great treasure-trove, Filling the entirety of the void of the ten directions.
It universally radiates light that illuminates every atom and land; Those touched by this light have their afflictions removed. Because afflictions are removed...
The Way of Awakening is perfected; one is able to perform the Buddha-work for all living beings. Merit, virtue, and lifespan are all increased.

This wondrous liberation was realized by Dushan (Dull Rock); unmoving from the fundamental limit, it is eternally tranquil. Reaching to the furthest reaches of the future, this path shall be proclaimed.

While presiding over the consecration of a statue of Mahākāruṇika, the Master ascended the hall. A lay practitioner came forward and asked, "Is it true that the Bodhisattva Mahākāruṇika has hands and eyes throughout his entire body?
The Master said, "Yes. The practitioner continued, "Does the disciple also possess them? The Master said, "Yes.
The practitioner further asked, "But when, in the middle of the night, one sees not a single thing, where are the hands and eyes? The Master said, "They are simply pervasive."
[The Master] looked at him with his eyes. Jin said, "I thank the Master for this instruction. The Master sighed, "Heh heh," and then said:

"According to what is taught in the scriptures, the deluded perceptions of sentient beings do not depart from the sensory objects before them. When you open your eyes and see light, that light is not truly light; when you close your eyes and see darkness, that darkness is not truly darkness.
If you pass in front of the Buddha Hall, you do not see what is behind the Buddha Hall; if you pass behind the Buddha Hall..."
Seeing the events before the Buddha Hall, one realizes they all belong to deluded perceptions obstructed by external objects. If separated from these external objects, there is nothing to be seen.
According to Yongzuo’s perspective, the Great Compassionate Bodhisattva is fundamentally without a body and likewise without hands or eyes.
When someone says, "I understand! I understand!", he strikes him twenty-nine blows and drives him out, keeping one blow for himself.
"Is there anyone who can let go? If not, today we shall suffer defeat. Mazu raised the case of Magu asking Linji:
"The Great Compassionate One has a thousand hands and eyes; which one is the True Eye? Linji replied, "The Great Compassionate One has a thousand hands and eyes;
which one is the True Eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Magu dragged Linji down from his meditation seat and sat back down himself. Linji said, "I do not know you."

on the eighteenth day of the eighth month, the tide is even more direct. Whether heard or not heard, whether glimpsed or not glimpsed—Gazhou’s Great Elephant eats thorns; the Iron Ox of Shanfu bleeds.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "As for the two words 'Buddha-dharma,' do not touch upon them; if you touch upon them, they become unfit.
Here, dragons and snakes are intermingled, and ordinary people and sages dwell together. If you give rise to a mind of 'nothingness,' you will be beaten with a staff and driven out of the monastery.
Gold does not trade with gold; water does not wash water. How shall one speak this single phrase? Why do you act so foolishly?"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Upon the crown of the heads of the thousand sages, a single touch and you know; before the myriad phenomena of the forest and the heavens, they suddenly emerge and are difficult to discern.
From antiquity to the present, there is no seam or fissure; covering heaven and earth, it is beyond all nets and cages. You cannot pull it back; you cannot push it away.
You cannot crowd it together; you cannot disperse it by stirring it. It is such that the autumn light is deep and clear, its essence revealed in the golden wind."
The night sky is clear and serene; coolness arises within the jade palace. On the high branches dwell many birds; amidst the decaying grasses abound the fireflies.
To perceive the nature of the Buddhas as perfect and eternal through the deluded mind of sentient beings—to speak in such a manner would make even the monks laugh to death.
"What ultimate excellence does a patch-robed monk possess?
[The Master] lets out a shout. Small Assembly Sermon on the Winter Solstice. A monk asked: "Worldly affairs are wearying; it is not as good as dwelling on a mountain ridge.
Lying beneath the wisteria vines with a block of stone for a pillow—how does this differ from one who 'extends his hand' to enter the marketplace? The Master said: "Not by much."
The student said, "There is no distinction between the monastic and the lay. The Master said, "A pair of unperforated iron hammers; among them, one is the heaviest.
The student said, "If that is so, then all the old monks of the world are contained within this. The Master said, "By whom was this established?
The student said, "A few sounds of the clear chime lie beyond right and wrong; a single idle man dwells amidst heaven and earth. The Master said, "Just so."
As soon as he had rolled the pellets, he was about to grasp the *vajra*. The student asked, "Tomorrow is the festival of 'Writing Clouds' (*shuyun*);
what kind of cloud will you ultimately write? The Master said, "What kind of cloud is it over there? The student replied, "I only wish that next year the silkworms and wheat may ripen."
He gave one coin to Rāhula’s son. The Master said, "In a single day, his head turns white. He then said: "Lowering a hook ten thousand li long, he halts a black steed from a thousand li away;
spreading a net that covers the heavens, he strikes the glistening scales leaping through the waves. This is like what the Great Power Demon King says.
"I shall wait until all sentient beings have attained Buddhahood and the realm of sentient beings is emptied, such that even the name 'sentient being' no longer exists;
only then will I resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The butcher Guang'e cast down his butcher's knife and said, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas. He was already quite incompetent, yet he sat further upon the long meditation benches. Long...
Lying together on the same bed, with eyes staring blankly like a sheep that cannot be killed; what benefit is there in ten thousand years of existence within a single thought?
It would be better to be like a mud-pig or a scabby dog, for they still have the prospect of liberation.

I tell you clearly: the opening [of the mouth] does not depend upon the tongue. If you wish for an urgent resonance, tomorrow is the "Cloud-Recording" day (the winter solstice). Again, he cites Longji:
The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are nothing but the awakening to one’s nature. Originally, there is no person who is deluded or enlightened;
it simply requires realization today. The Master said: "If there is neither delusion nor enlightenment, what is there to realize? No one has recognized the merit of past labor on the battlefield;
one must re-examine the achievements that cover the age."
Ascending the hall: Above is heaven, below is earth; hearing sounds with the ears, breathing through the nose.

Setting aside for a moment the question of how the Iron Ox of Shanfu swallows the Great Image of Jiazhou—when he drags the Kingdom of Campā and the Kingdom of Silla together to clash their foreheads, what rank does this belong among the [awakened] mechanisms?
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and called to the assembly, saying: "I strike the staff here;
you hear the sound there. Do you hear it with your ears, or do you hear it with your mind? If you hear it with your ears—your ears are but two pieces of skin—how can they hear?
If you hear it with your mind—the mind is like a skilled actor, and the intellect is like the stage manager—then how [can the mind hear]?"
"Shengwen (Hearing Birth). One never hears within empty space. If one were to hear within empty space, it would be constant hearing;
why then wait until one plants a staff here before hearing? Fengshan does not plant a staff—why, then, does he not hear? Have you not seen how Mañjuśrī said:
"When sound is non-existent, it is not that sound has ceased; when it exists, it is not that it has arisen. Thus, both arising and ceasing are [empty].
Perfectly detached—this is the eternal reality. Yet, by retreating from the subsequent words, one merely adds legs to a snake;
to let go of everything with total abandon and to be free of any support, turning toward that side and even beyond it, is still not the time of arriving home.
As for the single phrase of "arriving home," how would you say it? "One only knows that affairs pass before one's eyes, unaware that old age has crept upon one's head."
Ascending the hall, he said: "If there is an old monk, there is no disciple; if there is a disciple, there is no old monk.
The disciple is simply the disciple, and the old monk is simply the old monk. One may call him 'disciple,' and one may also call him 'old monk.'"
Suddenly picking up his staff, he struck it once and let out a shout. He ascended the hall and said:

"In the moonlight of the thatched hall, the wind sighs through the bamboo doors. It is a time when the ice is frozen solid and the snow is withered; a night when the drum is silent and the bell has sunk.
When every thought is eternally stilled, the stone woman cuts the hair of a tortoise. When every moment pursues conditions, the wooden man carves..."
The horns of a rabbit are neither the Five Ranks of Dongshan nor the Three Mysteries of Linji. In the place where teeth and gums clash, not a single character exists.
Prior to the birth of one's parents, the total capacity is uniquely liberated; penetrating to the very top and bottom, it extends through all antiquity and into the present.
"Rice is made from grain. How would you say it in a single phrase? [The assembly] stood for a long time.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire realm is the whole body; there is not a single place that is not so, nor a single thought that is not so.
Suddenly, picking up his staff, he asked them: "Is this it or not? At that moment, among a thousand people, nine hundred and ninety-nine...
Nineteen mouths, each like a flat carrying pole. You must personally put an end to the thieving mind; only then will you believe that everything prior was not it.
That "not it" is precisely this very thing. Jiliao’s tongue spans three thousand miles. *He lets out a shout.*
Ascending the hall, he saw a staff and did not call it a staff; he saw a house and did not call it a house. This is precisely being deluded and running outside the gate.
To see a staff and simply call it a staff, or to see a house and simply call it a house—this is merely copying a cat by following the model.
When two people arrive together in the mountains, he gives them both a cup of tea, wishing to distinguish the black from the white.
"Wait for another time.
The Buddha ascended the hall after attaining the Way. "The three thousandfold great chiliocosm—the sun, moon, and stars; mountains, rivers, and seas;
insects, plants, and trees; sentient and insentient beings—all turn toward this very place," he said, holding up his staff, striking it once, and adding, "and attain equal enlightenment."
Perfect Enlightenment. Then, regarding Fengshan’s refusal to enter this monastic community—why was that?
It is the meaning of what Shitou spoke. On the New Year’s Eve small *paramārtha* (informal sermon), a monk asked: "The sun rises in the east and the moon sets in the west;
what is the meaning of 'non-transmigration'? The Master said: "Willow catkins follow the wind, drifting from west to east. The monk pressed further: "Every year is a good year, every day..."
"This is an auspicious day. The Master said, "A blind old woman blowing on a fire. He then said: "When one has not yet realized that objects are but mind, various kinds of discrimination arise.
Once one has realized that objects are but mind, discrimination no longer arises. Within this state where nothing arises, the mundane and supramundane dharmas are fully present.
When one is established, all are established; when one is refuted, all are refuted; when one is released, all are released. One.

Gathering all that can be gathered, it is fully encompassed within its very essence. Revealed directly before one’s eyes, this is expediently called the eternally abiding Dharmakāya, from which flow forth boundless oceans of samādhis—the realm of great beings such as Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra, and the domain of Deshan and Linji.
Uplifting [all beings] toward the ultimate, may those in this world and other worlds together achieve the Buddha-way. Whether through speech or silence, may the Wheel of Dharma be turned everywhere.

May the three periods of time be unified as a single moment, and the ten directions be encompassed as a single realm. Thus, the twenty-four seasonal energies and seventy-two climatic signs are all brought into harmony.
Three hundred and sixty-five days are but a single *kṣaṇa*. To realize this is for one’s every thought to be perfectly luminous;
to be deluded by it is to sink forever into birth and death. Again, Master Baoning Yong addressed the assembly, saying: "The World-Honored One spoke what was unspeakable;
Kāśyapa heard what was unheard. He struck his staff on the ground and said: "Where do the flowing waters and yellow leaves come from? A cow passes by with crows perched upon its dewlap."
"Remote village. The Master said, "Qingzhou pears, Zhengzhou dates; generally speaking, there is nothing better than a good provenance.

On the first day of the year, he rose at midnight to go to the Provincial Hall to offer incense and prayers. Having finished the prayers, he attended to formal greetings with the various offices of the Chancellor’s residence.
Once the greetings were concluded, he returned immediately to the main hall to burn incense, scatter sand, recite incantations over the earth, and circumambulate the corridors.

The Way. The various mountains prepare their offerings and ceremonies to receive the officials in due order. If one holds a Buddhist assembly at the start of the New Year, one will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
Regarding the two classes of monks ascending the hall: the tiger and leopard’s patterns derive entirely from the power of their claws and fangs; the transformation of the Kun and Peng is likewise so.
The mind relies on the power of wings; the Dharma community depends on its people. Thus, the monastic groves naturally gain vitality.
Muzhou assisted Huangbo, and Yangqi supported Ciming; together they erected the banner of the Dharma and displayed the true core of the patch-robed monks.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: "All moons take the single moon as their reality; all lamps take the single lamp as their essence.
One is all, and all is one. From where does this 'one' arise? To even attempt to provide a commentary here would be a mistake."
When the various mountain lecturers ascend the hall, they first cite the Way of the Sages: "All dharmas are not born of themselves, nor are they born from another;
they are not born from both together, nor without cause. Therefore, it is said that they are unborn. The entire earth is a sesame cake;
you may bite it horizontally or vertically as you please. In the Nālandā Monastery of India, ten thousand monks or so all had their fill; there was only [the Master] Ma...
The great deity Haka-ra could not eat it; he struck Mount Sumeru with a single blow, shattering it into a hundred pieces, while Śakra leaped up and fled to the Brahma Heaven.
Ascending the hall, he said: "That the mind is Buddha—misfortune does not enter the door of a prudent household. That the mind is not Buddha—the tongue is the axe that fells one's own body.
What the ancients used, the people of today employ; what the people of today do, the ancients have already done. When one dog barks at the void, a thousand monkeys howl at the reality.
Today, Fengshan, disregarding his own life, shall for all of you pull out the nails and pry out the wedges."

Yecha. When the Buddha ascended the hall for his final teaching before entering *nirvāṇa*, there were bird tracks in the sky to the east, west, south, and north; there were fish traces in the water to the south, north, west, and east.
Although Gautama exhausted all the strength of his life, even until now he has not been able to return.
Hudutār, the Grand Champion (Zhuangyuan), ascended the hall and said: "Juyuan Haobuzun once visited the Layman Dongpo in humble attire.
Haobuzun asked, 'What is your honorable surname? Dongpo replied, 'My surname is Chéng; it is the scale by which all elders in the world are weighed.
Haobuzun spat on the ground and said, 'How much does this single spittle weigh? Dongpo then withdrew. The Master said, 'Juyuan...'"
Yuan was a master of the school; Dongpo was a great Confucian scholar of his time. Meeting suddenly and unexpectedly, they both brought forth this Way.
Everyone says that Dongpo gave up; it is as if there were no stars on the scale’s tail. Yet little do they realize that eight ounces and half a pound are both entirely in one's own hands.
Even so, one must still raise up Yuyuan. It is just like when he said this: [The text ends here.]
As for the weight of this spittle—how many people can say it? Even if you could say it, I would spit on you once more.
Ascending the hall: The scenery is bright and clear; the lakes and mountains are layered with emerald green. With the Cold Food Festival approaching, we together enjoy the fragrant blossoms.
Painted boats everywhere resound with songs and music; the flower markets are layered with brocade and embroidery. These elegant young gentlemen fully manifest the ancient Buddha’s family style.
A beauty of vermilion powder. To reveal the very nose of the patriarchs, I bid you break the staff and hang up the alms-bowl;
there is no need to bow the head, for it is difficult to find through mere deliberation.
Ascending the hall: Here, where the bell is struck and the drum beaten, where the mallet is raised and the whisk brandished, and where yellow and black are discussed—it is all for you all.
There, in the long streets and short alleys, where children are carried on the back and held in the arms, and where angry fists and foul abuse are exchanged—it is also all for you all.
Hell is not yet the true suffering; rather, to remain within this "line of the robe" without clarifying the Great Matter—that indeed is suffering. This...
At that time, if one does not investigate the root source, one must simply wait for the future to ask Maitreya.
During the ceremony of bathing the Buddha, a monk ascended the hall and asked the Great Being Huiming, "Before descending into the royal palace, where was the Old Man Śākyamuni?
The Master said, "Blinking your eyebrows. The monk followed up, saying, "Thank you for answering my question, Master. The Master said, "It happens to coincide with my staff."
"It is not here. The Master then took up his whisk and drew a circle, saying: "Among the thirty-two marks, there is no such mark;
among the eighty secondary characteristics, there is no such characteristic. Limping and shuffling, pass through the time; when people come, there is no need to seek it further."
[The Master] gave a shout.
This was the Small General Precept (Xiaosan) for the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "The entire earth is the Buddha-body; where does one dwell and observe the summer retreat?
The Master said, "A layer of flowers spread upon brocade. The monk pressed on, saying, "Though the bamboo is dense, it does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through the mountains."

"How could height obstruct the flight of white clouds? The Master said, "To produce understanding following the words. He then continued, "In the kingdom of Magadha, [the Buddha] personally carried out this command;
one must risk one's life to know it. Even if you let go with both hands from a precipice, you must be willing to accept it yourself."
To revive after being dead is to deceive the Sovereign; it is merely staring with eyes wide open from within a coffin.
Here in Fengshan, there are no such matters. Usually, we simply take ninety days as one summer retreat. We eat yellow and brown rice with bitter and beneficial vegetable soup.
Before Zunseng Temple, the green mountains stretch on endlessly; at the Westing Ferry, the white waves roll vast and boundless.

To the point. Whether walking, let you walk; whether sitting, let you sit; whether emerging, let you emerge; whether entering, let you enter. Unfolding and rolling up at will—why be constrained by this or that?
Yet, it is not permitted to be buried within the heap of sounds and forms, nor is it permitted to depart from those sounds and forms.
If it is not like this in any way, then how is it? A young lord in brocade robes is noble; beneath the forest trees...
The Wayman Gao. There is also a verse that says: "Set aside the 'water-walking on the eastern mountain,' And a fragrant breeze brings a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions.
To dwell in the mountains costs not the slightest effort; There is someone who naturally carries the broken-legged cauldron."

Ascending the hall, he said: "A single phrase that hits the mark is a tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas. A person of keen intelligence who hears it and acts immediately has already been eight *ke* late."
Dongshan Shouzhi went up to the hall for the formal lecture. He related the story of Quandai Daowu visiting Ciming.
Ciming said, "A single cloud hangs across the mouth of the valley; from where does the traveler come? Daowu said, "Last night, where was the fire?

It burned out the graves of the ancients. Ciming said, "Not yet—speak further! Daowu then let out a tiger’s roar. Ciming struck him with his meditation mat. Daowu pushed Ciming onto the meditation platform.
Having clarified this, he made a tiger’s roar. Quan said, "I have encountered more than eighty virtuous teachers (kalyāṇamitra), yet only you have succeeded in carrying on the Linji tradition.
The Master said, "You have wrongly applied these names and phrases. At that time, Ciming would never have tolerated such a madman speaking thus;
he would have given him another blow from his sitting cloth. Just watch what kind of trickery he will perform! As soon as [Quan] opened his eyes—
His eyes fixed and his movements steady, he immediately chased him out with his staff. The Dharma-lineage of Linji has not yet fallen into desolation. Ascending the hall, [he said]:
"The bustling marketplace of red dust is the style of a noble youth; the vast wilderness and deep mountains are the livelihood of a practitioner of the Way.
One wanders through flowers and passes by willows; the other sighs at the moon and sleeps amidst the clouds. Which one gains and which one loses? The clouds are at the crest of the ridge."
"Not at leisure; the water flowing in the bottom of the ravine is too busy.
He ascended the hall and said: "Not falling into cause and effect, yet not being oblivious to cause and effect—neither of these has yet shed the body of a wild fox.
If you wish to shed the body of a wild fox, you must wait five hundred more lifetimes before it can be achieved. He called to the assembly, saying: "Do you all agree with Fengshan speaking thus?"
"The people of the entire earth do not accept it; they are all of the wild fox lineage. (He lets out a shout.

Ascending the hall in Central China, he said: "Monks, do not engage in deluded thinking. To give rise to thoughts and stir the mind is deluded thinking. To clarify the mind and still the thoughts is deluded thinking.
To become a Buddha or an Ancestor is deluded thinking. People often use one deluded thought to extinguish another deluded thought—there is no [end to this]."

There is a time limit. Even if you were to suddenly comprehend all the teachings of the past and present as clearly as a pearl rolling across a tray, I dare guarantee that such a person has not yet escaped the realm of the five aggregates (*pañcaskandha*).
Who can eliminate this "obstructing mass" within the breast? If it could be eliminated, that would be called liberation;
yet in reality, one has not attained total liberation. A true great man must transcend Vairocana and surpass Śākyamuni. This is what he ought to do.
Having reached such a state, why do you point to your chests and ribs, citing Yang and Zheng?
I have never, even in the sixth month, let fall a great snowstorm upon you all.
Ascending the hall: the bell is struck and the bell rings; the drum is beaten and the drum resounds. The Buddhas of the three periods vie with one another to show their heads;
the Patriarchs of the six generations have no place to hide their bodies. Within the bell there is no sound of the drum; within the drum there is no sound of the bell.
Bell and drum do not intersect; every phrase is without before or after. Ultimately, what does one call a "phrase"? He lets out a shout.

The donor watched as the Master ascended the hall for the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* discourse. He realized the wondrousness of the principle; with constant, clear awareness, he maintained a single state of equanimity, steady and without leakage.
Putting on clothes and eating food were merely his daily routine; seeing forms and hearing sounds was like being deaf and blind.
Thus, he could enter the realm of the Buddhas but not that of the Māras. Having penetrated the ten gates of Chan and emerged from the domain of the five aggregates, he dwelt therein.
Every place is nothing other than the work of the Buddha; every single thing is entirely a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
In wine shops and brothels, there is no obstruction whatsoever; through dragon palaces and tiger dens, one may pass at will. One may enter the realm of demons, and one may enter the realm of Buddhas;

thereafter, both Buddhas and demons are cast aside, and ordinary beings and sages cease to exist. One neither grasps at *nirvāṇa* nor dwells in birth-and-death. To say, "My great matter is finished," is to rely upon [the Way].
The staff was not there; he gave the broom handle thirty blows.
Ascending the hall, he said: "As soon as there is right and wrong, one becomes confused and loses one's mind. Do you still recognize the face of the Patriarch?"
Entering the new Sangha Hall for the formal address on the platform, [the Master] raised the case of Attendant Wang Changshi. One day, he visited Linji; they went together before the Sangha hall.
The Attendant asked, "Do the monks in this hall study the scriptures? Linji said, "They do not study the scriptures. The Attendant asked, "Do they practice seated meditation?
Linji said, "They do not practice seated meditation. The Attendant asked, "Since they neither study the scriptures nor practice seated meditation, what exactly are they doing?"
"What? Linji said. "I am simply teaching him to become a Buddha and a Patriarch. Wang the Attendant said, "Though gold dust is precious, if it falls into the eye, it becomes a cataract.
Linji said, "I took you for a mere worldly fellow. The Master said: "Where has Linji’s 'Blow-off Sword' gone?
If it were brought forth, what need would there be for Wang the Attendant? Since emerging from the cave, there has been none."
Regarding the adversary: where you can show leniency toward others, show them leniency.

On the occasion of a vegetarian feast, a *arhat* ascended the hall. Wind stirs in the ancient hall; the moon turns across the winding corridor. Fragrant smoke swirls in every direction; lamps and candles shine brightly.
Venerable Piṇḍola-bharadvāja, who partakes of offerings throughout the four worlds, has been nowhere he has not reached—has he now come here as well?

[The Master] asks, "What is this place? [The monk] replies, "It is a place where speech reaches what cannot be reached. He joins his palms and says, "The three virtues and six flavors are offered to the Buddha and the Sangha," and then descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "On Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, positions were filled according to one's capacity; on the path of Caoqi, substance was scarce while emptiness abounded.
Without regard for ordinary beings of shallow ground, you are immediately invited to stride alone through the crimson heavens. How fast! How fast! Is there anyone? Is there anyone?
Even if one attempts to emulate the phoenix, even the rabbit will not meet him."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "How wonderful, O virtuous Chan practitioners! Peach blossoms red, pear blossoms white; waters green, mountains blue. Amidst misty rain, pavilions and towers; in the marketplace, carts and horses.
Clouds unfolding and clouds rolling up, revealing several peaks and ridges. Boats departing and boats arriving, startling a flight of gulls and egrets.
By the bridge, the wine shop; beyond the willows, the houses. Behold them closely: they are clearly depicted. They are depicted!"
"It is not non-existent. How can one apply the brush? 'The lotus leaf moves though there is no wind; there must be a fish swimming beneath. Entering the hall, he said:
"The *pobing* cake is burnt—cut off all news. Beneath the flowers, the spring birds sing clearly: 'It is better to go back, it is better to go back.
From this point on, if you do not go back, you will surely attain it when you do. He let out a shout."
When the patron Songlin and the laywoman Miaolian of the Xiang family offered a precious canopy and ascended the hall, the Master accepted the offering with a mind of intentionality;
Vimalakīrti had long ago rebuked such an act. To have a dharma that can be preached is not permitted by the Tathāgata.

Only when one reaches the point where there is no object to be given and no dharma to be preached does one truly encompass Buddhas and patriarchs and nurture both sages and ordinary beings—yet even this is but half a jewel, not yet the complete treasure. Upon reaching this state...
Within this state, it is as bright as the blazing sun and as vast as the great void. A thousand sages cannot carry it away; ten thousand functions are stilled and eliminated.

It is thus in every atom and every world-system; it is thus in every thought-moment and every dharma. Taking all the lands within the dust motes of the ten directions at once, they are placed upon the point of a needle.
Yet from that very point of the needle, there flows forth the cloud of light of all-encompassing wisdom. At this—
Within those clouds, there appeared wondrous lotus flowers, equal in measure to the lands of the atoms of the ten directions, which merged into a single canopy.
From within it emerged hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, who with one voice and in unison spoke these verses: "In a single thought, universally observe immeasurable eons;
There is no going, no coming, and no abiding. Thus understanding the matters of the three periods of time, One transcends all skillful means and achieves the Ten Powers."
Having spoken this verse, he immediately entered into the eye of a needle. He ascended the hall and said:

"The mind of the Tathāgata’s nirvāṇa, the patriarchs’ true Dharma-eye, the extraordinary matter of the patch-robed monks, and the gate of liberation for those who know—these are all nothing but tattered straw sandals cast away upon the streets of the ten directions, now thrown into the Qiantang River. With that, he returned to the hall.
Small General Assembly for the End of the Summer Retreat. A monk asked, "What is 'first illumination, then function'? The Master said, "Splitting open Mount Taihua so it reaches the color of the sky;
releasing the Yellow River until its sound reaches the sea. The monk further asked, "What is 'first function, then illumination'? The Master said:
"The sword leaves its precious sheath because it is not at peace; the medicine comes forth from the golden jar to save the sick.
The student asked, "What is 'illumination and function occurring simultaneously'? The Master said, "Dingguang beckons from afar from Jindi; Zhiyi nods his head in secret at Jinling.

The student asked, "What is 'illumination and function not occurring simultaneously'? The Master said, "For three months, I am too weary to wander the paths beneath the flowers; my entire household..."
Sighing, he closed the door in the rain. A monk prostrated himself. The Master said, "Would it not be wonderful if you asked one more turn? The monk then withdrew.
The Master then said, "The style of the Linji school requires that you must discern the master. If you do not discern the master, having eyes is like being blind.

Therefore it is said: 'It allows no room for deliberation; only by cutting through the entire body does one attain it. This is called the Master of Masters. It is the numinous blade, the precious sword."
It is constantly manifest before you; it is like being on the verge of meeting a sharp blade, with corpses strewn for ten thousand *li*.

All of you who carry staffs and travel as pilgrims—have you ever yet discerned the Master? If you can discern him, then upon seeing that old fellow on the meditation seat, as soon as he opens his mouth and moves his tongue, you turn your back on the Dharma Hall and put on your straw sandals and depart. Only then will you have a bit of the true scent of a *śramaṇa*. But...

In such a state of softness and frailty, you are like one without bone. When you hear others speak of existence, you cling to existence; when you hear them speak of non-existence, you cling to non-existence.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, you lack any sense of mastery. With what will you confront birth and death? How will you digest the offerings of the faithful?
To bury yourself and bring disgrace upon the ancestral school—none surpasses such a person as this. Hardly has the summer retreat begun, and already we see...
The summer retreat ends. Day after day, year after year, we wait for Old Man Yan to come collect our meal money;
why do we not turn back early to reflect carefully and see what the underlying principle is? The skull constantly contains the myriad worlds; the nostrils are the family style of direct touch.
The divine light from ten thousand miles is the mark behind the crown. If you can realize this right now, you will transform the mundane.
To achieve sainthood takes but a moment. If this is not yet so, you will end up changing hands and beating your breast.

Again, it is said that an outsider asked the World-Honored One, "What Dharma did you preach yesterday? The Honored One replied, "I preached the Dharma of certainty. The outsider asked, "What Dharma do you preach today?
The Honored One replied, "I preach the Dharma of uncertainty. The outsider asked, "For what reason? Why was it certain yesterday and uncertain today?"
The Master said, "Yesterday was fixed; today is not fixed. The Teacher offered this verse: Having traveled dozens of stages throughout Jiangnan, At dawn, with wind and waning moon, I entered Huaping.
Upon the Chaoyuan Pavilion, the western wind is fierce; It all enters the Longyang grove as the sound of rain.
Upon returning to the temple after the interment of the late Master Jizhao at Mount Jing, he ascended the hall and said:
