(Shǔ guǐ qiè) [Shī] (Dīng mù qiè) Chān (Shì xián qiè) Dì (Dū jì qiè) Shí (Lín zhí qiè) Sù (Sè qiú qiè) Biǎn (Bēi jiǎn qiè) [Kǒu * Fó] (Fó yīn) [Kǒu * Hòu] (Hū gòu qiè) Wù (Gǔ wù qiè) [Kǒu * Lǜ] (Lì shù qiè) Huò (Xǔ huó qiè) Kān (Kǔ hán qiè).
*The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fúrì Pǔzhào Huìbiàn Chǔshí, Volume Eleven*.
Citing the Past;
Compiled by Attendant Mingyuan and Others.
Regarding Baizhang’s second visit to Mazu: While standing in attendance, Mazu held up his whisk. Baizhang said, "This very thing is its function."
"Is it apart from this function? Baizhang hung his whisk back in its original place. After a long silence, he said, "When you open your mouth in the future, with what will you save people?
Baizhang took the whisk and held it upright. Baizhang said, "Is it this function, or apart from this function?
Baizhang then hung the whisk back in its original place. Baizhang gave a shout. Later, when Huangbo arrived at Baizhang’s monastery, one day he took his leave, wishing to pay his respects.
Baizhang went to pay his respects to Mazu. Baizhang said, "Mazu has already passed away. Huangbo asked, "I do not know what words or phrases Mazu had.
Baizhang then recounted the circumstances of his second visit, saying, "At that time, I was struck by Mazu’s single shout;
it left my ears deaf for three days. Upon hearing this account, Huangbo involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Baizhang said, "In the future, you must not fail to uphold [this teaching]."
"Does he succeed Mazu? Huangbo replied, "Not so. It is only because you have brought this up today that I am able to see the great function of Mazu’s dynamic power.
Furthermore, I do not recognize Mazu. If he were to succeed Mazu, his descendants would later lose their own selves. Miaoxi said:
"When Baizhang was struck by the shout, his ears were deaf for three days straight; when Huangbo heard it mentioned, he involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Baizhang had doubts."
He was the successor of Mazu. Later, because Linji asked three times about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, he was struck sixty blows each time.
This left him with three days' worth of deafness to vent his frustration; it was only then that Linji realized [the teaching] was like being brushed with a stalk of mugwort.
"I venture to ask the great assembly: since there is a clear basis for these lineages of masters, why is it that their applications differ?
Do you understand? 'The waves at Caoxi are just like those elsewhere; countless ordinary people are submerged. The Master said: Baizhang raised his whisk; Mazu gave a shout;
Huangbo heard this mentioned and involuntarily stuck out his tongue. The Linji school flourished, yet the True Dharma Eye was extinguished. Father!"
"The sons did not transmit it. Regarding these secret instructions of the immortals, how can it be that the descendants of later generations all call a tortoise a soft-shelled turtle?
He then gave a shout.
He cited an ancient case: there was once an old woman who provided the funds to invite Master Zhaozhou to recite the Great Canon. Zhaozhou went down...

He circumambulated the meditation seat once and said, "The turning of the Tripitaka is now complete. When the attendant returned and reported this to the old woman, she said, "I have been requesting the turning of one entire collection;
why has the Master turned only half? Miaoxi said, "There was discussion among the assembly regarding this."
What is that "half-treasury"? Some say it is to circumambulate once more; some say it is a snap of the fingers; some say it is a single cough;
some say it is a shout; and some say it is a clap. To have such an understanding is simply to be shameless.

If one were truly that "half-treasury," let alone Zhaozhou circumambulating once more—even if one were to circumambulate hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, millions, or billions of times—[it would still not suffice].

In the portion belonging to the old woman, she can only obtain half of the Tripitaka. Even if she were to circumambulate Mount Sumeru a hundred thousand million times, in her portion she would still only obtain half of the Tripitaka.

Even if all the old monks in the world were likewise to circumambulate it a hundred thousand million times, in their portions they too would only obtain half of the Tripitaka. Even if the mountains and rivers...
The great earth, the myriad phenomena of the universe—whether grasses or trees—all possess the mark of the broad and long tongue.
With one voice and many mouths, from this day until the end of the future, even regarding the old woman’s portion, they can only attain half of the Tripitaka.
Do you wish to recognize the old woman? After a long silence, he said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold; I do not hold back the golden needle."
Dudu gave it to another person. The Master said: "This old woman claims that Zhaozhou only turned the *Banzang* (Half-Canon). She is merely playing with a false image as if it were real.
At that time, he should have simply said: 'Why do you not realize it before you have even circumambulated the meditation seat?'"
The World-Honored One, leading the assembly of noble ones, proceeded to the Sixth Heaven to preach the Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra.

He commanded all malevolent spirits and ghosts—whether from other lands or this realm, whether among humans or in the heavens—to assemble at once. They were all to receive the Buddha’s entrustment to protect and uphold the True Dharma.
Should any fail to attend, the Gate-Keeper Kings of the Four Quarters shall fly fiery iron wheels to pursue them and compel their arrival. Once they have gathered...
The assembly having gathered, there was none who did not comply with the Buddha’s command; each made a great vow to protect and uphold the True Dharma.

Only one Māra King addressed the World-Honored One, saying: "Gautama, I shall wait until all sentient beings have attained Buddhahood, until the realm of sentient beings is emptied and the very name 'sentient being' no longer exists;
only then will I resolve to attain Bodhicitta. Jianfu Huai remarked: "This is like facing the brink of peril..."
Unchanging. A true great man. O virtuous ones, how can you utter a single turning word to give vent to the indignation of the Yellow-Faced Old Man?
His ordinary spiritual powers, wondrous functions, wisdom, and eloquence—none of these are of any use here.
Throughout the entire land of Jambudvīpa, there is no one who does not love the Buddha. When we arrive at this point, what is the Buddha and what is Māra?
Is there anyone who can discern between them? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish to recognize Māra, it is seeing light with eyes open.
If you wish to recognize the Buddha, it is seeing darkness with eyes closed. As for Māra and the Buddha, [the Master] pierced their noses all at once with his staff."
Kongming said, "Miaoxi says that the old fellow Tianyi’s critique is truly extraordinary. Nevertheless, it still fails to avoid splitting the discourse into two separate parts.
If one were to simply rest at the point where it asks, 'What is the Buddha? What is the demon?'—that would be it."
This is enough to leave people in a state of doubt. Yet he says: "If you wish to recognize Māra, it is seeing light with eyes open;

if you wish to recognize the Buddha, it is seeing darkness with eyes closed. This is quite a clumsy performance. He further says: "As for Māra and the Buddha, I shall pierce their nostrils through at once with my staff!
This is like adding frost to snow. Miaoxi, however, provides a substitute phrase on behalf of Śākyamuni: "Wait..."
This Mara King said, "The realm of sentient beings is empty; there is no such thing as the name 'sentient being. It was for this reason that I resolved to attain Bodhicitta.
[The Master] replied to him, "I nearly called you by the wrong name, 'Mara King. These words contain two points of defeat (*paryāya*).
If anyone can examine them thoroughly, I grant that they possess the eye of a Zen monk. The Master said: "A vast marsh hides mountains; a wildcat can subdue a leopard."
The two great elders said: "What need is there for many words? It suffices simply to say to the Mara King: 'Mara King, Mara King!

Which of these do you recognize as the bodhicitta? Do you even know it yet? Even if all sentient beings were to become Buddhas and the realm of sentient beings were emptied until no name for a sentient being remained—if you wished to ascend to the mind [of enlightenment] at such a time, you still would not be permitted. Take this to heart.
With hands folded in submission, he surrendered.
The Obstructing Demon King (Vighnāntaka-rāja), leading his entire retinue, followed the Bodhisattva Vajrasama for a thousand years, searching for the place of his arising without success.
Suddenly, one day, he beheld him and asked: "Upon what do you rely for your dwelling? I have [sought this] for a thousand..."
Nian said, "I cannot find the place where you arise. The Bodhisattva said, "I do not dwell by depending on dwelling; I dwell by depending on non-dwelling.
It is in this way that I dwell. Miaoxi said, "Since you cannot find the place where he arises, what is it that has followed him for a thousand years?
Jingang Qi said, "I do not dwell by depending on dwelling, nor do I dwell by depending on non-dwelling."

And they remain. Remaining thus, they mutually deceive one another. As for the Way of the Dharma-eye, let us set aside for a moment the fact that the Demon King Obstructing-View does not see the Vajra-Line.
But as for the Vajra-Line itself—does it see the Demon King Obstructing-View?
To pass judgment in such a manner is like looking through a hole and driving in a wedge. Is there anyone here now who knows where Miaoxi (Wondrous Joy) arises? He lets out a shout.
"What was that you were muttering in your sleep? The Master said, "Vajrabodhi said: 'I do not dwell by relying on dwelling, nor do I dwell by relying on non-dwelling;
I dwell in this manner. At that very moment, he was captured and defeated by the Demon King Māra. Nevertheless..."
One must also support the vajra-shoulder before one can succeed.
To cite the twenty-fourth patriarch, Venerable Siṃha: once, when the King of Kaśmīra held a sword before him, he said, "Have you attained the emptiness of the aggregates?
The Patriarch replied, "I have already attained the emptiness of the aggregates. The King asked, "Since you have attained the emptiness of the aggregates, have you transcended birth and death?"
The Patriarch said, "I have already departed from birth and death. The King said, "Since you have departed from birth and death, may I beg for your head?

The Patriarch said, "Even my body is not mine; how much more so my head? The King then struck off his head, whereupon white milk gushed forth several feet high, and the King's arm fell off of its own accord.
Miaoxi said, "Alas, Old Man Meng! He went about in such a manner. The Master said, "It is similar, indeed it is similar, but it is not so."
That is not yet correct.
Take the twenty-fifth patriarch, Praśāstrasena, as an example. Once, while debating with a non-Buddhist, the non-Buddhist said, "I request that you debate in silence, without resorting to words.
The patriarch replied, "If one does not resort to words, how can victory or defeat be known? The non-Buddhist said, "But..."
The Patriarch took up the meaning [of his words] and asked, "On what do you base this meaning? The non-Buddhist replied, "I take 'no-mind' (amanasikāra) as the meaning.
The Patriarch said, "Since you have no mind, how can you possess a meaning? The non-Buddhist replied, "When I speak of 'no-mind,' it is a designation, not a meaning. The Patriarch said:
"You say 'no-mind' (acitta), yet this should be called 'not meaning' (an-artha). I say 'not mind' (na-citta), yet this should be taken as the meaning (artha) rather than the name.

The non-Buddhist said, "If it is the meaning rather than the name, who is able to discern the meaning? The Patriarch said, "Your 'name' is not the meaning. What kind of name is this? The non-Buddhist said, [and remained silent].
To distinguish what is not the meaning, he said, "This is called namelessness. The Patriarch said, "Since the name is not a name, the meaning is also not a meaning.
Who is it that distinguishes? What is there to be distinguished? Thus they debated back and forth for fifty-nine rounds, until the non-Buddhist was silenced and submitted in faith.

Miaoxi said: "Vasishṭha, why do you need to be so distressed? At that time, had you seen him say, 'I request the Master to discuss this in silence,' rather than relying on words, you would have simply said, 'The meaning has already fallen. Is there anyone here now who can discuss with Miaoxi in silence?
Perhaps some monk might come forward and say, 'The meaning has already fallen. I also know where you are heading—toward the realm of ghosts."
"Making a living inside a cave. The Master said, "If I were the twenty-fifth patriarch, as soon as I saw a non-Buddhist enter the gate, I would strike him out with a staff.
Would that not be a man of stature? Yet he waited for the teacher to engage in silent debate, going back and forth fifty-nine times—how far removed from the truth!"
To cite the Sixth Patriarch, Master Huineng: A monk asked, "Regarding the meaning of the Yellow Plum [sutra], who is it that attains it?

The Patriarch said, "One who understands the Buddha-dharma attains it. The monk asked, "Does the Master yourself attain it? The Patriarch said, "I do not attain it. The monk asked, "Why does the Master not attain it?
The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma. Miaoxi said, "Do you see the Patriarch yet?"
“If you do not see it, I shall point it out to you, Jingshan: ‘Banyan tree, banyan tree; its leaves have long since vanished.

Suddenly a gust of wild wind arises, just like that in the wall-corner of the eastern corridor within the thirty-six courtyards of the Great Xiangguosi Temple in the Eastern Capital—Master Wang’s tattered cassock. After all, what is it? Return to the hall for tea. The Master said.
A staff strikes the head of a stone man; *bò bò*, he discusses the actual matter.
Regarding the phrase "placed beneath the ox-head," this refers to National Teacher Xuanting. Once, a monk asked him about the Fifth Patriarch’s statement: "True nature is dependent origination."

"What is the meaning of this? The Patriarch remained silent. At that time, as the attendant was in his turn of service, he said, "Virtuous One, at the very moment you give rise to the thought of asking the question, this is precisely dependent origination within the true nature. Upon these words, the monk attained great enlightenment.

Miaoxi said, "Even before the thought of asking the question has arisen, it cannot be that there is no dependent origination. At that time, another monk said, "Before the thought of asking the question has arisen, call out 'Shan'!"
[The Master] acted as the condition for this. Miaoxi said, "I also want you to speak in such a way. The Master said, "A Kunlun slave wearing iron trousers;
strike him with a staff and he takes a step forward."
To cite Chan Master Guoyi Qin of Mount Jing in Hangzhou: When Mazu sent a messenger with a letter, the letter contained a circle.
Upon opening the seal and seeing it, the Master placed a dot within the circle and returned it sealed.
Later, when National Teacher Zhong heard of this, he said, "Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma. Xuedou said, "Mount Jing was deluded."
Let us set that aside for a moment. If you were to present this to the National Teacher, what other skillful means could you employ to avoid being deluded?
An old master said, "At that time, he would have simply sat [in silence] and let it be. Others have also said, "Just draw a line through it. If you act in such a way, you are merely lacking in shame.
I dare say that all the teachers throughout the land possess the diamond eye; they should extensively manifest their spiritual powers.
"Transformation—can it still be avoided? Xuansu’s insight must also be known by all of you.
As for this Master Ma, at the very moment he drew [the circle], he was already deluded himself. Miaoxi said: "Master Ma faced the severe cold of mid-winter;
Guoyi encountered the gradual heat of early summer. Although the cold and heat differ, both did not miss their proper seasons. Because of this, National Teacher Zhong...
Xuefeng said, "Even Master Qin was still deluded by Master Ma. Do you understand this thoroughly? 'Without wind, the lotus leaf moves;
there must be a fish swimming beneath. The Master said, "If one places a drop of ink within a perfect circle, the sun and moon lose their light, and heaven and earth sink into darkness."
At first, you were not deluded; it was Master Qin who was deluded. Master Ma was deluded first, and his delusion subsequently reached Old Nanyang.
What a total mess! After a long silence: "Throughout my life, I have laid bare my liver and gall toward others; yet those I know are treated as if they were strangers."
To cite Chan Master Niaokuo: One day, his attendant Huītong was preparing to take his leave. The Master asked, "Where are you going now?
Huītong replied, "I have left home for the sake of the Dharma. Since the Master has not bestowed compassionate instruction upon me, I am now going to various places to study the Buddha-Dharma.
The Master said, "As for the Buddha-Dharma, we have a little here as well. Huītong asked, "What is it?"
The Master was asked this question regarding the Buddha-dharma by his *upādhyāya*. The Master plucked some cloth-pile from his body and blew upon it;

the attendant thereupon attained realization. Daopei Xiu said, "It is a pity that this monk took the sound and color of another’s words as his lifelong guide, failing to realize that his own radiance covers heaven and earth. Miaoxi said, "Miaoyan [Daopei] gave such a verdict."
[The Master] judged: "You have not even dreamed of Bird Nest. The Master said: "Huitong understood it at the moment the feather was picked up;
he then shouted, thereby sparing himself from being scrutinized by those in all quarters. For me to speak thus is also to increase delusion for the sake of idle matters."
To cite the Venerable Master Wuzhuo: while traveling to Mount Tai to present offerings, he was met by Mañjuśrī. As they proceeded, Mañjuśrī asked, "Virtuous One, from where have you come?
Wuzhuo replied, "From the South. Mañjuśrī asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South? Wuzhuo said:
A bhikṣu of the Dharma-ending age observed the precepts only sparingly. Mañjuśrī asked, "How many followers do you have? He replied, "Three hundred or five hundred.
Mañjuśrī then asked him, "How do you maintain the community here? Mañjuśrī said, "Ordinary people and sages dwell together."
Dragons and snakes were intermingled; [the assembly] asked, "How many people are here? Mañjuśrī said, "Three by three in front, three by three behind.
Miaoxi said, "If he had seen them at that time, he would have simply told them: 'For a Master to maintain the Dharma in such a manner is truly not easy.
The Master asked, "Ultimately, how many are those 'three by three in front, three by three behind'? Some say: "The 'three by three in front, three by three behind'..."
3. "I am not your equal; you will surely find what is good for yourself.
Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying: "In Jiangxi, Mazu says 'this very mind is Buddha. I, Old Man Wang, do not speak thus:
it is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. Is there any fault in this? At that time, Zhaozhou came forward.
Having prostrated, he departed. A monk asked Zhaozhou, "The Senior Monk (Zhangshang) prostrated and then left;
what was his intention? Zhaozhou said, "You should ask the Abbot instead. The monk then went to ask Daoyuan, "Just now, what was the intention of the Senior Monk Zhen?
Daoyuan said, "He indeed grasped my meaning. Miaoxi remarked, "Though these two old fellows..."
"Moving one's fingers inside a leather case—little do they realize that bystanders are laughing. The Master said, "Nanquan and Zhaozhou were both brought to account by this monk in a single stroke."
It is said that one day Nanquan asked a presiding master, "What sutra are you lecturing on? The master replied, "The *Sutra of Maitreya’s Descent to Be Born.
Nanquan asked, "When will Maitreya descend to be born? The master replied, "He is currently in the heavenly palace and has not yet come.
Nanquan said, "There is no Maitreya in heaven; there is no Maitreya on earth. Dongshan Shoujian cited this and questioned Yunju. Yunju said, "In heaven..."
"There is no Maitreya. There is no Maitreya beneath the earth.
When asked this, Dongshan was so struck that his meditation seat shook, and he said, "While I was at Yunyan, I once asked the Old Man about this, and my incense burner shook."
Today, when I was questioned by Beizi, it caused my entire body to break into a sweat.

Dayang Xuan said, "Now, as this old monk raises [the matter], if there is anyone who can answer, bring forth a question. He then said, "The earth shakes. Miaoxi said, "The meditation seat moves; the brazier moves;
the earth moves—these three old fellows are certainly not lacking. But if you want to see Nanquan, you must go directly."
"One must wait until Maitreya descends to be born before one may attain it. Suddenly, a man comes forward and says, "There is no Maitreya above in heaven, and there is no Maitreya below on earth.
Then what person are you going to have descend to be born? How would you answer? Simply say to him: [The text here implies the master's response to this challenge.]
"The old monk has committed a transgression. The Master said, "To weep until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one's mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring.
He cited the case where Layman Lu Xian addressed Nanquan, saying, "Master Zhao is truly extraordinary;
he can explain that heaven and earth share the same root and all things are one body. Nanquan pointed to the peony in the courtyard and said, "Layman, when people of this age see this—"

"Flowers on a branch are like a dream. Miaoxi said, "If you look at this from the perspective of principle, not only would Nanquan not be able to deceive Grand Master Lu Xun for a single moment, he would not even have touched a single hair on the back of his heels."
If you look at this from the perspective of phenomena, not only did Grand Master Lu Xun fail to deceive Nanquan by even a hair’s breadth, but he has not even dreamed of the stench of his sweat.
Should anyone come forward and say, "Great Master Jingshan, you speak of principle and phenomena," simply tell him:
"Just understand it within the context of principle and phenomena. The Master asked, "Does the assembly understand yet? You..."
If you seek understanding through the principle that heaven and earth share the same root and the myriad things are one body, you fall into the trap of Master Zhaoshan.
If you seek understanding through the integration of principle and phenomena (*li-shi*), you again fall into the tangles of Miaoxi. In either case, you have no freedom whatsoever.
It is just like Nanquan pointing to a peony and saying to Lu Xun: "Great Officer, when people see this single stalk of flowers..."
It is like a dream. How will you ultimately understand it? Tianning does not begrudge his eyebrows; for all of you, he provides this commentary:
"Where the level marshes end, there are green mountains; the traveler lies even beyond those green mountains."
Jue of Gehu asked the eminent masters, "In walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, what ultimately constitutes the Way? They replied, "It is that which knows.
Jue said, "It cannot be known by wisdom (*jñāna*), nor can it be cognized by consciousness (*vijñāna*). Why do you say it is 'that which knows'?

Another replied, "It is non-discrimination. Jue said, "One may be well able to discriminate the characteristics of all phenomena (*dharma-lakṣaṇa*), but regarding the primary truth (*paramārtha-satya*..."
Buddhamitra said, "It is immovable; how could it be without discrimination? Fayun said, "The four dhyānas and eight samādhis are [the answer].

Miaohui said, "The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any numerical categories; how could the four dhyānas and eight samādhis be it? The entire assembly was left speechless. Miaoxi said:
"If you scold me, I’ll let you have at me with your beak; if you spit at me, I’ll let you splash me with water. The Master said, "A monk stays overnight in a temple;
when a thief strikes, he cannot guard his own home.
He then cited Baolin’s story: One day, while on the road, he saw Layman Pang and asked him, "What was that phrase from the time of Nanyue when you gained strength?"
"Have you ever presented this to anyone? The scholar said, "I have. Lingyun asked, "To whom did you present it?
The scholar pointed to himself with his hand and said, "Master Pang. Lingyun said, "Truly, even Maudgalyāyana and Śāriputra could not praise him enough.
The scholar then asked Lingyun, "Who can understand the phrase by which one gains power? Lingyun then donned his bamboo hat and departed. The scholar said, "Excellent wayfarer!"
The Way. Once Ling departed, he never looked back. Miaoxi said, "If it were not for Master Pang, this matter would have nearly been misstated to others.
Nevertheless, Bai Ling was outdone by Old Pang by a single move. Why is that?"
At that time, had he not obtained a broken straw hat to cover his skull, what face would he have had to see Master Pang?
The Master said, "Baolin put on his hat and departed; bring forth clearly the phrase by which he gained strength.
For what reason did the Elder Miaoxi say, "What face did Baolin have to see Master Pang? This, too, is an instance of supporting the strong rather than the weak.
Weakness! Someone has taken over the role of Master Miaoxi. He asks: "What is the phrase that brings forth power? Speak quickly, speak quickly!
If you hesitate even for a moment, he strikes you across the spine with his staff.
Citing Master Pang’s question to Mazu: “The person of original nature is not obscure; I ask you, Master, to cast your eyes high. Mazu looked straight down.
The Master said, “A single stringless lute—only you, Master, can play it exquisitely. Mazu looked straight up. The Master then prostrated.
As Mazu returned to his quarters, the Master followed him in and said, “To be clever and end up clumsy. Miaoxi said, “Master Mazu!”

Looking up and looking down is not without its purpose; yet, alas, one’s original person remains obscured. Although the layman prostrated himself, it was like swallowing a whole jujube—whole and unchewed.
When Master Ma returned to his quarters, the layman followed behind him and said, "I have used cleverness and ended up with clumsiness;
I have saved half. The Master said, "What do you mean by 'saved half'? Thirty years from now, you will beat your breast with your hand."
A story from the past:
Once, a monk asked Zhaozhou, "I have newly entered this monastery; I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, "Have you finished eating your gruel?
The monk replied, "I have finished eating my gruel. Zhaozhou said, "Go wash your bowl. Thereupon, the monk attained realization.
[The monk] attained enlightenment. Yunmen said, "Now tell me, was there an instruction or not? If you say there was, what did Zhaozhou say to him?

If you say there was not, why did this monk attain enlightenment? Miaoxi said, "Yunmen is much like the Asura King, churning up the great city of the three realms and the ocean of all afflictions. He then shouted, "What is this idle chatter?"
The Master said: "O worthy ones, it is easy to see Yunmen; it is difficult to see Miaoxi. Where does the error lie?
The sword has long since been lost, yet you are still marking the boat."
Citing the case of Zhaozhou, when a monk was taking his leave, Zhaozhou asked, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to study the Buddha-dharma in various quarters.
Zhaozhou held up his whisk and said, "Do not dwell where there is a Buddha; pass quickly through where there is no Buddha.
Even three thousand miles away, do not speak of this in error when meeting people. The monk said, "If that is so, then I shall not go. Zhaozhou said, "Plucking the willows..."
"Plucking the willow blossoms. Miaoxi said: "Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; an iron weight has been eaten through by worms.
Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly, bumping into the broken stove that fell at Mount Song. Three thousand miles away, do not mistakenly raise this to others.
Two stone men whisper to each other. If it were so, then one would not go. This story has already spread everywhere."
Wandering through the world. Plucking the willow blossoms, plucking the willow blossoms. *Oṃ maṇidāri hūṃ phaṭ*. After Lin-yün Yüeh finished citing the words of Master Miao-hsi, he said:
"The old man Miao-hsi exerted his full strength, yet he could only reach this far. Do you know where Xiang-shan lands?
When the Iron Mountain collapses and crushes the Silver Mountain, the bowl rolls the pearl, and the pearl rolls the bowl."
Densely woven, the mandarin ducks are embroidered at leisure; the golden needle is never shown to others. The Master said:
"The Great Ancestor Miaoxi sang this before; I, a distant descendant of Tianning, harmonize it after. Before the gate grows lettuce; from the lettuce grow chopsticks.
From the chopsticks bloom lotus flowers; from the lotus flowers form papayas. Suddenly a papaya falls to the ground, scattering—"
Countless, countless sesame seeds come forth. Why is this? It is because they must enter the threshing floor.
[The Master] cites Zhaozhou’s discussion on doctrine with Wenyuan: "We contend over inferiority, not superiority; the victor loses a sesame cake. Wenyuan said:
"Please, Preceptor, establish your thesis. Zhaozhou said, "I am a donkey. Yuanwu said, "I am the donkey’s stomach.
Zhaozhou said, "I am the donkey’s dung. Yuanwu said, "I am a worm in the dung. Zhaozhou said, "What do you do in there?
Yuanwu said, "I spend the summer retreats in there. Zhaozhou said, "Bring me some fried cakes. Miaoxi said, "The Text."
"Far away, spending the summer retreat amidst donkey dung. A red face is not as good as straightforward speech. Zhaozhou, coveting a small profit, won only a sesame cake.
Examining this from the start, it was like a man from Puzhou escorting a thief. But in the end, how is it? The Goose King chooses his own milk;
he has never been of the duck class. The Master said: "At that time, Wenyuan waited for Old Man Zhaozhou to say, 'I..."
"This is a donkey," he said, "and you have already lost your sesame cakes. The old man went to take the cakes, but [the master] snatched them from his hand and walked away.
Once, while Changsha was enjoying the moon one night, Yangshan said, "Everyone possesses this very thing; it is only that..."
"You cannot use it. Sandal said, "Precisely; I am borrowing it from you to use. Shishuang asked, "How will you use it?
Sandal then gave him a kick that knocked him over. As Shishuang rose up, he said, "You are truly like a great tiger! Miaoxi said:

"A single bright orb, its cold light extending ten thousand miles. Those who are sharp-witted know autumn when the leaves fall; those who are dull and sluggish find that loyal words are contrary [to their desires]."
"Listen! Whether resting or not resting, whether having ceased or not having ceased—this little Śākyamuni possesses the mechanism of a tiger-trap, yet this great beast has no teeth.
At that time, a single kick was by no means a matter of haste; falling suddenly to the ground was no mere accident. After a long silence, he said:

"Even if there were someone among you who could distinguish the black from the white and bring forth these two elders, it would still be like swinging a club to strike at the moon. The Master [concluded].
Xiaoshijia said, "How do you apply this? Cendachong then gave him a kick.
Everyone said that he transcended the mundane world and walked alone within the realm. Tianning, unable to restrain his impatience, also intended to place a torch in a cold spot.
The two great elders have thus revealed themselves; at the gateway of their transformative teaching, one may truly behold the marvels.
Yet as for this very matter, it is likely beyond all reach.
To cite the case of the attendant Gan-zhi: he entered Nanquan’s hall for a vegetarian feast where Huangbo served as the head seat (shouzuo).

The attendant requested that alms be given. Huangbo said, “Between the two gifts of wealth and Dharma, there is no distinction. The attendant took his money and went out. A moment later, he returned and again requested that alms be given.
Huangbo said, “Between the two gifts of wealth and Dharma, there is no distinction. Thereupon, the attendant distributed the offerings. —Miaoxi.
Yun said, "In one sense, they are equally following the heterodox and pursuing evil; yet Yunju Luohan is slightly superior.
The Master said, "In this way, in this way—upright Ganqi and topple Huangbo. Not in this way, not in this way—upright Huangbo."
Overthrowing Ganji: "If it is thus within the state of 'not thus,' yet not thus within the state of 'not thus'—how then?
A lion bites a man; a hunting dog chases a clod of earth.
Citing Guishan: Once Guishan entered the mountains with Baizhang to perform manual labor. Baizhang asked, "Have you brought fire? Guishan replied, "I have. Baizhang asked, "Where is it?
Guishan took a piece of firewood, blew on it twice, and handed it over. Baizhang said, "It is like an insect boring through wood.
Miaoxi said, "If Baizhang had not spoken those final words, he would have been deceived by the head cook. The Master said, "Baizhang, however—"
Because of his subsequent words, he was exposed by others, bringing misfortune upon the steward who followed the deviant and pursued evil. Fortunately for Tianning, there was no trouble;
but as for you all, what are you seeking here? "One blind man leading a crowd of blind men, pulling each other into a fire pit.
With his staff, he drove them all away at once.
Huangbo raised the topic for the assembly, saying: "All of you here are nothing but fellows who eat the dregs of wine.
Traveling on pilgrimage like this, how could you have a 'today' [of realization]? Do you know that within the Great Tang Empire there are no Zen masters?

At that time, a monk asked, "But as for those in various quarters who guide disciples and lead assemblies, what of them? Huangbo said, "I do not say there are no Zen masters; it is simply that there are none."
The Master said, "Miaoxi said: 'Tell me, is this a phrase of ambrosia or a phrase of poison? The Master said:
'A sword that kills, a blade that gives life. Let those with eyes discern it.'"
It is said that one day Huangbo was asked by Nanquan, "Regarding the equal cultivation of concentration and wisdom and the clear realization of Buddha-nature—what is the principle of this?
Huangbo replied, "In the twelve periods of the day, you must not rely upon or depend on a single thing. Nanquan said, "Is this not your own personal view, Elder?
Huangbo replied, "I dare not say so. Nanquan said, "Setting aside the price of the gruel for a moment, who will pay for the straw sandals?"
Huangbo retired. Miaoxi said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one's sword; if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem.
The Master said, "This is meeting what is convenient, yet it is also falling into what is convenient."
Yangshan was once asked by a monk, "Does the Dharma-body understand how to preach the Dharma?
Yangshan replied, "I cannot preach it; there is another person who can. The monk asked, "Where is that person who can preach it? Yangshan then pushed out his pillow.
When Guishan heard of this, he said, "Jizi (Yangshan) employs the business of the sword's edge. Miaoxi said, "Guishan was precisely..."
Out of pity for his son, he was unaware of the ugliness [of his teaching]. Yangshan pushed out the pillow—this was already a "leakage" (a slip).

To further apply a name and call it "the matter on the edge of a sword" is to mislead those who merely mimic the words; they then proceed in this manner, receiving echoes and transmitting them as empty sounds.
Although Miaoxi borrows water to offer flowers, the principle remains without deviation. Do not, even now, [fall into such error].
There was one who was unwilling to comply; he came forward, saying, "I wish to question you. He pushed out his pillow and asked, "Does this count as the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma?
The Master said, "This monk asks about the Dharma-body preaching the Dharma, yet he does not even realize he has missed the mark.
Yangshan pushed out his pillow; when had he ever seen it? Great as Moshan was, he took the wrong for the right and matched it against the edge of a sword.
He tied the objects together into a single bundle and weighed them on a scale; they came out at eight taels and half a catty.

If there were no difference in weight, then at that moment, as soon as he saw this monk ask whether the Dharma-body can preach the Dharma or not, he would have immediately taken long strides back to his quarters.
Is this not the mark of an extraordinary master? It spares the monks of the world from further censure and disparagement.

It is said that Yangshan once asked Xiangyan, "Disciple, you have recently composed a verse on the realization of the Way; try reciting it for me. Xiangyan then recited his verse on striking the bamboo.
Yangshan said, "This is merely something you fabricated during your leisure time. He then recited another verse, which began: "Last year I was poor..."
"This is poverty. Poverty this year is the beginning of poverty. Last year’s poverty, one still had enough ground to set a single awl upon; this year’s poverty, there is not even an awl.
Mazu said, "You have only attained the Buddha-dharma (Tathāgata-citta), you have not attained the Patriarchal-dharma (Śāstr-citta).
He then presented another verse, saying: "I have a device: I blink my eyes at him. If anyone does not understand, I shall call for a novice monk. Mazu said, "For now..."
Xiji said, "My junior brother appreciates the Patriarchal Chan of our ancestors. Miaoxi said, "In his later years, Guishan was fond of puppet shows.
He taught them how to perform a whole stage of meat puppets; they are truly lovely. But what is it about them that makes them so lovely?
They look at one another face to face while their hands and feet move; who knows that the speech is that of others? The Master said, "Elder brother, younger brother; last year, this year."
What path do you discuss? What dhyāna do you speak of? This is nothing more than swinging a staff to strike at the moon; how is it any different from digging into the earth to seek the sky?
Dhyāna, dhyāna—there is neither subtlety nor mystery therein. Do not mistake the envelope for the letter itself.

Xiangyan raised this case for the assembly, saying: "Suppose a person is at the edge of a thousand-fathom precipice, with a tree branch in their mouth, neither hand having anything to grasp and neither foot having anything to tread upon.
Suddenly, someone asks about the meaning of the Westward Journey. If they do not answer, they violate the questioner’s intent;
if they do answer, they lose their body and life. At such a moment, what would you do? At that time, there was Houtou...
Zuō said, “I do not ask about having already climbed the tree; I ask the Master to speak before climbing it. Yán laughed heartily.
Mìxǐ said, “To swallow the thorny chestnut and penetrate the diamond ring—to look at such talk is like a person from Sīzhōu seeing the Great Sage.
The Master said, “The Elder Xiāngyán explained through skillful means; Tǔtóu Zuòshàng had not yet [attained it].”
To discern the initial signs: if one were to discuss the vigorous stimulation of this matter, it would take sixty kalpas across three lifetimes.
Take, for example, Lingyun’s awakening upon seeing peach blossoms; there is a verse: "For thirty years I have sought the swordsman;
/ Several times the leaves have fallen and branches have sprouted. / Since first beholding the peach blossoms, / To this very day I have had no further doubt. This is cited as an illustration.
Guishan said, "Entering through conditions, one will never again fall back or lose it. You must guard and uphold this well. He then presented this to Xuansha.
Xuansha said, "It is precise, most precise; yet I dare say you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate. Miaoxi said, "When one house has trouble, a hundred houses are busy.
The Master said, "If a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate anxieties. Even if one were refined a hundred times..."
Gold cannot avoid entering the furnace for further smelting.
[The Master] cited the case of Muzhou seeing a monk coming and saying, "This is a settled case; I grant you thirty blows.
The monk said, "I am like this. Muzhou asked, "Why does the *vajra* at the gate raise its fist? The monk said, "Even the *vajra* is thus."
The Master struck him. Miaoxi said, "Although it is a holeless flute striking a felt clapper, the five notes are truly harmonious and the six pitch-pipes are perfectly tuned.
Yet, if one examines this closely, it cannot avoid being laughed at by the bystanders. Now tell me, who is the bystander?
After a long silence, he said, "Do not touch it; if you touch it, I shall break your donkey’s back. The Master [laughed].
It is said: "Muzhou and this monk—were both of them adepts, or were both of them non-adepts? Is there anyone who can discern this?
[The Master] cited the occasion when Linji was attending upon Deshan. Deshan said, "I am exhausted today. Linji said, "This old fellow is talking in his sleep."
"Ma! Shan then struck him. Ji overturned the meditation seat. Yunfeng Yue said, "How extraordinary, all you practitioners!
These two masters—one pressing, one nudging—briefly reveal their style. It is very much like climbing a high mountain hand-in-hand.
Nevertheless, even so, they cannot avoid being laughed at by the bystanders. But tell me, who is the bystander? He gave a shout and descended from his seat.
Miaoxi said: "Yunfeng’s critique in this manner is very much like a man from Puzhou. If Jingshan saw him, he would have bound him into a bundle and cast him into the river.
Have you not heard it said: 'When the clam and the heron hold each other fast, both fall into the hands of the fisherman'? The Master said:
"Among the assembly, they say that Deshan and Linji are 'fine hands presenting fine hands within their hands; hitting the red heart within the red heart.'"
The Red Heart. Little do they realize that by exhausting their own minds, they only end up making others laugh.
To cite Linji’s inquiry: "There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home; there is another person..."
Having left his home and not being on the road, who is it that deserves the offerings of devas and humans? Miaoxi said, "The thief’s identity has already been revealed.
The Master said, "The heavens share the dawn with white clouds; the waters flow with the bright moon."
Baoshou raised the case of his questioning Hu Dingjiao, saying, "Are you not Hu Dingjiao? Hu replied, "I dare not say so. Baoshou said, "Can you nail the void?
Hu said, "Please let the Master nail it broken for me. Baoshou then struck him. Hu said, "Do not strike me in error.
Baoshou said, "In the future, when you encounter a talkative master, he will point it out for you. Hu—
Later, he arrived at Zhaozhou and brought up the previous story, asking, "I do not know where my fault lies.
Zhaozhou said, "This very seam—there is still nothing one can do about it. At these words, Dingjiao attained awakening.

Miaoxi said, "Even if one were able to nail down this seam, when subjected to critical examination, it would still not be the work of a true master. It is truly pitiful that these two old Chan masters instead faced a layman."
People say that one should not speak of a family’s internal disgrace. The Master said, "The barbarian tailor! He fundamentally did not know about this single seam.
At that time, had Zhaozhou not provided the thief with a ladder to climb over, even if he had worn out one hundred and twenty pairs of straw sandals, it still would not have been noticed.
Although you may understand the meaning of the nails and hinges, you are still three thousand *li* behind Baoshou.
To cite the case where Sansheng asked Xuefeng, "What does the golden fish that has passed through the net eat? Feng replied, "Wait until it comes out of the net, and then I will tell you.
Sansheng said, "A teacher of fifteen hundred people who does not even recognize the head of the matter!"
Feng said, "The old monk’s duties as abbot are many. Miaoxi said, "One person is coarse like a mountain; another is fine like rice powder.
Although their coarseness and fineness differ, when weighed on the scale, their weight is exactly equal. Today at Jingshan, I truly announce this to all:
you must absolutely avoid boring through tortoises or striking tiles. The Master said, "When a golden fish has passed through the net, what can be used [to catch it]?"
"Eat. Wait for you to come out of the net, and then I shall tell you: 'Piercing through the azure void, a thousand fathoms of pines;
cutting off the red dust, a single stream of water.
He then cited Nan-yuan’s case where a monk asked: "Upon this lump of flesh, it stands like a cliff ten thousand feet high—is this not the Master's [teaching]? It is indeed so.
"What do you say? The Master said, "Yes. The monk then overturned the meditation seat. The Master said, "Look at this blind fellow making such a mess!
The monk hesitated, and the Master struck him out. Miaoxi said, "I now guarantee for you that this matter shall never be in vain.
The Master said, "This monk dared to rub an itch on the head of a venomous snake and scale the jaws of a blue dragon. Who [could do otherwise]?"
I do not praise his audacity; it is simply that he lacked one move at the end. Since leaving the cave, he has had no rival, yet where he could have spared another, he chose to spare him.
One day Xinghua said, "Kebin, the Rector, you will before long become a master of the Dharma assembly. Kebin replied, "I will not enter this community.
Xinghua asked, "Do you refuse to enter because you understand, or because you do not understand? Kebin said, "It is neither so.
Xinghua then struck him and said, "Rector Kebin, you have been defeated in the battle of the Dharma. You shall pay a fine of five strings of cash. He then set up [the collection].
The rice gruel was served in a single hall. When the next day came, Xinghua personally struck the gavel and said, "Venerable Kebin, you have not been victorious in the Dharma-battle;
you shall not eat. He then immediately drove him out. Yunju Shun said, "This is like refined gold from a great furnace—it should remain unchanged in color.
Yet, Xinghua’s enforcement of the command was too severe. Even had it not been Venerable Kebin, it would still have been very difficult to bear."
"If one were like those common, drifting fellows of today, how much time would it take to turn over their faces?
Miaoxi said, "Yunju twists the crooked to make it straight. Miaoxi continued, "If you wish to be a brilliant descendant of Linji, you must indeed turn over your face.
The Master said, "Kebin was defeated in the battle of Dharma; Xinghua acted according to the command to uphold and promote [the teaching]."
The spirit of the Linji school reveals the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye: "From the tip of the staff comes the filial son; the Buddha-dharma knows no human sentiment.
At that time, one might think the thatch is long or short, but once it is burned away, one finds the ground was originally uneven.
[The Master] cited the occasion when Yaoshan asked Shitou: "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
However, I have heard that in the South they point directly to the human mind and see one's nature to become a Buddha; I truly do not yet understand this clearly.
I humbly hope that the Venerable Master will compassionately provide instruction. Shitou said: "It is not so, nor is it otherwise. It is neither 'so' nor 'otherwise. Totality...
"No. "How do you understand it? Sansheng paused for thought. Deshan said, "Your karmic conditions do not lie here.
There is Master Mazu in Jiangxi; go there, and he will explain it for you. Sansheng went there and questioned him as before.
Master Mazu said, "Sometimes I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink; sometimes I do not instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink."
At times Mazu would instruct him that raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes was it; at other times he would instruct him that raising the eyebrows and blinking the eyes was not it.
At this, Shanshan attained a realization and prostrated himself. Mazu asked, "What principle have you seen?
Shanshan replied, "When I was with Stonehead, it was like a mosquito on an iron ox. Mazu said, "Since you are thus, you should guard it well."
Miaoxi said, "What a fine topic! Who can bring it up? Even if one could bring it up perfectly, I would not yet dare grant my approval.
The Master said, "Yaoshan only knows of the mosquito on the iron ox; he does not know that the iron ox bites the mosquito.
The pillar was personally struck once; the lantern has no place to hide its body. Startled by this, Great Master Mazu transformed himself into Old Miaoxi."
Let me ask you this first: from where does the root of these words arise? If you scold one another, I grant you the right to jab at each other’s mouths;
if you spit at one another, I grant you the right to splash water.
[I cite] Dongshan’s address to the assembly: "At the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, whether going east or west, you must head toward the ten thousand miles of nothingness."
"One must depart from the place where there is not even an inch of grass. But as for the place where there are ten thousand *li* and not an inch of grass—how does one go?

Later, he mentioned this to Shishuang, who said, "As soon as you step out the door, it is grass. Upon hearing this, Xuedou said, "In all the land of the Great Tang, how many people could there be [who understand this]?
Miaoxi said, "A single drop of lion’s milk scatters ten bushels of donkey’s milk. The Master said, "Thief!"
This is a base person whose wisdom surpasses that of a gentleman.
Jia Shan raised his staff and addressed the assembly, saying: "Recognize the old monk at the tips of the hundred grasses; recognize the Son of Heaven in the bustling marketplace."
Yunmen said, "A shrimp drills through your nostrils; a venomous snake pierces your eyes. You must understand this within the tangle of vines.
Miaoxi said, "Jiashan sets up a trap and draws an arrow upon himself; Yunmen mistakes a thief for his own son.

Although it is so, those who recognize kindness are few, while those who betray it are many. The Master said, "At the tips of the hundred grasses, to whom do you offer your realization? In the midst of the bustling marketplace..."
"What do you recognize?
[The Master] raised the case of Jiuping when he was serving as an attendant at Shishuang. Because Puhui had passed away, the assembly proposed the Head Seat to take over as abbot.
Jiuping said, "One must clearly understand the late master’s meaning before one may occupy this position. He then asked, "The late master said: 'It is like being inside an ancient temple...'"
"The incense burner has gone; it has gone cold and still; it is like a single length of white silk; a film has formed on its rim. "How do you, Head Seat, understand this?
The Head Seat said, "I understand it as a matter of the realm of uniformity. Xuefeng said, "You have not yet grasped the meaning of our former teacher."
"He must not remain," the Abbot said. "Bring incense here. If I do not understand the meaning of my predecessor, I shall not be able to cast off this body when the smoke rises.
As soon as the smoke began to rise, the Head Seat (Shouzuo) cast off his body. Daofeng then patted him on the back and said: [He has departed.]
"Passing away while seated or dying while standing—this is certainly not something the Head Seat lacked. Yet, he had not even dreamed of the late Master’s intent.

Miaoxi said, "Two iron hammers without holes; among them, one is particularly heavy. The Master said, "The Head Seat passed away while seated or standing, yet the attendant speaks of yellow paths and black ways.
The late Master’s intent lies at the tip of the hook; you must believe that within the curve there is a straight line. If it were at the brink..."
"Under Jie’s gate, who is to eat these thirty blows? As soon as one speaks of right and wrong, one is already a person of right and wrong.
[The Master] cites Caoshan’s address to the assembly: "Everywhere else they all employ restrictive measures;

why not give him a turning word to let him go without doubt? Yunmen then asked: "In the place of absolute secrecy, why is it that one does not know there is [something]? Caoshan said: "It is precisely because..."
"Thick and dense. Therefore, one does not know that it exists. Wumen asked, "How should one approach this person?
Deshan said, "Do not approach him in the place of thickness and density. Wumen asked, "What is it like when one does not approach in the place of thickness and density?

Deshan said, "Only then do you understand how to approach. Wumen responded with two "Nos. Miaoxi said, "It is like adding more turbid oil to an already damp lamp wick. The Master said, "The Snowy Mountains."
[The mountain] extends three thousand li to the south.
He held up Qianfeng Peak and said to the assembly: "If you raise one, you must not raise two. To let pass one move is to fall into the second."
Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and said, "Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan.
Feng said, "Tomorrow there shall be no communal labor," and then descended from his seat. Miaoxi said, "Ganfeng was washing his face when he felt his nose;
Yunmen was eating his meal when he bit upon grit. The two met by chance, and it turns out they are old enemies after all."
"Even so, it is permitted only for the Old Barbarian to know; it is not permitted for the Old Barbarian to understand. He further said, "Both are exposing their own family's ugliness;
fortunately, there are no bystanders to witness it. The Master said, "Two hunchbacks have met each other; in this world today, there is no upright person."

This is recorded in the *Biyan lu* (Blue Cliff Record), Case 20. It is also cited in the *Wumenguan* (Gateless Barrier), Case 19. Furthermore, in the *Jingde chuandeng lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp), Volume 13, the account of Magu’s enlightenment under Nanquan is recorded as follows: Magu asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan said, "Ordinary mind is the Way. Magu asked, "How does one maintain ordinary mind? Nanquan said, "Wherever your thoughts go, that is it. Magu then bowed in gratitude. Magu was originally a layman from Xiangzhou who had studied the Vinaya. One day, while traveling through the mountains, he encountered a tiger and leaped onto its back. The tiger roared and fled, leading him deep into the mountains. There he met an old man who asked, "Layman, where are you going? Magu replied, "I am seeking the Way. The old man said, "If you seek the Way, you will never find it. Why not just be ordinary? At these words, Magu experienced a great awakening. He then took up the monastic life and traveled to various places to study under masters such as Huairang, Mazu, Baizhang, and Nanquan. Eventually, he settled at Mount Gu in Tanzhou. His teaching style was direct and unadorned; he often used the staff to strike people or simply remained silent. He passed away in the second year of the Dazhong period of the Tang dynasty (848 CE) at the age of ninety-three. His remains were enshrined at Mount Gu. He is known posthumously as Chan Master Shouzhuo. His dharma heirs included Fayan Wenyi, Xuefeng Yicun, and others. He is ranked as the twenty-third patriarch in the lineage of the Linji school. His teachings are preserved in the *Zuting shiyuan* (Anthology of the Patriarchal Hall), the *Dongshan lu* (Record of Dongshan), and other collections. He is frequently cited in Zen literature for his skillful use of the staff and his ability to cut through conceptualization. His legacy continues to influence Zen practice and philosophy to this day.

Xiangyan said, "All myriad functions cease; even the thousand sages cannot carry one away. Shushan made a gesture of vomiting.
Xiangyan said, "Does my junior uncle not approve? Shushan said, "It would not do to be without fault. Xiangyan asked, "Where does the fault lie?"
Mount Yun said, "When the myriad functions have ceased, there is still something remaining; though the thousand sages did not carry it with them, it is nevertheless obtained from man.

"What is it? [Yanguan] said. "I assent. "And what is it you assent to? Guishan said, "If you assent, you assent to all the sages;

Whenever Baizhang ascended the seat, there was always an old man who listened to the Dharma. One day, when the assembly had departed, the old man remained alone.
Baizhang asked, "Who are you? The old man replied, "I am not a human being. However, five hundred lifetimes ago, during the time of Kāśyapa Buddha, I once resided on this mountain.
Because I gave a mistaken answer to a student regarding a single phrase, I have been [reborn as such] for five hundred lives."
"In a former life, I fell into the body of a wild fox. Now I wish to raise this koan; I beg the Master to answer it. The Master said, "Try raising it for me.
The old man said, "Does a person of great cultivation still fall within the realm of cause and effect?
I replied, "He does not fall within cause and effect. The Master said, "Ask me, and I will tell you. The old man then asked, "Does a person of great cultivation still..."

"Neither falling into nor not falling into cause and effect. Baizhang said, "Cause and effect are not obscured. Thereupon, the old man attained awakening, cast off his wild fox body, and departed as a transformed spirit.

Closing the door to build a carriage, yet opening the door to find the tracks already aligned. Changing the bushel-measure and shifting the stars; taking the sun and making it the moon.
When cold, it is cold; when hot, it is hot. The wooden horse gallops like smoke; the clay ox flows with blood.
Whenever it was time for the meal, Jinniu would personally carry the food to the front of the Sangha Hall, clap his hands, and laugh heartily, saying:
"Sons of the Bodhisattvas, come and eat! Sons of the Bodhisattvas, come and eat! Later, a monk asked Changqing, "What is the meaning of 'Sons of the Bodhisattvas, come and eat'?
Changqing replied, "It is very much like celebrating and praising because of the midday meal. Another monk later asked Da... [text fragment]
Guang. Changqing said: "Regarding the celebration and praise during the meal, what is the underlying meaning? Guang performed a dance. The monk then prostrated.
Guang asked, "How do you understand this? The monk also performed a dance. Guang said, "You wild fox spirit!"
A single plate of rice from the Ox-Head Mountain, deliberately sprinkled with pepper and ginger—it is not fit for a gluttonous man to eat; it would be a vain labor for his sleeves to flutter long.
If this monk were a man of heroic spirit, even the pores of his skin would still need to be fragrant for seven days.
Shushan addressed the assembly, saying: "Before the Xiantong era, this sick monk understood the affairs of the *dharmakāya*;
after the Xiantong era, I understood the matters above the *dharmakāya*. Yunmen came forward and asked: "What are the affairs of the *dharmakāya*?
Shushan said: "A withered stump. Yunmen asked: "What are the matters above the *dharmakāya*? Shushan said: "Not a withered stump."

Mendun asked, "Do you permit a student to speak according to principle? Mount Yunmen said, "I do. Mendun said, "As for a withered stump—is that not clarifying matters pertaining to the Dharma-body (dharmakāya)?
Mount Yunmen said, "It is. Mendun said, "Is it not the case that what is not a withered stump clarifies matters above the Dharma-body?
Mount Yunmen said, "It is. Mendun said, "I wonder, does the Dharma-body encompass all things or not?"
Mount Yun said, "The Dharma-body is all-pervasive; how could it not encompass everything? Baizhang Huaihai pointed to a pure water jar and asked, "Is there a Dharma-body here as well?
Mount Yun said, "Do not seek it within the pure water jar. Baizhang said, "Yes, yes."
Snatching the deer from the mouth of a fierce tiger; dividing the rabbit from beneath the talons of a hungry hawk.
Shushan encounters Yunmen—here one may see him walking alone through the entire realm. Before the Xiantong era and after the Xiantong era; above the Dharma-body and beside the Dharma-realm.
A single red thread connects two people; it was simply that at that time, their conversation had not yet reached its conclusion.
On the road to Mount Tai, there was an old woman. A monk asked her, "Where does one go on the road to Mount Tai? The woman said, "Go straight ahead.
As soon as the monk began to walk, the woman said, "What a fine master, going off just like that! This occurred when monks questioned her from both before and after.
It was all like this. Later, a monk recounted these events to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "Wait; let me test and expose this old woman for you.
He then went to her and asked, "Which way does the road to Mount Tai go? The woman replied, "Go straight ahead.
Just as Zhaozhou began to walk away, the woman said, "What a fine master! And yet, you go off like that. Zhaozhou returned and related this to the assembly, saying, "I have tested you for you..."
"Having broken this old woman, he has seen through her completely. The Elder (Lao-su) picked up the point and said: "Where was she broken through?
"The beginning of his journey did not reach its destination; the end went too far. Sitting in Zhaozhou’s house, he broke through the old woman of Mount Tai.
A lion bites a man; a hunting dog chases a clod of earth. This old fellow of seven hundred years has today been caught red-handed with the stolen goods."
Yunmen addressed the assembly, saying: "To awaken to the Way upon hearing sound; to clarify the mind upon seeing form. What is it to awaken to the Way upon hearing sound?
What is it to clarify the mind upon seeing form? Raising his hand, he said: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys fried cakes with money.
Lowering his hand, he said: "It turns out to be steamed buns after all."
The Old Man of Shaoyang speaks in sounds and colors; among the rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds, how many monks can truly know the essential point?
It turns out that a sesame cake is just a steamed bun; a great man ought to be free.
Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the door? The monk said, "The sound of raindrops. Jingqing said, "Sentient beings are inverted;
they lose themselves and pursue external things. The monk asked, "How about you, Master? Jingqing said, "I have not lost myself. The monk said, "..."
"What is the meaning? Qing said: "To manifest one's person may still be easy; to shed the entire body in the Way should be difficult.
Regarding the sound of falling rain, how can it be heard? If one is not deluded regarding oneself, who would lean their ear toward it?
Does the sound come to the side of the ear, or does the ear go to the side of the sound? Both banks are profound; neither is complete.
Nanquan addressed the assembly, saying: "Last night Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma;
I gave each of them twenty blows and banished them to the two Iron Ring Mountains. Zhaozhou stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "Whom did the Master’s blows intend for them to eat?
Nanquan said, "What fault has Old Wang committed? Zhaozhou bowed, and Nanquan descended from his seat and returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The two Iron Ring Mountains; the Buddha’s vision and the Dharma’s vision—Nanquan and Zhaozhou were adept at seizing the opportune moment. When exhausted, one changes;
when changed, one penetrates. The wind follows the tiger; the clouds follow the dragon.
Xuefeng asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk said, "Fuchuan. Xuefeng said, "The sea of birth and death has not yet been crossed;
why have you overturned your boat? The monk was speechless. Fuchuan spoke on his behalf, saying, "He has no birth and death.
Xuedou spoke on his behalf, saying, "I have long admired Xuefeng."
The ocean of birth and death is boundless; who knows who can cross it? A single phrase from the "Capsized Boat" cuts off both paths.
Old Xuedou fusses and fumbles; within the armory of our King, there is no such blade.
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the teaching for all generations? Yunmen said, "I speak in response to one.
This is like being startled by a clumsy fellow, speaking in response to one; it is like sticking to a fixed peg while tuning the strings, or swinging a club to strike at the moon.
Who is this person appearing beyond the heavens? Their nostrils remain, as before, tucked over the upper lip.
A monk asked Yunmen: "When it is neither the mechanism before one's eyes nor the matter before one's eyes, what then?
Yunmen said: "Turn it upside down.
Who can turn it upside down when facing the pivot? Seven strides and eight leaps; a thousand differences and ten thousand distinctions. Shitian calls out to the earth.
Plowing with oxen. Without sowing, spiritual sprouts grow everywhere throughout the world.
Once, when Guishan asked Yangshan, "The weather is cold; are the people cold? Yangshan replied, "Everyone is right here. Guishan said:
"Why do you not speak directly? Yangshan said, "Just now, I was not being indirect either. How about you, Master? Muzhou said, "For now, you must simply go with the flow.
Muzhou and Yangshan—when the weather is cold, people are cold; this single phrase of "going with the flow" manifests in ten thousand ways and a thousand forms, like a ball rolling over a board.
A pearl rolling on a platter—rely on the gentleman to observe this closely. Neither increasing nor decreasing is the vajra-body;
neither sage nor ordinary is the lump of red flesh.
Once, when the World-Honored One was staying in one place for the ninety-day summer retreat, on the day of *pravāraṇā*, Mañjuśrī suddenly arrived. Kāśyapa...
Question: "Where did you observe the summer retreat this year? Mañjuśrī replied, "I observed the summer retreat in three places.
Kāśyapa then addressed the assembly, intending to expel Mañjuśrī. As soon as he struck the *gaṇḍī* gong, he beheld every single Buddha in immeasurable Buddha-fields.
Each and every Mañjuśrī and each and every Kāśyapa raised their mallets, intending to expel him.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One said to Kāśyapa, "Which Mañjuśrī do you now intend to expel?"
The unique Mañjuśrī, the non-dual Mañjuśrī—hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, filling every corner of the dusty world.
What a pity that the Venerable Kāśyapa missed his chance at that moment! Since he had already raised the mallet, why did he not strike once?
To see something and fail to seize it is a regret that will haunt one for a thousand years; it is nothing but a medicine bag trailing behind a funeral carriage.
Yantou raised it up and addressed the assembly, saying: "The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* states: 'The intent of my teaching is like a poison-coated drum;
whoever hears it, whether near or far, perishes upon being struck. A monk asked, 'What is the poison-coated drum? Yantou leaned his body forward and said, 'Han Xin at the imperial court.'"
The poison-coated drum kills all who hear it; how many have died upon the level ground! To find life within death—this is truly worthy of being made a model for the monastic community.
Whether Han Xin knew it when facing the throne or not, he suddenly emerged at Dangyang and gave voice to this discourse.
[The text] cites Mañjuśrī’s question to the woman Antivāsinī: "What is the meaning of 'birth'? The woman replied:
"The meaning of birth is that which is born through non-birth. Mañjuśrī asked: "How is it that the meaning of birth is that which is born through non-birth? The woman said:
"If one can clearly know that the four conditions—earth, water, fire, and wind—have never themselves attained any state of combination, yet are able to function accordingly..."
[The Master] said, "This is appropriate; I take this as the meaning of life. Shu asked, "What is the meaning of death?
The woman replied, "Death takes the non-death of death as its meaning. Shu asked, "How is it that death takes the non-death of death as its meaning?

The woman replied, "If one can clearly know that the four conditions of earth, water, fire, and wind have never themselves attained any state of separation or dispersion, yet can [respond] accordingly to them—"
It is appropriate to regard death as righteousness and life as being born through non-birth. A winter melon hanging from a gourd trellis—this is life. To regard death as not dying—this is death.
Holding a night market within the eye of a gnat. Union and separation each follow what is appropriate; ultimately, [they are all such].
Who was he? Guizong addressed the assembly, saying: "I now wish to speak of Chan; all you sons, come forward. When the great assembly stepped forward, Guizong said:
"Listen to the practice of Avalokiteśvara, which skillfully responds to all places. A monk asked: "What is the practice of Avalokiteśvara?"
Zong snapped his fingers and asked, "Did you hear that, everyone? The monks replied, "We heard it. Zong said, "You lot! What are you looking for here?
He struck them with his staff to drive them away, then laughed heartily and returned to his quarters.
A single snap of the fingers by Guizong: in every land and at every dust mote, they arise from meditative concentration.

Within their eyes, hundreds of thousands of millions of Mount Sumerus can be contained; within their ears, inconceivable oceans of water can be held. How can the practices of Avalokiteśvara be compared?
The Shaolin teachings are but a vain discourse on skin and marrow.
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huibian Chushi, "The Sun of the Buddha Shining Universally," Volume Twelve Phonetic Transcriptions:

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huibian Chushi, “The Sun of the Buddha Shining Universally,” Volume Thirteen, Part One:
Verses and Eulogies for Buddhas and Patriarchs.
Compiled by Attendant Wensheng, Zhenglong, and others.
In the third year of the Zhizhi era, the year being Guihai, in the sixth month I received an imperial decree and arrived at the capital.

In the eighth month, I went to the White Stupa Temple to behold the auspicious sandalwood image carved by King Udayana. I prostrated myself a hundred times and paid my respects, and thus composed this eulogy.
In this praise, I do not grasp a single dharma, even as small as a mote of dust; I do not discard a single dharma, even as slight as the tip of an autumn hair.
I have always perceived the Buddha in this manner, yet there is neither seeing nor non-seeing. Excellent, O Udayana, it is likewise so: neither grasping nor discarding.
Śākyamuni and Maudgalyāyana likewise possess such supernormal powers; among the thirty-two marks, there is none that is not thus.

It is for this reason that he fashioned this sandalwood image, fully endowed with the eighty minor marks. While remaining without grasping or rejecting in the world, he is yet able to grasp and reject within the world.
The inclinations of sentient beings are diverse and manifold; thus, the Buddha’s transformations also differ accordingly. Sentient beings—
The unfilial were transformed by filial piety; thus, for his mother’s sake, he ascended to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. Sentient beings who lacked compassion were transformed by loving-kindness;

thus, he descended again from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven. The world honored what was heterodox and turned its back on what was correct; therefore, he departed from hegemony and proceeded toward kingship.
Desiring to close off evil and open the Great Path, you manifest such signs of coming and going. I address the assembly of those from the ten directions who gaze upon and pay homage:
those who practice this contemplation are said to contemplate me correctly. Now I prostrate to Śākyamuni, who, in every land and at every atom, grants his testimony.
Wang Zhenpeng personally painted this auspicious image of sandalwood, extolling the Buddha in his celestial palace as he delivers his mother.
King Udayana carved an image that is said to match the true likeness; may these auspicious signs be perpetually transmitted throughout the three thousandfold world system.
Fourteen skilled artisans were carefully selected, yet only the *brahmanic* resonance could not be carved; had it not been for the merit of past lives, one would not behold it.
For what reason? Those who busily seek form and sound miss the Tathāgata’s body of wondrous marks.
King Aśoka, in composing his eulogy for the true-body relic stūpas of the Buddha, cast eighty-four thousand small stūpas from a single crucible; within each stūpa, he enshrined a true relic.
Benefit! Sentient beings together prostrate to the Buddha’s physical form. The Brahma-heaven manifests as a purple-gold realm; its summit is marked by a moon-bright pearl.
We, possessing the karmic affinity, are able to make offerings, so that throughout realms as numerous as motes of dust and sands, we may realize Vairocana.
Praise for the Stūpa of Prabhūtaratna Buddha:
Throughout immeasurable kalpas, the Honored One Prabhūtaratna has remained with his entire body preserved within this stūpa until this very day.

Five thousand railings encircle the chamber, and ten billion golden bells hang from jeweled banners. On this day, they surge forth from the earth to hear the sutra, filling the void as music plays and rain falls.
The flowers are in full bloom. One must know that the two Buddhas sit cross-legged; only when all sentient beings have been saved will they close their gates.

Śākyamuni Buddha praised the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time as sharing a single mind; this single mind is not separated by past, future, or present. Regarding the conditions for Dīpaṃkara’s bestowal of the prediction: there was none.

Attaining it, Prajñā discusses emptiness and sighs over its profound depth; the impoverished son is gathered back into the land of An-yang. At the site of enlightenment, he proclaims the sound of Nirvāṇa;
Yunmen is truly the one who knows how to repay kindness. He understands how to apply the needle to the painful spot within the stream of Chan.
A Hymn to Amitāyus Buddha:

How pitiable are the sentient beings of this defiled and evil age! If they do not cast themselves upon the Compassionate Father, to whom else shall they turn? His single teaching gathers the multitudes of the Three Vehicles;
The nine grades of lotuses bloom within the Seven-Jeweled Pond. Having attained Buddhahood after immeasurable kalpas, He remains present at the moment of one’s final passing.
At that time, the Gate of Vows, six-eight spans wide, will admit those who enter; all who enter shall become world-transcending teachers.

Maitreya, the Honored Buddha, praised Maitreya, asking when he would not descend to be born; throughout the human and celestial realms, his name alone is invoked. At the break of dawn, the monastery first opens its gates.

Entering [the path], Perfect Enlightenment suddenly heard that the evening scene was complete. Though the three assemblies for saving beings have their limits, the single mind that acts as a Buddha has no set course.
From the very beginning, he cultivated compassion and forbearance in every thought; thus the great earth, mountains, and rivers became as level as the palm of his hand.
Eulogy on the First Patriarch, Mahākāśyapa:
In the past, when the Tathāgata was about to pass into parinirvāṇa, he earnestly charged him to uphold and transmit the Dharma of the robes.

A peerless master whose ascetic practices were perfected, he was like a second branch of the *utpala* flower blooming. At Mount Kukkuṭapāda, he awaits Maitreya; at the assembly of the Dragon Flower, he shall entrust [the teaching].
Kāli! In a single thought-moment spanning past and present, one transcends the three periods of time; that the patriarchs and Buddhas have transmitted the faith lies herein.

To the second patriarch, the Venerable Ānanda, who was the peer and successor to the Wheel-Turning King and the Dharma King—my first teacher, the most learned among men—I offer praise at the foot of the Pipphali Cave, where all taints have ceased.
Exhausted. How many lifetimes has it been held within the Sūtra-piṭaka? Coming from kalpas of antiquity without transmission, it proclaims the Three Vehicles as they are established.
One can only laugh at those who recite the *Shao* while forgetting the broom, yet claim that a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru.

Eulogy of the Third Patriarch, Śāṇakavāsin: The nine-branch lush grass robe appeared spontaneously; even before emerging from the womb, he had already donned it. In the past, the World-Honored One once prophesied:
"After a hundred years, who else shall be the Arhat? Only then did the Fire Dragon believe in the greatness of his compassion; his supernormal powers arose because of his lack of indolence.
Generosity through pride; ultimately there is neither mind nor dharma. What prevents a disciple from going to seek a teacher?
The Fourth Patriarch Upagupta was seventeen years old when he praised his own nature.
At that time, everyone who reached this point fell into deep reflection; it was truly difficult to open one's eyes before such a sight.

The mouth speaks; the whiteness of hair has long been unrelated to the mind. When the study hall is filled with counting-sticks, many scholars arrive; when the three corpses fall from the crown, the myriad demons pay homage.
Among my disciples, many are like lost swords; one must simply seek them by looking at the marks carved upon the gunwale.
The Fifth Patriarch, Diṭṭhagāmaṇi, did not seek his own liberation through body or mind; who then shall succeed and uphold the lineage of the Buddha? Point clearly toward the path ahead of the sound;
take care not to plant flowers in the eye. Dreaming that the sun rises high above the roof, one follows the assembly of immortals to their end.
Eliminate deviance. At the very first thought, it must be true and correct; simply endure the divergences that arise during the intervening stages of retribution.

The Sixth Patriarch, Micchaka, praised the state where there is no mind, no dharma, and no teacher: "Once awakened, it is the same as when one has not yet awakened. If you do not perceive this gate, you will form attachments.

Liberated! I have entirely forgotten my encounter with Asita in a previous kalpa; now, fortunately, I have emptied myself of all outflows (*āsrava*). As I approach extinction, why should I not reveal one marvel?
To sever the cycle of birth and death is itself the goal. You eight thousand companions of the immortals, do not harbor any doubt.
The Seventh Patriarch Vasumitra:
