Originally there is not a single thing—what is transmitted outside the teachings? When I first entered the Great Tang, my eyes could not see my own nostrils; now as I return to Japan, my feet...
Do not step across the gunwale. The mud-bull entering the sea rushes like lightning; the wooden horse running along the river flows like smoke.
To the Chan practitioner Wén of Tīngzhōu:

when Bodhidharma came from the West, he did not establish written words. To "see one's nature and clarify the mind" already falls into the secondary. Only that which transcends the ordinary deserves the name.
O practitioners of the Way! You must sit and sever the heads of both the *nirmāṇakāya* and *saṃbhogakāya* Buddhas; otherwise, you will have sand in your eyes. How can one grasp the moon in water?
The number of venerable elders in all quarters is like the sands of the Ganges, and students carrying their staffs follow them like ants swarming toward food.

Cast aside that first principle of Nārāyaṇa; everything else is merely superfluous furniture. Travelling across the four seas in search of spiritual friends, they discuss the profound and speak of the wondrous, yet it is all empty.
Exerting effort, one must directly penetrate the ancient Vimalakīrti. A single phrase, suddenly realized, transcends billions of worlds. From Tingzhou and Quanzhou to Fujian;
from Mingzhou, Yuezhou, Wenzhou, and Taizhou—every gate stands wide open, every dharma is fully encompassed. Mice run about the ground;
seize a cat and bring it here!
Seeing off Zen Practitioner Yu back to Sanping:
Before one’s parents were born, there was this excellent original face. In daily life, how has it ever been lacking? Who says this matter is insufficient?
The mountains are green and the waters are lush; rising early and retiring late, the crow does not need to be blackened by the sun.
The crane does not bathe daily. When you hold a staff, simply call it a staff; when you have a house, simply call it a house.
Do not inquire about the Zen of the Tathāgata or the Zen of the Patriarchs. It is like the rustic songs and the "Spring Breeze" melodies. Long ago, Sanping saw Dadian:
a broken string must await the phoenix-glue to be mended.
Sending off the Abbot Hongzang back to Mount Jing: A Note to the Head Seat Xibai.
Reaching the highest peak, one gazes upon the green mountains as white clouds arise. Clouds and mountains emerge and vanish like surging waves;
who can know how many layers of the Great Flower Treasury Sea (Mahāpuṣpa-garbha-loka-dhātu) there are? Layer upon layer they encircle Mount Lingxiao, like Mount Sumeru.
The absolute summit is just this: when Kāśyapa hears the golden bell struck, throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of worlds, there is not a single thing to be grasped by the hand.
Tied together as a single brush made of tortoise hair, how can one write even a single character at the beginning of a sutra?
Written with clarity and spoken with intimacy; I restore the eyes to the person, the celestial and human beings.
Sending Zen person Shun of Goryeo back to his homeland:
taking a single step within the body of Samantabhadra, one transcends Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Only yesterday did he leave the seacoast.
Come. This very morning we shall go to Goryeo. How does this Zhejiang of mine differ from your own land? In winter’s cold one sits by the fire; in summer’s heat one seeks the cool breeze.
For those who have realized their fundamental mind, every single thing is the Way; for those who obscure their true nature, they are lost in confusion at every turn.

Before one's parents were born, what hardship was there for him to bear? He merely carried a skin-sack. When Sudhana visited spiritual friends, he paid homage to Mañjuśrī and sought out Maitreya, yet he did not know [the Way].
Once he lets go of the mind that runs toward seeking, there is no news from within, without, or in between.

Sometimes wandering among the mountains, sometimes facing a wall; sometimes extending his hands into the void, sometimes concealing his brilliance and hiding his traces—thus forging ordinary beings into saints.
In but a moment, it supports the earth and props up the heavens—how extraordinary! Zen student Shun, you must understand this thoroughly: the red sun shines in mid-spring;
the clear breeze arises from the eight directions.
Seeing Off Chief Seat Qin on His Return to the South:
When the Sixth Patriarch arrived at Guangzhou, he stayed at Zhengfaxing Temple. There, he briefly discussed the dialogue concerning the wind and the banner with two monks.
From this point, the tangled vines were drawn forth and spread across the lands of the South Sea; later generations failed to uproot them, so that year after year they grew more and more.

Cherish these words, O Zen Master Qin: you possess a truly heroic spirit. You have traveled to various quarters without ever gaining anything; you have questioned the Dharma, yet remained entirely without understanding.
I guarantee this person. They sit loftily upon the seat of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.

To send an attendant to inquire, one must inquire with true inquiry; to awaken, one must awaken with true awakening. What a fine monk! If you go forth in this manner, you will be in the assembly at Vulture Peak.
A person is always a celestial qilin. A hundred or a thousand years of stagnant goods; handled with increasing spirit, one misses Zhaozhou’s Chan and is laughed at by Wenyuan.
Competing in inferiority rather than superiority, one ends up stuck in donkey dung. Reflecting on this old "iron hammer," a branch grows from beyond the joints.
With a single stroke, everything is crossed out—only then is one a true "kitchen-stepper. This is the White Snow of my own house.
Song: Furthermore, let the man of high realization be at peace. When Buddhas and Patriarchs appear, they all submit to his authority.
Verse for Sending Off Attendant Ning on His Pilgrimage to Pay Homage to the Patriarchs:
Within the assembly of Buddhas and Patriarchs, there is no fixed rank. When traveling on pilgrimage, whose business is it? To follow a single thought as it arises is already a deviation.

"Zhang! Do not seek the ultimate meaning within the gates of Chan. You must know that for those who are true sons of the Way, they forget their own concerns everywhere out of compassion for themselves and others.
They take up boiling bubbles to fill their bowls, yet return to plant lotus flowers upon rocks. The National Teacher called his attendant three times;
the attendant responded three times. "Call! Respond! Head straight, tail straight. To seek a teacher, one must surely reach the source. This is the secret.
The clear and bright intention resides within you; on the day you return, there will be no point of convergence. You must suffer the full force of the Patriarch’s fist.
Regarding the Dharma-gate of the Mind-Ground for sending off the Abbot Xuedou Rong back to his country:
it is not obtained from others. To go directly like this would leave one as far apart as heaven and earth—this is the Lion’s way of teaching its cub.
Able to throw it back; when the antelope hangs from its horns, there is no trace. "The character 'yi' is not it. The eight characters are not the Awakened Heaven.

The sun and moon increase their brilliance. At the top of a hundred-foot pole, five *liang* hang down. The Great Tang returns once more to Fusang. Fire is hot, wind moves, water is moist, and earth is solid.
Breaking through the Iron Ring Mountains, there is no different path throughout past and present. As you depart—
What need is there for further instructions?
Send the attendant to visit various quarters;
the Buddha-dharma is omnipresent. Amidst the vast and chaotic multitude, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, one may suddenly encounter it and call it forth.
Return! Piercing clouds and crossing waters, I follow you; A hat upon my head, a bundle at my waist. I carry the clear wind and bright moon upon my staff.
Never having bitten through a single grain of rice, Even ten thousand taels of gold would be worth it. Open the gate, and you must recognize the master;
If we know each other well, why need there be a formal introduction? Leaning back against the Dharma Hall while wearing straw sandals— This was never within the confines of a secret chamber.
A private conversation: The mountain is not yet high, and the sea is not yet deep. Zhaozhou Wen Yuan’s zither without strings—its public verification was clear at that time;
who in the four seas can recognize this mind?
I am sending the Great Canon of the Dharma to the Abbot Yuecang; it speaks of nothing but this. Whether East Land or West Heaven, they are clearly seen through.
Now, I take hundreds of thousands of millions of Jambudvīpas and hang them upon the corner of my bed; what need is there to distinguish between Silla and Japan?

The Buddha’s vow flows through Lufu (Liuqiu). It is vast and tumultuous, yet cool and still. Sometimes it releases, sometimes it gathers; its gathering and releasing are纵横 (unrestricted) and entirely without hindrance.
Its rolling up and unfolding, its appearing and disappearing, are always free. Who says there is no offering when a guest arrives?
It does not hinder the bowl being filled with parched bubbles.
The Chan practitioner Dao-ren, Zhi, has come to me three times; only now does he finally request my long verse. This matter is clear and distinct right before one’s eyes.

When asked why he must act so abruptly, [the answer is that] the ten directions are already present before one’s eyes, and the Great Way is fundamentally not outside of things. If you understand this, then...
If you understand, then Ganmu plays his part wherever he encounters the stage; even if you do not understand, there is no lack.
This is entirely one’s own livelihood: treading upon the crown of all Buddhas’ heads and pulling out the patriarchs' nostrils.
The four great oceans stand like walls, and the five Mount Sumerus are pulverized. What a fine great man! He can truly add vigor to the Zen groves.
Seeing off the Zen practitioner Wu Zhongzi: Suzhou is here, Changzhou is there; clearly, face south and look at the Big Dipper. Master and attendants come forth in this manner;
the elephant king turns in circles, the lion roars. When you eat salt, you perceive its saltiness; when you eat vinegar, you perceive its sourness. One becomes many; two.
There are not two kinds. Speaking of food with the mouth never satisfies; only by wearing clothes upon the body is one freed from cold.
Have you not seen that the mountain of the Daoist home is a fine mountain? Within that mountain grows rootless grass; it is the month of the twelfth lunar month, yet it is truly spring wind.
The five petals and single flower’s fragrance remain unfulfilled.
Sent to Hai, the Venerable of Zhongzhu:
may you contemplate non-arising, empty the ocean of existence, sit and sever the path of Śākyamuni, and completely transcend Avalokiteśvara. —Zhongfeng.
The sounding of the *ghanṭā* atop the head causes all people throughout the great earth to sever their doubts. Venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya possesses a point of excellence;

to whom can this single phrase be clearly presented? Whether sitting, reclining, walking, or pacing; whether rolling up or unfolding, emerging or submerging—the mechanism of "biting the arrowhead" is like a flash of lightning.
The gods of the Thirty-three Heavens build a ball of air; with both hands supporting the plow, the water reaches his knees.
Presented to the Abbot Huizang of Guangnan:
A single bright pearl from the deep sea. Within the Tathāgatagarbha it remains deeply locked;
suddenly it emerges from the tip of the staff, illuminating thousands of myriads of mountains and rivers. If you ask what color this pearl is, it is perfectly round and luminous.
Vividly clear: south of the Southern Mountain, north of the Northern Mountain—directly pointing it out, yet people do not recognize it. Return!
Return! It remains hanging high upon the Terrace of King Yue.
I send this Zen person to Zhedong, to take another step beyond the hundred-foot pole. At every household door lies the road to Chang’an.

The waters of Zhexi and the mountains of Zhedong leave even those with hawk-eyes and dragon-vision utterly at a loss. Not recognizing the Buddha as Buddha, they ride a donkey while searching for a donkey. I, now—
Going alone, one encounters the "He" (the True Self) wherever one goes. There is no need to add feet to a painted snake; six times six is originally thirty-six.
Sent for Dong Shi-zhe to T'ien-p'ing.
The Peak of the Balanced Table and the Brush is most extraordinary. Upon entering the gate, one beholds the stele of Fushan. Among its nine bands, not even ten reach completion;
those who read it cannot help but harbor doubts in their hearts. This venerable monk comes from the land of Fusang; he is accustomed to seeing the lapis lazuli sky submerged in azure.
At midnight, the golden cock crows but once, and both nostrils and eyes are utterly lost. He has traveled far and wide across the East and West.
North and south, as before, there is nowhere to find traces of his path.
Seeing off Master Chang, the autumn wind is cool;
the autumn nights are long. In the well, the wutong trees shed their withered leaves; on the crags, the osmanthus sprays its fragrant scent. Do not treat this as mere worldly convention.
Circulate this! Most strictly, do not engage in intellectual deliberation regarding the Buddha-dharma. If you proceed thus, the jade palaces and crystal towers have never required a roof.

If you do not proceed thus, the silver mountains and iron walls suddenly obstruct and conceal. Cutting off both extremes, moving freely in all ten directions—look instead at the old Venerable with the Long Eyebrows, who sat cross-legged and never once descended from his meditation seat.
Sent to Attendant Wanshou Tong:
His entire body is it; his whole being is it. Cast aside the "True Person of No Station" and cut off the self of the empty kalpa.
On the single path beyond, there is no room for deliberation. What need is there to seek out empty flowers or mirages? Why further search for snake's feet or salt-fragrance? Mid-winter.
The bitter cold has passed; in early summer, the heat gradually increases. From antiquity to the present, who has been skillful and who has been clumsy?
When Niaoke blew up his cloth-hair, it was like driving a nail straight through with an axe—decisive and unyielding. If you practitioners have any doubts, go home and ask Chan Yue.
Seeing off Daozang, the Abbot of Jingci, as he returns to Jingde:
The Yellow-Faced Gautama did not move his tongue, yet for forty-nine years he spoke at length and in all directions.
Who is it that has repeatedly entangled himself in these complications? In the end, there is no second moon in the sky. Yiyuan recently left Nanping; I suddenly ask him to look.
How wondrous! In this state of mere silence with palms joined, the blue sky and bright sun resound with thunder and lightning.

Old Dragon Bay, Old Dragon Bay—when uncle and nephew forget themselves, their affinity is all the more profound. When the luminous pearl of the ocean is sought, he pours it out for him, a full measure.

I bid farewell to Old Yū, a man of true substance who dwells among the mountains like a monk of the Western Hall; he bears not even a trace of axe or hatchet. For thirty years such as these, his reputation for the Way has filled the heavens and the earth.
Arranged below are the successive Buddhas and Patriarchs from antiquity; with the Mount Sumeru mallet, they beat the drum of empty space and fully reveal it.
The Lord among Lords facing the sun—there is no need to discuss the Lord, nor is there any need to boast of the Guest. With the bamboo stick of Wondrous Joy, some are struck and others touched;
who can scatter earth and further throw sand? When meeting rice, eat the rice; when meeting tea, drink the tea. Thus do brothers meet one another.
Abundance or frugality follows one’s household circumstances. A white ox in the open field, content with sweet water and grass, need not hinder one from gathering a little bit everywhere.
When the Great Being Zongzang, the Abbot, brandished his ruler once, Zhaozhou circled the bed once. How much entanglement has there been throughout the ages! These two elders—
Cut it off at the head! Master Baohua Zang has thoroughly saturated the monastic groves; he has traveled far in search of friends and teachers over many years.
In the twelfth month, flowers bloom upon the shadowless tree; in the springtime, a melody is played on the stringless lute. The east wind blows fiercely, the east wind blows fiercely;

above, below, and in the four cardinal directions, nothing can penetrate him. He has completely trampled the blue sky beneath the waters; when has he ever been so careless as to let his shoes get wet?
When sending off the Venerable Administrator Zhengshou, do not bow your head;
it is difficult to find such a person through mere deliberation. Truth does not conceal falsehood, and the crooked cannot hide the straight.

The Buddha-work of sound and voice flows forth, casting wide open the threshold of the sages and worthies. Dongshan’s "three pounds of flax" and Yunmen’s "dry dung"—these have already been scrutinized.
Coming from all directions, how can it ultimately be described? The staff is like a dragon, lively and darting; held crosswise or used upside down, heaven and earth are vast.
I see you off, Elder Shou of Jingci, as you return to Japan.
The moon atop Mount Fuji; the water upon the Dragon’s Creek. The moon does not come here, nor does the water go there.
Precisely at the moment when water and moon reflect each other’s radiance, ten thousand miles have never been separated by so much as a single thread.

The stone woman weaves fire-washed cloth; the mud ox tramples through coral branches. Whether there is a Buddha or no Buddha, both are but deceptions; whether it is this mind or not this mind, it is all exhausted.
The same applies to slander. The net of the teachings is spread wide, yet one has not yet entered its depths; the direct pointing of the ancestral gate remains a drifting current.
Thus it is said: "The Eye of the True Dharma breaks the sand pot; this Way of antiquity resounds through heaven and earth. Though gold fills the nation, it is difficult to repay its price;
it is entrusted to the true bone-descendant who dwells in stillness. When the patriarchal hall raises it up, all is shattered into fragments—do not allow yourself to be burdened by him.
Cast it beyond that side, and even further beyond. Ordinarily, simply maintain a state of leisurely ease. It is just so—truly marvelous!

The great masters of all quarters find this most laughable; it is like feeding a baby with someone else’s chewed rice. I only fear that Śakra and Brahmā will descend from the void, for the *tánhuá* (rare lotus) blooms once more without artifice.
Sending off Chan Master Zishou, Guest Prefect of Linji:
The Master’s words on guest and host. Zhaozhou, upon seeing a monk, said, “Go drink tea. A whirlwind rests immovably atop his head;
he has traversed the ends of the earth without shifting a step. Nine times nine is eighty-one from the start; in his ordinary life, he reveals the primordial source even more.
Dense and pervasive. A manly son who props up heaven and supports the earth; his hands and eyes manifest throughout his entire being, brilliant as the sun.
Sending Guest Master Cheng of Jiangshan to the top of Dulong Peak, beneath Tiaozhu Peak: When a guest comes, you must look upon them; when a thief comes, you must strike him. Return to the ancients!
The wind and regulations extol the Dharma-society of ascending peace. Once the lion’s claws have been displayed, the antelope’s horns are hung up.
Being able to harmonize with the light and become one with the dust, one may naturally forget all emotion and sever all conceptual understanding.
A gnat swallows Mount Sumeru; the thatched hut sheds its lapis lazuli tiles.
I send this to the Zen Master Ishō of Japan:

The matter within one’s own person is fundamentally clear and plain. Yet, when a thought stirs, it becomes separated by clouds and water. The Old Barbarian (the Buddha) needlessly crossed the shifting sands himself;
he did not understand that single stroke right before his eyes. Day after day the sun rises in the east; day after day the sun sets in the west. Of what use is it?
There is speech with a mouth; no strings, and it is truly a zither. When a man of the Way holds a staff in his hand, he strikes across the spine of both the holy and the ordinary.
He turns the Rising Sun back to become the Great Tang, startling the Dharmakāya from its hiding place in the Northern Dipper.

To the Abbot Fuzang of Lingyin: When the three karmas are pure, the Buddha appears in the world; at every step, one treads upon the golden ground. When the three karmas are impure, the Buddha enters nirvana;
on the golden ground, it is difficult to take even a single step. Thus and so it is: when manifest before one’s eyes, it is brilliantly clear; yet it is not thus.
Not so. The entire world is shrouded in pitch-black gloom. When the two secure gates are broken through, the seas hidden for a thousand miles dry up.
Which of these is bodhi and which is affliction? What can be called birth-and-death and what nirvana? All the people of the great earth stare with bated breath;
the moonlight upon Flying Peak chills the bones.
Sending Attendant Liang to travel among the masters, the National Teacher called out to the attendant three times; the attendant responded three times. The earthworm passes over the Eastern Sea;
the lotus fiber pierces through Mount Sumeru. From of old, this Way has neither beginning nor end; without stirring a speck of dust, it transcends Buddhas and Patriarchs. To be deluded—ah!
What need is there to speak of awakening? Whether in speech or silence, look for yourself. Day and night the spring breeze blows through heaven and earth;
in every place, the gardens and groves turn crimson and emerald. Each and every thing is interlaced like the pearls of Indra’s net; at every point, the assembly on Vulture Peak is revealed.
"Ha! Before Chief Seat Guan reached Yunmen, he had already seen Master Zhisheng at Lingshu; the Chief Seat has realized the Way. One couplet.
A seamless iron hammer: before it there is no Śākyamuni; after it there is no Maitreya. The Sage is truly difficult to know;
how can an ordinary person fathom him? But tell me, what have you awakened to? A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech. In the seventh and eighth months, the autumn wind is cool;
through a thousand mountains and ten thousand peaks, the traveler’s road is long. Sitting cross-legged within the Taiping Hermitage, acting spontaneously—there is nothing that cannot be done.
I have sent Attendant Zhan of Shuanglin here;
he comes in this very way, and he departs in this very way. Buddhas and patriarchs do not act for the sake of others; from ancient times to the present, there has been no divergent path.
Ordinarily, he eats rice and congee; why wait for him to speak of nature or mind? He sits upright while receiving offerings, consuming ten thousand taels of gold daily.
Even if one were to overturn the Great Tang Empire and search for a single person who understands the Buddha-dharma, not one could be found.
I see two clay oxen fighting their way into the sea; even until now, there has been no news.
To send off the Abbot Juzu of Lingyin with hot water from Cold Spring—this vast and long tongue flows on day and night without ceasing, yet in the end, one knows not where it leads.
The preaching is complete; the scroll ends at five thousand and forty-eight [characters]. How can one listen with the faculty of hearing thus blocked?
When listening with perfect clarity, the path of the mind is severed. Where the path of the mind is severed, the True Eye opens: the lantern climbs the wall toward the terrace.
When Mowei-na Yunfeng was sent to visit Cuiyan, he entered the room with sincere devotion. Surely he did not lack the mouth born of his mother; yet the Master refused to speak for him.

One day, the wooden band on a water jar burst, and sweat broke out over his entire body. He threw open his robe and went up to the abbot’s quarters; truly, one may rejoice that the Great Matter was finished.
"You came from Mount Xiang yourself to ask me for the essential instructions. I set you among miscellaneous tasks, and you have been preoccupied with them for years.

Now that you have abandoned the site of construction, I have appointed you to the position of *karmadāna*. When your term is complete and you wish to travel abroad to seek the Way, you must rely upon a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)."
From West River back to East Zhejiang—after all, by whose power was this sustained?
To the attendant Long:
This matter is clear; it is neither transmitted nor received. A single point of numinous light has existed from time immemorial. Śākyamuni and Kāśyapa share the same void.
Emptiness. What trace remains of Shen Guang of Shaoshi? I owe you, and you owe me. The attendant answered three times to the National Teacher’s call.
I am in the Great Tang; you are in Japan. At midnight, a golden old crow flies out.
To the Abbot Run of Ruiyan in Siming:

From the very beginning, there has not been a single dharma; The oceanic mouth cannot proclaim it. The frosty wind sweeps away the yellow leaves— To call this "money to stop a child's crying" is a mere convention.
If you encounter a person with clear vision, set it aside for a moment. Smash the mani jewel; let an iron ship float upon the great ocean.
If you can leave both hands empty, you will not be entangled by external objects. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—wherever you are, there is no place that is not meditation.
As I see off Chief Librarian Jiuzang on his journey to Tiantai and Yandangshan, buddha after buddha hands it down;
patriarch after patriarch transmits it. Facing south, one gazes at the Northern Dipper; carving into stone, one plants red lotuses.
With a single breath, one turns the entire Great Canon. Water flows to the moist and fire seeks the dry; ten thousand miles of wind carries the Peng-bird across the sea. How many times!

For years I have been like a leopard hidden in the mountain mists; I have done nothing that adds anything, and I have acted without acting. I uproot suffering and bestow joy; I give rise to loving-kindness and exercise compassion.
Having found the honeyed fruit atop the Huangbo tree, I carry it home in a bottomless basket.

It is right here—cease all picking and choosing! New Gao-li lies to the east of the sea; Japan has many merchant ships. When the bow is drawn and the arrow drinks the feathers, both banks are reached at once.

Mysterious! The stone whips upward with a roar, yet not a hair’s breadth separates them. Clouds float over Mount Tai, dotting the sky with azure; the moon drifts over the Sheng River, spreading a vast expanse of white.
Farewell, Attendant Xuan, as you return to your native village.
When Niaoke blew on a piece of cloth, someone immediately attained awakening. Now, what is it like? As numerous as the sands of the Ganges, those who are coarse and muddled.
Since Chan Master Xuan was so preeminent, he must have understood the phrase that transcends the ordinary. Seeing forms and hearing sounds—this cannot be a second time.
The autumn wind blows through the osmanthus; its tangles of blossoms open across the entire tree. Suddenly, amidst a dream, I smell its fragrance; upon waking, there is no place to find it.
Turning over, I reach for my pillow—only to realize it is made of nothing but wood. To accept things just as they are in this way is like traversing the layered mountain passes.
I replied: "Master Daochang of Qingyuan is a dragon among my nephews in the Sangha.
He bestows the rain of the Dharma upon all people; though their faculties may be sharp or dull, his mind is fundamentally without discrimination."
A cliff standing ten thousand fathoms high reveals the green mountains ever alone. Who says there are masters and disciples? This matter must be transmitted in secret.
Bodhidharma did not understand Zen; Miaoxi was likewise no patriarch. Everywhere is a site of enlightenment—why trouble oneself to distinguish subject and object?
Exert yourself from this very day! Take high strides to follow the ancients.
Entrusted to the mountain master Nisun Jing, I have a single mechanism:
held up in its entirety toward the ultimate, it transcends Buddhas and patriarchs; it is the Sumeru Mountain within the sea, above heaven and below heaven.
Those who know this are few. When one hesitates, the blow falls upon the spine. The Venerable Master Wuzu Deng swept away the Linji lineage;
Yuanwu and Dahui were each dragons producing dragons. There was a nun, Wuzhuo, whose correct pulse flows to this day.
Always manifest before us throughout past and present—look, what kind of standard is this?
Sending off Master Zunjang of the Meditation Hall:
The mind is not the Buddha; wisdom is not the Way. In the heavens above or the world below, where can one seek it?
This year, at sixty-eight, I am clearly both old and yet not old. How shameful that we, as men of the green mountains, gaze upon one another in this desolate place.
He asked me about a most extraordinary matter: "A wind-chasing iron horse wears a *qilin* saddle. Last night the lunar disc was as hot as fire;
it scorched the crows until they were white as snow. This natural, wondrous, and inconceivable reality—its essential principle is pointed out in a single phrase, penetrating one beneath the words."

To send forth this wisdom-gate, the eye of the Way possesses three angles: its peak is as steep as the Five Marchmounts; withered trees are strewn with blossoms, and hailstones fall from a scorching sky.

Having mastered the art of untying adhesions and removing fetters, there is no need to lengthen the ducks or shorten the cranes. Such a person, such a Way—once in a thousand years! The face of the sun, the face of the moon.
Face-to-face, past and present; after the phrase, before the sound—none can fathom it. At the blow of the staff and the shout, there is ultimately no partiality.
Have you not seen Old Zhimen play a single melody? Once the strings are snapped, who else is left to continue?
The lotus flower and its leaves are perfectly clear; this too is a response to your inverted desires.
To instruct his disciples:
when traveling to various quarters, you must go wherever one person resides; you must also go wherever half a person resides. Upon entering the gate, do not ask who the host is.
Observe their opening of the mouth to grasp the essential pivot. If there is a single word of accord, enter the hall immediately; do not shrink from hardship or toil.
Neighborhoods. Sewing a cloth bag to carry provisions for the midday meal; morning attendance and evening invitations to hear the Dharma being proclaimed.
Leaving home is intended solely to realize the mind-ground; one never seeks fame or profit from others. All the ancient worthies came from this very path;

those born later must surely look up to them as they would a steed. A stone of Mount Tai is worn through by dripping water; the peach of longevity blooms only once every three thousand years. Suddenly—
Fire burns beneath the waters; at that time, he returned and received a painful blow from the fist.
From the seven Buddhas of antiquity down to the present, there have always been attendants to assist and support the patriarchs, thereby establishing the Dharma community. Xianglin was in Shaozhou.
Yang heard the instruction to "steal in the dark. When Linji tested Luopu, he seized his staff and struck him, resolving to sever the life-force of intellectual understanding.
How could he ever be willing to mistake a servant for a lord, or follow others in taking a deer to be a horse? Lately, such people have come to be carried by carts and measured by bushels.
To speak at length would be like clouds arising and water pouring from a vase. Fortunately, the Chan of spring is naturally heroic and spirited. One’s realization must be free and unencumbered;
suddenly, the radiance becomes grand and flourishing, whereupon one may perceive its elegance and refinement. Why is this? *Asafetida* has no counterfeit; mercury has no imitation.
When the attendant Jin sent Shushan away to sell his cotton robe and travel on foot for three thousand li, he suddenly smashed the lacquer bucket;
it was as if a tiger’s head had grown horns. Chan Master Jin came specifically to the Central Plains, cutting through the currents of the vast ocean for thirty thousand li—how can one fail to laugh?
A blind donkey runs with the great crowd; holding his staff upside down, it whistles through the wind. Beyond the land of Fusang, the single orb of the sun does not rise until well after dusk.
[Zhi] blinding the top-knot eye of Mahesvara, there are no patriarchs or Buddhas in this land or in the Western Heaven.
The Head Seat, a man of the Way, has come from Japan to see me off. What will he carry across the sea? If there is a word, it involves deliberation; if there is no word, it becomes an obstruction.
It is like the King of Golden-Winged Birds soaring atop the peak of Mount Sumeru; do not emulate the dull bird that dwells in reeds and flies low.
Merely attached to the pond. How is the Mahāyāna Dharma explained? It transcends the four propositions and is beyond the hundred negations.
Willow filaments dance in the azure mist; plum blossoms fall, scattering fragrant snow.
To the Venerable Kuan, Rector:
The Buddhas of the three periods do not know "there is. Each one faces south and gazes at the Big Dipper; yet the cat and the white ox know "there is.
Having grasped the nostrils, they have lost their mouths. Before the golden mallet within the sleeve is raised, it clearly transcends Vaiśālī.

Lushi was suddenly reduced to a hundred fragments in a single blow; Shih Hu spat out the wooden sheep. "Qu-qu-qu, wo-wo-wo"—in every turn, movement, bowing, and rising, there is nothing that is not permissible.
Having recognized the transmission of the Patriarch’s intent from the West, one sees a peak of green mountains amidst the shadows of white clouds.
A few dozen lines of short verse and two or three words of long prose to see off Attendant Zhi—neither long nor short. A spark from flint leaping into the blue sky:
when Yuanwu served as an attendant, how could he have ever mastered Zen? At that time, Master Deng was not free from partiality in his own views.

When the Dharma has endured long, it eventually falls into decay; one must forget both the fish and the trap. Later generations run in pursuit of the crowd, wrapping themselves in paper while still bound by hempen cords.

For decisive discernment to be clear and bright, the dynamic function of unfolding and rolling up must be complete. A man of the Way is such from the very beginning; he can shoulder the Buddhas and patriarchs.

A fine steed does not submit to the halter; it soars and gallops along the long road of its own accord. Covering thirty thousand li in a single day, it traverses the eight extremities of the world in an instant.
The wondrous joy of the stinking leather shoes, the *vajra-circle* of Yangqi, and the orthodox eye of the True Dharma of Linji—all these have been extinguished within the jaws of the blind donkey.
The nostrils are roughly visible; who among all quarters would dare to pierce them?
Presented to the former Xiyin, Yujian, for his blood-written *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*:
The Vairocana-nature-sea has no boundless limit. It is neither ancient nor modern, neither Great nor Small. At times, it can be gathered into a single hair-tip.
The head; blood dripping as it is swept away. At times he extends his broad and long tongue; though he rolls up a hundred scrolls, his proclamation is not yet finished.
The old man of Jade Stream, the treasure of Golden Creek—this likeness of the Tathāgata is fashioned within the heart.

Good Wealth (Sudhana) still does not know where to turn; crossing waters and piercing clouds, he searches in vain. Flowers bloom upon the steps, reflecting in the curtains; the porcelain bowl is white as snow, filled with incense.
Swaying and drifting. The one who naturally awakens dwells within this; ultimately, they do not follow others as they strike or circle about.
This verse in rhyme is presented to Shi-ca Yan-shi of Xi-yin Bai-shi, and Wu-yen of Jin-su.
They share the same root and are of one accord; they uproot the foundation and block the source. Hearing what is unheard, seeing...
There is no view. It is like casting a single drop of a lion’s blood into six bushels of donkey’s milk; the milk scatters like stars. Within one's own storehouse is a *maṇi* jewel;
one must know it does not reside within the dragon palaces. The breast and mind are vast and open; the brows and countenance are radiant and moist.
A half-scoop from the blue ocean, a speck of dust upon the great earth—this causes Flying Eagle Peak to leap and bound, and the rain to overturn the basin beneath the valley thundering pavilion.
