Verses on the Three Attendants, compiled by Wenbin and others,
presented to Dharma Master Tiyi of Wutai.
There is but one Mañjuśrī; there is no second Mañjuśrī. Yet hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, millions, and billions of him fill every corner of the dusty world.
Sometimes he appears as an old man, sometimes as a youth; sometimes he dwells in mountain forests, sometimes in the bustling markets.

At times he rides a lion, traversing the void; at other times he manifests radiance rising from the earth. For long has the Dharma Master resided on Mount Wutai, his pair of pure eyes forever wide open.
Though gold is precious, it cannot be worn; the six classes of ordinary beings and the four types of noble ones are all but dust.

Now, do not dwell upon them with thought; at the gates of the six sense-faculties, all is empty and desolate. Do not sit in meditation, nor read the sutras; the white clouds are naturally white, and the green mountains are naturally green.
After the meal, walk once around the corridor, and in a single kṣaṇa, the vow for Bodhi is fulfilled.
I send my disciple, Secretary Xian, to travel among the masters.
In his day, Luopu’s departure from Linji was no ordinary red carp; before he had fallen into the pickle-pot of Jia Shan, he would have been well-supported by a resounding shout.
Master Xian planted his staff by the banks of the Qin River, and through repeated cycles of cold and heat, he has forgotten himself.
How arduous! Why should the monastic groves alone value reputation and integrity? It is clear that parents are not one's true kin.

Huanglong was merely Nan’s secretary; though his virtue and learning could have brought fame to the age, it was left to the direct old Yangqi to let his inner spirit flow forth, covering heaven and earth.
I send my attendant to travel to Tiantai.
Tiantai rises eighteen thousand *zhang*; viewed with the True Eye, it is as level as the palm of a hand. There is no need to traverse winding paths or forked trails;

in every speck of dust and every world-system, all is the vast expanse of the Dharma-realm. With a bamboo hat upon his head and a pack at his waist, he wanders forever through green waters and blue mountains.
Yao: A patch-robed monk is fundamentally without fetters; even ten thousand taels of gold would be fit for him to consume.
This is the foremost medicine for true realization sent to the Abbot Ying of Huqiu. For one who is a person of transcendent capacity, their mind is naturally luminous and vast.
At Tiger Hill, he swept away the teachers of false views; with the flash of lightning and the spark from flint, he revealed his prior mastery.
All clever monks were dealt with directly and decisively—there was no need to ask what time it was now. From this moment on, the Great Canon and the Minor Canon have departed;
how could there be any place for the root-faculty to take firm stand? On the crossroads stands a bottomless shoe; upon the thousand-year-old rock grows a rootless tree.
Seeing off the Abbot Hai of Jingci at the gate of Yongming, there was a lake before him. "The fragrance of its lotuses extends ten li;

the Buddhas of the three periods have never reached it, and the entire Tripitaka cannot lift it up. Zen practitioners are not permitted to take this upon themselves recklessly; rather, it is empty space that understands."
Proclaiming it aloud: with the faculty of hearing blocked, where can one listen? Without moving the tongue, the words flow resonantly.
Contemplate carefully the verse of the Master in the Hall; do not attempt to understand it through petty, dualistic consciousness. Yesterday there was rain, today it is sunny;
when Mr. Zhang drinks, Mr. Li gets drunk.
I send the attendant Yin to travel to Mount Nanyue.
Have you not seen how Mazu sat in meditation, intending to become a Buddha? Alas, why seek out such a nest?
Master Rang did not trouble to use hook or hammer; his family fortune was confiscated all for nothing. And have you not seen how the five hundred bhikṣus were always present?
Samādhi. Each monkey wears a rhombus-patterned mirror. I ask you: where is the point of confusion? One must by all means refrain from speaking of "false" or "true" to others.
Upon the roots of the green pines on the Paṇḍaka rock, the sun stands at noon and the sky is cloudless. Shining through antiquity and soaring through the present—it is simply this.
The mudrā of the cross-legged posture leaves its traces upon the moss. To let go is to gather; to gather is to let go. Thus it is for the monks of the world.
Take this as a model. Silla remains as it was, on the eastern edge of the sea. The gateway does not reside upon the tongue.

All seventy-two peaks are available for wandering; strange flowers and numinous herbs have neither spring nor autumn. When the stone bridge is stepped upon and broken into two pieces, only then will one see that while the bridge flows, the water does not.

Sending his heart-nephew to travel among the masters, Ciming threw himself into the midst of a fire-rank, seeking only to test the Elder of Fenyang. At midnight, the deceased kin demanded a sacrifice;
at dawn, he feasted heartily until the cups and dishes were empty. At that time, many "elephants and dragons" were present in the assembly, yet they could not help but disperse and follow him.
East and west, the rolling hundred rivers flow into the sea; when the skin and flesh fall away, the true reality remains.

When the General crossed the Yuanzhou pass on a single horse, his parting instructions added luster to his legacy. Now, the earth is full of his descendants, yet not one person has been able to extinguish his lineage.
Shoushan says only this: look beneath your feet; there is no need for Buddhas and Patriarchs to open their mouths to swallow you.
I see Venerable Yunju Yu off as he departs for Putuo to pay his respects;
Yu Chan is traveling once around the South. Those who have realized the Buddha-dharma are as numerous as cow-hairs, yet they must strike it with the tip of their staff.
For him, I shall sever the high clouds of heaven, extinguish the ancestral lamp, sweep away the barbarian seed, and hold no longing for the various sages.
One’s own spirit is not held in high esteem. A pair of white jade discs from ten cities is inherently flawless; a handful of *maṇi* jewels—whom do they serve?
I have always admired Old Shushan, who could say, "A 'yes' or a 'no' cannot be complete. I have also heard the Elder Yunju say that things of the inner chamber must be discarded.
To break up the household and scatter the estate as one's livelihood is to transcend the time before King Bhīṣmagarjitasvaras. Tiantai Nanke.
To the north of the bridge, within the Avalokiteśvara Hall, Maitreya unfolds the twenty-five perfect penetrations. Peach blossoms at the corner of the eaves reveal the springtime colors.
Presented to the Abbot Yizang.

"You have performed your salutation and are standing to one side. This is neither the Tathāgata-dhyāna nor the intention of the Patriarchs. When it is used, it is used immediately without deliberation;
what need is there to speak of the definitive or the non-definitive? Sentient beings are originally Buddhas—what further need is there for the bestowal of prophecy at Vulture Peak?
Moving freely in all directions, asking about the distant while answering the near—a teacher-monk such as this is indeed clever."
Casually casting forth a mani-jewel, its divine light directly reaches beyond the heavens.
Sending Chan master Xuan to Jiangxi to visit Mazu, since that time of chaotic confusion, he has clearly exposed his family’s disgrace before the assembly. Coming and going, this is Pang.
The Duke: Having drunk the Western River dry, he does not open his mouth. Eighty-four men beyond the mundane world—shaking their heads and wagging their tails, all are golden-scaled dragons.
Yet they stir waves upon level ground; sitting grandly at the window, they occupy the vital ford. One cannot count the number of leftover soup and rancid rice;
though one unfurls the cooking cloth, there is nowhere to place it. It would be well to brandish the ancient sword before the skull, scorched by the sun and buffeted by the wind.

When Chui Quan revealed his whole being, and when Songcheng and Shizhe went to visit various teachers and attained Chan, I did not yet dare grant them my full approval. When their terms of office ended, they spoke of traveling abroad; as they were about to depart, they requested a parting verse from me.
Those born later are truly to be feared; I, this old monk, place my full hopes in you. The spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) of all quarters preach the Dharma like clouds and rain.
One who travels on pilgrimage must carry eyes; upon entering a gate, one must discern the master. Take heed and clearly remember this single phrase from Shoushan.

The Chief Librarian Dazang was returning to his hometown to attend to the funeral of his parents, both of whom had passed away. Seeking a verse for the journey home, [the Master] asked: "Who is it that repays this debt of gratitude? Where is one's native land?

Having traveled to the ends of the earth and the corners of the sea, there is nowhere left to seek through study. The ten directions are not apart from what is before one's eyes; it is simply thus, in silent solitude."
Vast and expansive! Do you not see Master Heze? He rushed into the Sangha Hall and struck the gavel.
Before Mahāprajñā had opened his mouth, the lamp-stand and the lanterns had already let out their roars.
As I see off Attendant Cheng, the autumn wind blows yellow leaves everywhere. He sits upright upon his straw mat sewing tattered robes.
When I, the Way-man, bid him farewell to travel afar, I asked him three times, yet he did not answer. Try looking now: what time is this? The ancestral Way hangs suspended like a thousand-jin weight.
Regarding the thread: it is certainly not the case that the teacher has leisure to seek disciples; rather, it is the disciples who must seek their teacher. Have you not seen?
"Casting a needle into the depths to startle the fierce dragon; joining palms before to pay homage to the auspicious image. Having grasped the mountain monk’s rabbit-horn staff..."
In years to come, he will stand atop a solitary peak.

To say that the "Great Canon of the Buddha's Teachings" (Dazangjiao) is a rhyming word is incorrect; it does not fit the level tones of level, rising, departing, or entering. It is the gateway of the mouth of Śākyamuni.
Narrow! Cast away both afflictions and bodhi. In every monastery, yellow leaves fall. A leprous dog born in heaven soars like a crane among the clouds;
let it fill the valleys and overflow the mountain peaks as it pleases. For now, take up the black staff and bind it to the high pavilion.
To see off the Abbot Yan of Jingci as he travels to Mount Lu, [the Master] picks up a single leaf and shifts it to become the entirety of Mount Lu. This is the true concern of the ancients;
it spares one the triviality of traveling back and forth, wearing straw sandals and trailing a staff through prefectures and counties, indulging in the utmost deluded thoughts. If this were not so...
An extraordinary man of the Way must surely possess a unique skill. To act in such a way yet not in such a way is like striking wood and finding no sound;
to act in a way that is not so yet nevertheless so is like knocking at emptiness and producing a resonance. If you wish to know the height of Mount Lu, listen further to the ballad of Mount Lu:
"The ten billion Jambudvīpas all fit within a single autumn hair. To the north of the mountain lie the two forests, East and West. Since ancient times...
Master Yuan established this site of supreme traces; eighteen people formed a society to practice together, and at the end of their lives, they all departed for the Land of Lotus Flowers.
To the south lie the six interconnected monasteries of Guizong, Kaixian, Wanshan, Xieyan, Luohan, and Huirui.

There are the Five Elders Peak, Moonlight Spring, Incense Burner Peak, Lion Peak, Golden Wheel Peak, and Jade Abyss. One gazes from afar upon the waterfalls, which cannot be approached, as they scatter like flying snow.
Crashing thunder pierces the cliff-side rocks; thousands upon thousands of pine trees intertwine and curve in complex patterns.
Here and there, white cranes dance and prance with joy. The ground is covered with auspicious flowers and beautiful grasses, while at all times, auspicious mists and fragrant smoke swirl.

What need is there for venerable masters to open their mouths? Let the myriad phenomena simply preach Chan. This is neither in long prose nor short verses, nor is it the direct pointing of the single [truth].
The Transmission: He overturned the old tracks of the five schools and swept away the declining lineages of the patriarchs. A needle’s eye swallowed the great chiliocosm;
a man from Fusang plowed the fields of Shaanxi.
As the Chan practitioner Cong departs, a pure breeze rises with every step. A single oar on an iron boat traverses thirty thousand *li*. The great fish is swallowed by the small;
it contracts its dragon’s head and extends its serpent’s tail. Before reaching the Central Plains, he has journeyed through them all—the mountains of Zhejiang are like dark eyebrows, the rivers...

Like a seasoned traveler, leaning against the wind and pressing my ear to listen to the local dialect, I find that my native land remains on the western shore of the sea. In Buddhism, there is no question of priority;
in the Way, there is no selection between the refined and the coarse; in Chan, there is no attachment to delusion or enlightenment; and in wisdom, existence and non-existence cannot be grasped.
Śākyamuni and Maitreya are but his servants—what man among us would not be a true hero?

As he was being sent to serve as the Great Compassionate Letting-in Charge of the Venerable Officers, in the brief space of a moment, his every movement—turning, stepping, bowing, and rising—transcended the summit of the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence. This spiritually sharp patch-robed monk was never ordinary;
how could his traveling for study have been merely to view the scenery? Upon the tip of a single hair stands Mount Ciyun; his straw sandals have worn through the mountains.
Layer upon layer. Having already achieved victory in the Dharma-battle of those years, you will naturally be able to revitalize our school in the future.
As for the perilous cliff-phrase—the mechanism for trapping a tiger—why wait for it to be entrusted once more in the Western Studio?
I see Master Wuzang off as he returns to Japan from Central India.
Since first arriving in the Great Tang, this Way has already been perfected; moreover, many years have passed, and through repeated refinement, the gold becomes ever more pure.
It cannot be increased, nor can it be diminished. Its application is as vast as the sands of the Ganges—how could there be any limit?

Do not ask of the common masses or the superior sages; who would discuss great wisdom alongside ordinary consciousness? The waters of West Lake and the mountains of West Lake—motion and stillness do not depart from within the square inch of the heart-mind.
The moon hangs over the Central Peak as the night draws on; who can reach for the celestial fragrance of the cassia blossoms? Nor is this called "mind."
It is not called "Buddha," nor is it called "half or full," "partial or complete," or "the provisional and the real that illuminate the moon.
To turn the prow of the boat is to reach one's native home; the dragon swallows it, yet the azure lapis lazuli remains inexhaustible.
As the attendant You sent off for Mount Tiantai and Yandang Shan, he thought:
"Before Śākyamuni and after Maitreya, the mind does not perceive the mind; no form can be grasped. Stepping out the door, there were green waters and blue mountains.
Everywhere the flowers are red and the grasses are green; to point toward such things as this is to confuse "yu" and "lu.
To accept it directly is to be worlds apart. Cold Mountain said: "The tracks of ancient sages upon a thousand-year stone; a single point of emptiness before a ten-thousand-foot cliff."
This single point of emptiness cannot be grasped; whether at Tiantai or Yandang, one follows wherever the West or East may lead. Let monks on pilgrimage refrain from making light judgments;
I have briefly used an open mind to mark this station. It is neither ordinary nor holy, yet I have forcibly assigned it a name. Treading high upon the crown of Vairocana, one moves above all.
As he saw off the Abbot Yizang on his journey to Mount Ming and Mount Tiantai, [the Master] picked up his staff and said: "Whether in mountain forests or cities, first pass through Linglong Rock;
there, listen first to the Master of the House proclaiming the wondrous sound. Then, turning the body, ascend straight to Jade Shelf Peak, treading upon that which has been there from of old."
The family treasure: the eighty-four thousand *śarīras*. You must know they do not reside within a golden casket. A favorable wind safely carries the boat to Potalaka.
At every land and in every atom of dust, one encounters the Great Being. Visiting Xuedou and roaming Qingliang, everything met by the eye is none other than a sacred site of the Way.
Tianning Dingshui is a true spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*); when the lion roars, the foxes hide. How could this be merely a city of rosy clouds?
Observing the scenery alone, I must call forth the five hundred śrāvakas; one by one, I instruct them to emerge from the world.

Amidst the clamor, my body and mind remain undisturbed and tranquil. Even if a wondrous flower should manifest upon a tea bowl, I still wait for the minds of sentient beings to accept it of their own accord.
Who does not know the Three Sages of Guoqing? When inspiration strikes, I compose new poems wherever I go. Taking empty space as paper and the great ocean as ink.
Rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds are all but hair-tips; throughout the various quarters, the discourse on Chan is vast and sweeping.
Who now can understand and raise this koan? On the slippery stone bridge, it is difficult to set foot; below lies a bottomless valley where dragons coil. How many travelers dare not peer down?
From the precipice, silver waterfalls fly day and night. Raising one’s head, one gazes further at the clouds atop Mount Huading—stretching for thousands upon thousands of miles.

They followed one another. Rubbing his staff, he returned once more to Xizhou. Suddenly, from the tip of a single hair, Mount Sumeru emerged, escorting all the attendants on a tour of Tiantai and Yandang.
The Tai Shan mountains are green; the Yan Shan mountains are azure. Filling the eyes and filling the ears, they are neither sound nor form. First, pass through Sheng County to pay homage to Maitreya.
Do not say that his entire body is but cliffs and crags—who else could support the heavens and pillar the earth?
He constantly reveals himself to people, yet they do not recognize him. Try serving tea to the five hundred arhats; from each cup appears a single branch of blossoms. Clearly he has brought it forth.
At this one move, how many monks have missed him! Having roamed Huading Peak, he went to Guoqing. The famous monastery lies right in the midst of profound seclusion;
the true countenances of Fenggan, Hanshan, and Shishi are revealed there. Twisting cold vines climb high trees; slowly and steadily he walks into the Furuang Village.
Strange peaks and steep cliffs, where clouds vomit and swallow; on the left and right of Lingyan are eighteen monasteries. Monastery...
Every temple has a mountain facing its gate. Jñānaketu sat all day long with his knees drawn up, gazing upward as the waterfall tumbled from the void.
Do not say that the Venerable One did not preach the Dharma; he scattered forth ten million pearls of the black dragon.

Following each matter, I offer you a *huatou*: "If you do not resolve it now, when will it ever end? There is no Buddha-dharma within the Great Tang Empire—just look at the iron boat floating on the water."
Floating upward, he sends off the Chan practitioner Shou;
who can truly discern this exalted manifestation? White clouds lock away the colors of Cold Mountain; the wandering monks are far too alert.
Wake up! Raising the eyebrows, the two eyes are azure. Since the time of the Patriarchs, many have raised this teaching; now, do not ask what to do.
Eat when hungry and drink when thirsty—there is nothing more. Cast off the head-stall and unload the pack-saddle.

I see my Zen practitioner departing, his bony shoulders slung across the ancient vine. His two sandals tread upon the withered snow; the sun-bird cries out, never ceasing. How shall we part from these spring mountains?
With eyes heavy from drowsy sleep, where shall they open? He must surely point toward the bright moon on the path ahead.
Sent to the attendant Sōji of Kenchō-ji in Japan:
Within the Great Tang land of the Chan school, not a single person has yet raised the cry. With a casual hand, he plucked up a tuft of cloth; how shameful, Master Wukuo!
This story has been transmitted for several hundred autumns; five pairs and ten individuals have drifted along in idleness. The lanterns...
The incense burner pillar is far too talkative; the myriad phenomena and the entire cosmic order sing in unison in response.

As this traveling boat passes the mouth of Pén City, atop the peaks one already hears the lion’s roar. The Five Elders simultaneously smile with bared brows; the waterfalls do not flow, yet the green mountains run.
Setting aside the ordinary and the extraordinary, how do you communicate the news when meeting people?
Riding an iron horse backward up Mount Sumeru, one wins the pure breeze arising throughout the eight directions.
Seeing off Zen Practitioner Ming to visit Jingshan; at the same time, a note to Master Guding:
from where have you recently come? Have you ever been here before? A brilliant monk like you must not open his mouth recklessly in public.
Tianning’s staff—let us not fail to strike it across the back; it shall certainly not reach thirty blows, but rather twenty-nine, leaving one stick for myself to eat.
How will those in all quarters analyze this? Old master Lingxiao will surely nod his head in approval.
He does not utter the cry of a jackal, nor does he let out the roar of a lion. If a person can comprehend this meaning, they are fit to continue the lineage of the Muni.
Sent by the Japanese attendant from the Great Tang to Japan: East and West, eyes equally slanted and noses straight; the mud ox at the bottom of the sea has its horns plucked away.
Dragging it along. A stone woman in the clouds throws her shuttle and weaves. Zen Master Ri was fortunate enough to be pitiable, yet he said there was news from the West.
Originally, there has been no news from the West. On level ground, one plants thorns in vast confusion.
Where did Wenyuan ever see Zhaozhou? Even Sudhana never visited Maitreya.
The First Seat of Tianning Temple was sent to the Second Seat of Lingshan;
this is not the same as other quarters. He understands and laughs at the Lesser Śākyamuni, who dreamed of ascending to the Tuṣita Palace.

The hundred negations and the four propositions—vast and open, they unravel the thicket of discourse. Where speech is employed, it becomes silence; where there is obstruction, nothing is not penetrated.

A venomous snake swallows a turtle’s head; a fierce tiger bites a great beast. Sitting and cutting off the tongues of Buddhas and patriarchs, this was from the beginning not a matter of cultivation or realization.
In the three winters, withered trees flourish; in the nine summers, snow-tipped leaves turn crimson. Holding this up like an old monk, he uses it to clarify his own person.
With a direct shout from below, one cannot avoid being deaf for three days. Three days of deafness is still bearable, but it will frighten to death the old man of the eastern village.
To the attendant Hong of Zhongzhu:
Great capacity and great function are not transmitted; who can understand the golden-haired lion’s roar?
The seventy-year-old old man of Qiansui Rock has eyes all over his body and hands all over his body. If you say he entered nirvana this year, a true man would never accept such a thing.
People mock it, yet the rhinoceros fan remains; it truly brings a cool breeze that fills the hall with frost.
To the Librarian of the Canon at Jing Mountain:
the great web of the entire Tripitaka is but idle entanglement; no one in all the world can leap out of it. Meng’an was originally an extraordinary monk.
Son, at midnight the Fusang tree spits forth the red sun; picking up the tea from the summit of Lingxiao Peak, it is actually the tangerine from Lake Dongting.
Within the three thousand worlds, there is the *āmala* fruit; whether released or gathered, who can question it? The pine wind and mountain stream discourse on the profound of themselves;
yet they laugh at those who fussily debate the provisional and the real. Provisional is not provisional; real is not real. Baiyun says this:
"Prāṇa! You have brought misery upon your children and grandchildren, suffering in vain.

This Master Yue of Zhongzhu has come specifically to consult and study with me. When there is 'me' and there is 'another,' it becomes a falling into talk. As soon as he stepped across the threshold, I raised [my whisk]."
The eyebrows are clearly parted as the treasure-store opens its golden lock. To the west of the Tang Empire and to the east of Japan—everything is gathered within a single mote of dust.
How many coral groves are there? They reflect the morning sun, glowing red at the third watch.

Though Śākyamuni preached for forty-nine years, it was like purchasing cinnabar to paint the bright moon. In Central India, the application of the spiritual mechanism is indeed distinct; this is the Vajra-treasure.
The sword cuts directly at the head.

Bestowed upon the attendant Yuan, Buddha hands it to Buddha; Patriarch transmits it to Patriarch. Yellow-headed and blue-eyed, under the bright sun and clear sky: to stir a single thought is already to deviate.
To open one’s mouth is already an error. There is no need to lengthen the duck or shorten the crane; why must one level the mountains or fill the valleys?

Those who penetrate this depart from mind, intellect, and consciousness; those who study this leave the paths of the holy and the mundane. In years past, when I came from Japan, a single lotus bloomed upon the red furnace.
On this day, as I go forth to all quarters, the iron whip shatters the coral tree. East, west, south, north—everywhere.
Moving freely in all directions, one wins the pure breeze that spreads across the earth.

This inscription for the Dharma-keeper Lingyin Wen was written by Gushejia (Ancient Śākyamuni): "The present Maitreya does not come after; the rabbit's horns need not be non-existent, and the ox's horns need not be existent."
Who has entered together with him? With whom does he roar in one voice? For forty-nine years he has spoken incessantly, his skirt trailing through water and mud.
To such an extraordinary and brilliant monk, we must give our full praise; to forge a blade, one needs the iron of Binzhou. Eye meets eye, mechanism meets mechanism;
Cold Spring has gathered the *maṇi* jewel and returned home. Encountering people, he pours out a basketful; by day...
Thunder and lightning flash across the blue sky.

As soon as the abbot Huizang entered the gate, Deshan the Old One struck him with his staff; as soon as Linji the Master entered the gate, he let out a shout. Thus, generation after generation, the barbarians were utterly extinguished.
This seed has been free from doubt for the sake of vast kalpas; this practice is like a sail catching a favorable wind, blowing down three or five petals of plum blossoms.
The entire Great Canon of Teachings speaks only of this very Dharma; the old man Zhaozhou merely wandered around his meditation seat in vain.
Joyfully, my duties at Nanhu have now been fulfilled. Before hundreds of thousands of people, he held up a flower; Kāśyapa’s smiling eyes opened and closed of their own accord.
A fine horse requires no coral whip.
Seeing off Attendant Qiū of Japan for Jinling on the first day of the tenth month:
the cold wind howls through the ancient trees; Jinling is far away, yet your journey is so swift.

Before Bodhidharma arrived from the West, the mountains of north and south Huai stood in dense clusters. No reliance on words or letters, pointing directly at the human mind—like the blind turtle finding the floating log.
Rolling a mustard seed through a needle’s eye: from the very beginning, there have been no Buddhas or patriarchs. To fully realize this matter is neither of this age nor of antiquity.
As for the National Teacher’s attendant, what was his intention? You owe me, and I owe you.

I see that the attendant Duan and the attendant Wenyuan of Zhaozhou, along with the two masters Baiyun and Qingning, have together established a Dharma community where the elephant-king and the lion gallop side by side.
Alas, I am already decrepit at Mount Ling; with no one by my side to whom I might express my inner thoughts, I am filled with shame.
Chan Master Duan came from Japan; the iron ox does not eat the grass by the fence. Inquiring after your welfare this morning, when a guest arrives, one burns incense.
The upper stroke is short, the lower stroke is long. If you step forward further to seek instruction, the mountain monk is currently busy receiving officials.
Moon Hermit:
The moon in the heavens, the moon in the water—there is but one moon, never two. Though one searches for it again and again, it is groundless;
at the full fifteen days, how could there be any difference? Recalling Master Mazu of those years, the whole family enjoyed the clear autumn together.
Nanquan shook his sleeves and departed; who could open wide the doors and windows before the window?
For many decades there has been no such work; it rises at night and falls again at dawn. Within one’s own house, all is dark and dim; to seek outwardly is entirely in error.
Calling back the head for their sake, I say: the single point of numinous light is the same in darkness and dawn, shining through heaven and reflecting upon earth.
It is not yet known. Ask Old Wang of the north of the river or the south of the river.
Yunhai is not yet clear; Yunhai is direct and immediate. Let us speak for now from the perspective of a single wave: when one wave moves, ten thousand waves arise. One...
When the waves cease, ten thousand waves are extinguished. Thus, the afflictions of sentient beings do not depart from arising and ceasing.

When one dharma reaches the ground of all Buddhas, afflictions are transformed into wisdom. Both wisdom and afflictions are fundamentally empty; both sentient beings and Buddhas are suchness (*tathatā*).
Yet, pointing directly within this [reality], it is vast and surging, flooding the heavens and soaking the sun. Even this flooding of the heavens and soaking of the sun does not exist.
End. I do not know from where this current finally ceases. At times it forms a tide that exhausts the waters within a hundred million continents;

at other times it dries up the three thousandfold world-system while surging with waves. When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ocean-Cloud contemplates the ocean of clouds, he sees only layer upon layer of unobstructed expanse.
My contemplation of the ocean of clouds is fundamentally different: it overturns the sun and moon and swallows the void. This is not the view of the Śrāvakas.
Horse and rabbit; the Bodhisattva is neither elephant nor dragon. Old Śākyamuni is full of empty talk; he wishes to speak of clouds and seas, but his words first reach their limit.
To call them clouds, they are not five-colored; to call them seas, they are devoid of a single drop. Mount Sumeru is shattered and the kalpa-stones are consumed.
The end of the future is unfathomable; it is unfathomable. Facing the present with such clarity, how could there be any limit?
The clouds of Yun’an drift and vanish; they emerge from the great void. To say they emerge is fundamentally without intention; to say they vanish is to depart [from attachment].
Nests and dens: sometimes following the dragon for thousands of miles, meeting again and again; sometimes clutching stones—here a fragment, there a shard, impossible to find.
By the waterside and beneath the forest trees, their hidden wonders are revealed. Who, even with the finest brush and ink, could paint them?
Gathered in, they are utterly without a trace; let them go, and they swallow the eight directions. One is of many kinds; two are not of two sorts. Far away...
Within the square inch of the heart, one is separated by a great trichiliocosm. Ordinary beings do not realize the Stage of the Cloud of Dharma;

Sages do not dwell in the Heaven Without Clouds. The Cloud of Virtue eternally abides atop Mount Miaofeng; the Spirit of the Sea universally responds before the faces of all sentient beings. These hundreds of coils and thousands of layers—whose realm is this?
Unfolding to the left and rolling up to the right, such is the skillful means of the successive sages. Have you not seen the man from Guansi, who has submerged his head?
The brain. He falsely styled himself Yun’an to manifest his Way; the Buddha’s hand has not yet been extended, yet the donkey’s feet have opened. Clearly, he betrayed the old Huanglong.
You now likewise style yourself Yun’an, yet this meaning remains vast and obscure—I have not yet understood it. Three times he questioned him, and three times he did not know.
The white clouds remain as they were, stretching across the fragrant grasses.
In Mirror Hermitage there is one thing: black as lacquer, bright as the sun. Though the six windows leave no place for dust to settle, the myriad phenomena cannot escape its shadowy substance.
Dongping exerted all his strength trying to smash it, yet it remained whole; even a sharp-witted monk lacks such sharp wit. Each monkey—*míhóu*—[is distinct].
Wearing the rhombus-shaped mirror of the ancient past, its vast divine radiance illuminates heaven and earth. How many springs have passed since the Hu came and the Han appeared?
Who is the person who recognizes the master? If you further inquire about the middle, the outside, and the inside, though free from dust, you cannot avoid generating dust once more.
In ancient times, before Yin and Yang were yet distinguished and the physical shell had not yet separated, there was not a single tile above nor a needle-point’s space below.

Daring to compete with the Dragon King in wealth, let the patch-robed disciples give rise to doubt; neither on this shore nor on the other shore, nor dwelling in the middle stream—acting according to circumstances.

Adapting to circumstances: when the pure is raised and the turbid stirred, the waves subside and the wind calms; when traces are extinguished and sounds withdrawn, thunder rolls and lightning flashes.
Whether the Buddhas of the three periods know it or not, whether the Patriarchs of the six generations see it or not—should one hesitate or set up defenses, the oar strikes the mouth and one falters;
to flaunt the line at the tip of the pole is to immediately plunge into the surging waves, while failing to do so leaves one separated by mountains and passes.
When both ends are severed, heaven and earth are vast; with a single stroke, one traverses the eighteen rapids of Jiangxi.
From the Deer Park at the beginning until the Bahudhika River at the end, he never spoke a single word—this makes the sick Vimalakīrti laugh to tears.
The Great Being Vimalakīrti remained in silence, yet he manifested and entered [realms] as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

Though the thirty-two teachings may seem confused and manifold, all numerical phrases and non-numerical phrases are but such. As for the old Chan master with missing teeth who sat facing a wall for nine years, he split open skin and tore through marrow.
Chinese words and barbarian tongues—were you to consult the *Longkan Shoujian*, the *Tangyun*, or the *Yupian* from beginning to end, you could not explain them away.
He took his single sandal and returned to the Western Heaven; the seal of the winter melon has been transmitted for a long time. The ancient script is clearly held in his hand;
when the Master strikes once, everything shatters into a hundred pieces, and even the lamp-stands and lanterns all let out a roar. Ten [miles] of Qiantang...
The moon is high and the wind is brisk; he showed me a scroll of verses as thick as a cow’s haunch. White is the paper, black are the characters.
When was fragrant ink ever dipped into purple-hair brushes?
This path was bestowed upon Wanshou by the Librarian You.
Buddha after Buddha handed it down; patriarch after patriarch transmitted it. It is right here and now, not involving words or explanations.

Therefore, when guiding disciples and leading the assembly, they speak of the wondrous and discuss the profound. This is like joining bamboo poles to reach for the moon, or like gluing the bridge-pins of a lute while trying to tune the strings.
Clearly manifest within daily life, it fills the expanse of empty space. Striking against it and bumping into it—who understands it, and who does not?
Valued like soil, yet despised like gold; Mount Sumeru is not yet high, and the waters of the great ocean are not yet deep.
Wander aimlessly through the east, west, south, and north; how many people in this dusty world know this mind?
The Seven-Ber-Year-Old Ancient Adept of Mei-yin: With pine blossoms for food and lotus leaves for clothing, Though all desire to see him, he cannot be found;
A thatched cottage surrounded on four sides by green mountains. A monk wearing a robe woven from rattan vines suddenly arrives; No sooner does he open his mouth than he meets with disaster.
A strange laugh. From this point on, an evil reputation spread throughout the world. Who would have known that his words lacked any profound mystery?
To take "this very mind is Buddha" as a realization is an error; "neither mind nor Buddha" is merely the ordinary. Who would be willing to eat leftover soup and rancid rice?
To take fine flesh and further gouge it to create an ulcer. Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; where there is no Buddha, one must run past in haste. I urge you: do not emulate this.
The man who waits by the stump. Seven cushions worn through sitting in vain.
A Great Awakening bestowed upon Zhongzhu Huo, the Abbot:
a phrase of Great Awakening that strikes the vital point, bursting forth from the throat and between the teeth. Riding a great ox within the hollow of a lotus fiber.
The Peng-bird. Within the eye of a gnat, a night market is set up. A single word is not too few; the entire Tripitaka is not too much.
When a lantern sees a pillar, it claps its hands and laughs heartily. Empty space falls crashing to the ground; the alms bowl opens its mouth and swallows mountains and rivers.
*Mitrā-gu*, *Mitrā-jñā*. Not a single stroke is attached to a character; you brothers have added ten strokes.
In those days, Huangbo was truly without cause; with sixty strokes of his broom handle, he struck Linji.
To Zhongzhu’s Secretary Zhen, I present these pine and stones:
The green pines stand tall and solitary; the white stones are sharp and distinct. Above, they rub against the Milky Way; below, they embrace the clouds and valleys. If they were used as rafters...
To serve as a beam; to serve as a hall for state affairs; to be a *gui* or a *zhang* jade token;

to be the glory of dukes and marquises—none of these compare to the Daoist practitioner who has no concerns, daily forgetting himself amidst pines and rocks. When the pure breeze rises, he utters the dragon’s cry; when the fragrant grasses reflect, he crouches like a tiger.
Amidst the clamor and bustle of the dusty marketplace, my home lies deep within the green mountains.
The Dharma-body is formless; it is presented here by the Japanese Abbot Nōzō.
It is clearly manifest right before you: the eye does not see form, and the ear does not hear sound. Though one hears nothing, it is so.
Not seen. Yet, one understands how to respond with adaptability according to circumstances. Since the great void was shattered, the Śūnyatā-deva has been constantly face-to-face.
—A gift from Longyuan to the Abbot Licaang.
The dragon is not the phrase "dragon"; the abyss is not the phrase "abyss. One must ask: where does the dragon-abyss reside? The entire earth is waves.
Suddenly, thunder arises from the blue sky; sun and moon abruptly turn black; mountains and peaks collapse.

It scatters the sweet moisture across the four seas and five lakes, reviving the withered roots of the three grasses and two trees. If one cannot understand this like Lord Ye Gong, one cannot avoid falling into error.
A mistake. With empty hands, who can come to receive the pearl from the neck? From ancient times to the present, the true horns have never been revealed.
To the Japanese Librarian Yen, I present this without outside:
neither empty nor non-empty. Holy and profane alike dwell within the circular light. The Floating Banner King-land and the Fragrant Water Sea.
Do not ask about north, south, east, or west. One is all; all is one. From the beginningless past to the endless future, who gains and who loses?
It is entirely contained within the tip of a hair, yet you seek it elsewhere. Even if you were to find it, it would not be the reality.
How many people are there who can see this clearly right now? The Buddhas have provisionally spoken of thirty-two marks; you must recognize them for what they are.
The Original Body.
A gift to Elder Xianyan Jin of Aoshan:
How extraordinary is Aoshan! It anchors Huangyan while floating in verdant hues; its peaks are steep and towering, lofty and precipitous.
Lí. Gazing upward directly toward the clouds, how can one reach the limit? Have you not seen how Xuefeng once met the old man Yantou?

For thirty years, he poured out his heart and soul until it overflowed from his breast to cover heaven and earth; it was at the Shaoshan Inn that he finally attained the Way. Dragon scales shimmer, fish scales glisten;
how many times have the red dusts of the mortal world flown across the vast blue seas? Even when the fierce Vairambha winds blow, they cannot stir him. Ten...
The three islands of this continent are as long as spring.
Ancient trees bestow their splendor;
when heaven and earth were yet undivided, there stood the first gnarled branch. Though there are trees upon Jambudvīpa, alas, how slow was their rooting!
How many times cold, how many times heat! Its trunk resembles bronze, its leaves like iron. Standing firm, what need to fear winds that shake the earth?
Its lofty standard is formidable even against snow piled mountain-high. The *pien*, *nan*, *qi*, and *zi* trees are all but common timber; none of them were not grown from a mere span or inch.
Yet they are not things destined for a thousand or ten thousand years; before long, they turn to dust and ash. As for Zhuangzi’s *chun* tree—now...
Already decayed. Do you know the cassia tree of Shaolin? What is it that supports the heavens and props up the earth? Each and every one looks southward at the Northern Dipper.
—Presented by Xinyuan to Layman Yue.
The three dots are like flowing water; the curve resembles a sickle for reaping grain. Neither Buddhas nor Patriarchs can speak of it; who among others could grasp it?
I have heard that Hanshanzi has verses that are no mere talk; they hang in vain upon the lips and teeth, yet the autumn moon shines upon the azure pool.

Who else knows that nothing can compare to it? Coldly containing the void, its clarity reaches the very bottom. In a single instant of turning the light back upon itself, from where does this single pulse originally arise?
Sholin presents this to Chan Head Guo of Zhongzhu;
the Elder of Muzhou recognized Linji. A cool and shady great tree received a direct transmission; indeed, its canopy covers all people under heaven.
Today, its descendants spread across the earth; each and every lofty branch supports the vast void, and layer upon layer of dense leaves come forth.
Pure Wind: The great forest stands out beyond all things; it is not the same as ordinary flowers and trees. Throughout the world, frost and ice cannot affect it;
though it changes with the seasons, it remains imperishable. How could birds and beasts dare to dwell there at will?
There is always the roar of the golden-haired lion.
Daji’s Gift to the Head Librarian of the Japanese Tripitaka:
On the Necessity of Integrating Great Function with Great Capacity. When capacity and function are directly applied, the path of the mind is cut off.
Deshan’s single blow caused the mountains and peaks to collapse; Linji’s single shout split the void. Do you not see Changsha’s tiger, Cen? His functioning did not conform to—
The same applies to all directions. Jizang personally once raised this point; he was kicked by him [the Master] once, and the transmission has been passed on endlessly.

This man of the Way has long possessed the ambition to soar through the clouds, revealing the supreme matters of the School Gate. When he casually picks up a thorny mallet, billions of Mount Sumerus are reduced to powder.

One might offer to the Lord of the Mountain an infinite gift of hundreds of billions of three-thousandfold world systems; yet if one were to pick up a single clod of earth from the ground, even empty space would eventually suffer depletion.
The light of time in this mundane world fades and decays so easily; only this mind is neither extinguished nor born, enduring through vast eons.
Now, from this very moment until the end of the future, one laughs at Maudgalyāyana for exhausting himself over the Buddha’s voice.
Zhiyin bestows [this teaching] upon the deluded practitioner of Chan;
existence and non-existence differ by but thirty li. Obscuring his traces and concealing his brilliance, he finds joy within himself. A decree has flown forth from the Phoenix Hall.
Liu. Three times he entered the mountains, yet was not summoned forth. The Sage is fully endowed with the dharmas of an ordinary person; the ordinary person is fully endowed with the mind of a Sage.
Neither ordinary nor sage, they transcend all. The path lies amidst the deepening depths of white clouds.
Without concealment, I present this to my Zen practitioner:
in daily life, the whole body is manifest in its majesty. Putting on clothes and eating meals, morning follows evening. At Vulture Peak, the Buddha held up a single flower;
hundreds of thousands of gods and men were all at a loss. Form is not form; sound is not sound. It cannot be depicted.
It cannot be described; it cannot be painted. It is right before one’s eyes—do not seek it elsewhere. The green mountains and blue waters become all the more distinct.
Composed by Siyuan for the Japanese attendant Wen.
In a single thought, universally contemplate immeasurable kalpas; there is no going, no coming, and no abiding. Seeking them throughout the three periods of time, they cannot be found.
A cast-iron weight has been eaten through by worms; Bodhidharma crossed the shifting sands and arrived unexpectedly in China.

Though it was said to be a hundred thousand li away, in the end he did not leave home. Even if you were to run through all the worlds of the floating banners, east, west, south, and north, there would be nowhere to hide.
As for these distinctions: when it is cold, the entire heavens and the entire earth are cold; when it is hot, the entire heavens and the entire earth are hot.
At this one place, mental activity ceases; empty space cannot contain it, and not even a thousand sages can describe it. Do you, O sharp-witted monk, know it or not?
If you do not know, then go ask the moon at the edge of the sky.
Guiryan bestows this upon the Elder Jūju Gatsujō of Japan:
Moonlight and cassia seeds drift through the seclusion of the crags. A single tree has grown for three thousand autumns. The autumn wind blows open the flowers upon its branches;
Wherever the blossoms reach, a fragrant scent wafts forth. Master Gatsu is originally a descendant of the Lord Kanesuke; The fragrance of his reputation fills the world.
Heaven and earth. The dream-like and illusory body of the Tathāgata Suvarṇaśālī does not require further receiving of the prediction of Bodhi.
Utterly devoid of illumination, the Head Seat Jing Luoluojue (Jing Luoluojue) is beyond all reception; it is stark and bare, with nothing to grasp. When Longtan blew out the paper candle, his eyes—

Its radiance shatters through the four continents; where neither sun nor moon reaches, even heaven and earth cannot conceal it. Within the great trichiliocosm, the true body stands forth majestic and bare.
Seeing arises from conditions and clarity; in darkness, vision becomes non-existent. When both light and dark are forgotten, the spiritual mind undergoes a hundred transformations.
Before one’s eyes there is no *ācārya*; upon the seat there is no old monk. When not a single thought arises, the three periods of time are severed. Support [this].
At midnight, the sun rises;

on Mount Gandhamādana, the Elder Guo is presented with the fivefold Dharma-body, which cannot be contained. It is neither sandalwood nor *kunda* flower; it is the solitary peak of Wondrous Summit, the Hall of Manifestation.

The Hall: The true mechanism of Shaoshi is clear and distinct; to smell it or touch it can cause the faculty of olfactory observation to penetrate. White clouds veil and reflect the azure, translucent clarity.
The blossoming of flowers and the falling of leaves are matters of every year; as before, Mount Sumeru towers loftily in the vast void.
A Gift to Chan Master Ying of Zhongshan:
Within the realm of heaven and earth, amidst the expanse of the universe, no brush and ink can depict you; your hands and feet are difficult to grasp.
Above, you are solitary and perilous; below, you are steep and precipitous. Unshaken through vast kalpas, the myriad peaks naturally encircle you. Do you not see? The Chaos...
Chun opened up the cosmos and divided the seven golden mountains; Sumeru sits aloft, severing the heart of the vast blue ocean. Yet the patch-robed monk does not understand the meaning of Zhongshan;
he merely busies himself, searching outwardly in vain.
The Great Peak presents this to Japan’s Accumulated Head Seat:
setting aside Mount Sumeru, all else is but small; a single mustard seed suffices to swallow it all.
I pick up a mote of dust for him—Fuji and Sarugaku join Penglao Island; China’s Tai, Heng, Hua, Huo, and Song peaks are carved out of azure by a precious blade.
The Hibiscus: When light is turned back and reflected within the square inch of the heart, the accumulated blocks and floating bubbles vanish within the three realms.

It cannot be gathered by pinching nor shattered by blowing; what thing is this that exists beyond heaven and earth? Gazing at the sea from a cliff, the ocean stretches vast and boundless; clouds arise from the rocks, gathering like flights of snow.

How are the two characters of "Great Mind" (*mahācitta*) to be translated? They do not fall within the realm of human sentiment or consciousness. Bodhisattvas of the Supreme Vehicle believe in them without doubt;
how could those of middling or inferior capacity fathom them? Śākyamuni of old and Maitreya of today—here, they manifest thousands upon hundreds of emanations.
Billions [of lifetimes]. *Dat-dat* and *dao-dao*, all empty exertion of effort. When one acts for others with crooked fingers, how could they ever be straight?
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, following one's natural spontaneity—this is precisely the subduing of demons and the turning of the Dharma wheel.

A single fist of no fixed direction shatters empty space; a single footstep overturns the great earth. East, west, south, and north are not distinguished; up, down, and the four intermediate directions have nowhere to rest.
The vast expanse of the Great Flower Treasury World is as wide as drifting clouds and water; a thousand million lands reside upon the tip of an autumn hair. Let it all be released.

Gathering it all together rests entirely within me; whether cast left or thrown right, how could it be difficult? Since it is neither defiled nor pure, how ultimately can one distinguish the heterodox from the orthodox?
Directly and completely upholding the command of Magadha, amidst the profusion of activity, one forever abides in the *nāga-samādhi*.
Nan-in was one of fifty-three spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra). Where could Sudhana find his traces? Mañjuśrī’s pointing was far too clear;
he has worn out his straw sandals for no avail. Dwelling neither in mountain forests nor in the dust of the world, he is neither ordinary nor holy, neither...
Whether distant or intimate, the patch-robed monk perceives it through and through: the Great Way is vast and boundless, yet there is nowhere for the body to hide.
To call this "leaving the nest" is to say that the entire realm is not obstructed. At midnight in Jambudvīpa, the sun stands at noon; it is right before one's eyes—why do you not see it?
Shi’an’s staff strikes the void with a resounding *pe-lo-po*. The stone man and the wooden man both respond in unison. Throughout the ten directions there is but this single, solid, and dense body;
iron walls and silver mountains are difficult to penetrate. Formless and extending through past and present, do not eliminate delusive thoughts to seek the truth.
Mind. Since the Ox-Headed One personally met the Fourth Patriarch, where can one seek the "hundred birds carrying flowers"?
He laughs at those within the clouds and mountains as the clouds come and go; though he has tried to detain them many times, they cannot be stayed. One fragment heads west, another...
To the east, for whom is it hung upon the green pine tree? Sometimes it is rolled up—disregarding high or low, near or far.

Sometimes it is unfurled, filling the great void from south to north and east to west. Originally it is without mind; do not inquire after its traces. Floating and drifting, it scatters and spreads according to the power of the wind.
Letting itself go as a white robe or a blue dog, it moves freely and unrestrainedly. Returning to stillness and back to emptiness, where can it be sought? Yet I fear that within the mountains...
Clouds mock people; their petty concerns cannot avoid the dust of the mundane world. If one can simply let go, there is peace and joy;
therefore, the Shaolin tradition has long used clouds as a metaphor for the body.
Bodhidharma faced the wall; Huiké found peace of mind. Two young cassia trees spread their shadows and cast their shade;

above they support the heavens, below they buttress the earth. The past was not of old, and the future is not of now. Since the single sandal returned to the Western Regions, year after year the spring breeze has added to their verdant hue.
Do not say there is no one in the courtyard who can stand in the snow; the fragrance of one flower and five petals—how could it ever end?
The West Spring (Xiyuan) presents this to the Senior Seat (Shouzuo) Yuan:
The Lake Anavatapta divides into four rivers; these four rivers flow together, their waves surging as one.

Not only do fish, dragons, shrimp, and crabs dwell therein, but there are also great-bodied asuras. Yuan of Tiantai has served me for a long time; he has taken up paper and requested my "West [Spring]."
A Song of the Source: In the Western Source there is not a drop of water; Buddhas and patriarchs are from head to tail.
Now and then, ancient and modern, they penetrate top to bottom. What more need be said of India and China?
Nanyue, Shitou, Mazu, and Layman Pang— It was simply because of swallowing the West River in one gulp That boundless waves arose from this.

The single source of all spirits is the single source. It is provisionally named "Buddha. Since "Buddha" is a provisional name, from where does this source emerge? Śākyamuni, the Old Man, never truly awakened to it;
for forty-nine years he circulated it through winding streams. Who says there is a separate transmission outside the teachings? Among the hundreds of thousands of people—
The vast sky has no place to take its measure. The Way of the Former Sage is this: flowing springs are its life-force, and profound stillness is its body.

From the beginning, it is neither clear nor turbid; even now, it is neither ancient nor new. The four great oceans are gathered back into a single drop; the five Mount Sumerus are rolled up into a speck of dust.
Golden waves pervade the entire realm, constantly surging and swirling, yet they have no interaction whatsoever with ordinary beings or sages.
The Wayman Haigu (House in the Sea) Pumen has requested a song from me; I cannot help but stir up wind and waves on level ground. Is the house the sea, or is the sea the house?
What is the true meaning of "House in the Sea"? From this, hundreds of thousands of oceans arise, yet even their arising does not depart from a single drop.
A single drop of water drenches the sun; its vastness surging to the heavens is truly marvelous. Rolling up and unfolding, all is contained within the window and the eaves.

I observe that the ocean of the Avalokiteśvara’s mind is empty, yet every Buddha-hall is arrayed within it. Reflected shadows join in radiant splendor within the jeweled pavilions; pearl banners and jade trees shimmer with brilliant clarity.
Yet when one withdraws the mind into stillness, not a single thing exists. I ask you, practitioner: do you know this? It does not descend.
The meditation seat pervades the ten directions; the spring breeze naturally sways the willow by the golden pitcher.
The dragon of Gu-yin listens with its horns; the ant listens with its body; humans listen with their ears. The wind calls and the valley responds; listening reaches the point where there is no sound.
The valley is empty of itself; mountains, rivers, and rocky cliffs communicate across vast distances. Even were one to use a thousand hands, they could not cover it;
thus, it is resonant and clear on all eight sides. Although it is hidden, how has it ever been hidden? Under the bright sun and blue sky, thunder rolls on and on.
Idle all day yet busily occupied; that matter is no hindrance. Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one is utterly naked.
To look at it requires the expenditure of great effort; to cultivate merit brings only weary toil. When hungry, eat; when tired, sleep. How joyful is such leisure!
*The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huibian Chushi, "The Sun of the Buddha Shining Universally," Volume Seventeen.
